title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午秋山西當大比士
御史馬〔象乾〕奉
上簡命馳至寔監臨之至則前御
史劉〔士忠〕所聘四方文學暨
諸百執事咸會乃以〔允芳〕暨
教諭官〔延澤〕爲考試官教諭
===
李〔起元〕吳〔時泰〕周〔至德〕吳〔守
忠〕劉〔不息〕訓導馬〔希龍〕爲同
考試官使職簾以內左布政
使侯〔丁趙〕右布政使嚴〔大紀〕
提調按察使張〔九一〕副使麻〔永
吉〕監試使職簾以外而御
史躬秉要束譏防劫毖覗昔
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午秋，山西當大比士。御史馬〔象乾〕奉上簡命，馳至，寔監臨之。至則前御史劉〔士忠〕所聘四方文學暨諸百執事咸會，乃以〔允芳〕暨教諭官〔延澤〕爲考試官，教諭李〔起元〕、吳〔時泰〕、周〔至德〕、吳〔守忠〕、劉〔不息〕，訓導馬〔希龍〕爲同考試官，使職簾以內；左布政使侯〔丁趙〕、右布政使嚴〔大紀〕提調，按察使張〔九一〕、副使麻〔永吉〕監試，使職簾以外。而御史躬秉要束，譏防劫毖，覗昔…
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), it was time for Shanxi to hold the triennial examination of scholars. Censor Ma [Xiangqian 馬象乾], having received the Emperor's selective commission, rode swiftly to the province and in fact served as Supervising Official over it. Upon his arrival, the men of letters invited from all quarters by the former Censor Liu [Shizhong 劉士忠], together with the various functionaries of all ranks, had all assembled. Thereupon he appointed me, [Yunfang 允芳], and County Director of Studies Guan [Yanze 官延澤] as Examiners; and County Directors of Studies Li [Qiyuan 李起元], Wu [Shitai 吳時泰], Zhou [Zhide 周至德], Wu [Shouzhong 吳守忠], and Liu [Buxi 劉不息], along with Assistant Instructor Ma [Xilong 馬希龍], as Associate Examiners, charging them with the duties inside the curtain. Left Administration Commissioner Hou [Yu 赵? 侯于趙, transcribed 丁趙] and Right Administration Commissioner Yan [Daji 嚴大紀] served as Proctors, while Surveillance Commissioner Zhang [Jiuyi 張九一] and Vice Commissioner Ma [Yongji 麻永吉] served as Monitors, charged with the duties outside the curtain. Meanwhile, the Censor personally maintained strict regulations, inspecting, guarding, and enforcing vigilance and caution [劫毖, for 戒毖?], which, compared to the past [覗昔, for 視昔?]…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
有加焉于是合巡按宣大御
史徐〔鳴鶴〕暨提學副使陸〔檄〕
所選士二千三百有奇鎖闈
三試之拔其儁六十五人籍
其名氏若文以
獻〔允芳〕竊惟孔子敘書斷自唐
虞以下而司馬遷氏作本紀
===
至西涉崆峒北過涿鹿漸海
浮江以求黄帝堯舜之處而
風教殊焉斷以爲古文近是
夫蒲平陽安邑間爲堯舜禹
所更都遷生其鄉習其風教
甚熟豈必覽觀四方而後知
其徵信于古文正見夫故都
punctuated:
有加焉。于是合巡按宣大御史徐〔鳴鶴〕暨提學副使陸〔檄〕所選士二千三百有奇，鎖闈三試之，拔其儁六十五人，籍其名氏若文以獻。
〔允芳〕竊惟孔子敘《書》，斷自唐虞以下。而司馬遷氏作《本紀》，至西涉崆峒，北過涿鹿，漸海浮江，以求黄帝、堯、舜之處，而風教殊焉，斷以爲古文近是。夫蒲、平陽、安邑間，爲堯、舜、禹所更都。遷生其鄉，習其風教甚熟，豈必覽觀四方，而後知其徵信于古文？正見夫故都
translation_en:
…surpassed the past. Thereupon, bringing together the more than two thousand three hundred scholars selected by the Regional Inspector of Xuanfu and Datong, Investigating Censor Xu Minghe 徐鳴鶴, along with the Education-intendant Vice Commissioner Lu Xi 陸檄, they locked the examination compound and tested them in three sessions. They selected sixty-five outstanding men from among them and registered their names and essays to present to the throne.
I, Yunfang 允芳, humbly reflect that when Confucius arranged the Book of Documents (Shu), he began from the eras of Tang and Yu downward. Yet when Sima Qian 司馬遷 composed the "Basic Annals" (Benji), he went so far as to cross Mount Kongtong in the west, pass through Zhuolu in the north, reach the sea, and float upon the Yangtze and Huai rivers in search of the places of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun; finding that the customs and teachings differed there, he concluded that the ancient texts came closest to the truth. Now the region among Pu, Pingyang, and Anyi was where Yao, Shun, and Yu successively established their capitals. Qian was born in this native land and was thoroughly familiar with its customs and teachings; why would he need to tour and observe the four quarters before knowing how to verify them against the ancient texts? It was precisely to show that the ancient capitals'…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
風教有獨異于四方者在也
〔允〕〔方〕今偎以校士之役憑軾
而入其境遐想夫岳牧元愷
師師濟濟之容思一覩其盛
而無繇則洛洛歎矣然而太
行恒霍如故也洪河汾沁縈
帶而演迤不改其流也
===
主上游神垂衣之烈隆儒術而興
太平而山以西聲教所首被
便章昭明比屋可封之俗非
易民而化也豈以舉士唐虞
之鄉而憂乏材乎顧聞之聖
王在位百里一士猶無有也
累世一聖千里一賢若比肩
punctuated: 風教有獨異于四方者在也。〔允〕〔方〕今偎以校士之役，憑軾而入其境，遐想夫岳、牧、元、愷師師濟濟之容，思一覩其盛而無繇，則洛洛歎矣。然而太行、恒、霍如故也，洪河、汾、沁縈帶而演迤，不改其流也。主上游神垂衣之烈，隆儒術而興太平，而山以西聲教所首被，便章昭明、比屋可封之俗，非易民而化也。豈以舉士唐、虞之鄉而憂乏材乎？顧聞之：聖王在位，百里一士，猶無有也；累世一聖，千里一賢，若比肩
translation_en: …moral customs and teachings are uniquely distinct from those of the four quarters. Now I, 〔Yun〕〔fang〕, having humbly been assigned the duty of examining the scholars, leaned upon the carriage crossbar as I entered its borders. I let my thoughts wander back to the harmonious and dignified bearing of the Four Peaks (Yue), the Twelve Pastors (Mu), the Eight Worthies (Yuan), and the Eight Harmonies (Kai), longing for a glimpse of their flourishing age; yet having no way to do so, I could only sigh in frustration [?洛洛歎]. Nevertheless, Mounts Taihang, Heng, and Huo remain as of old, and the great Yellow River, along with the Fen and Qin rivers, wind like sashes and flow far on without altering their courses. His Majesty fixes his spirit upon the illustrious achievements of ruling with hanging robes, exalting Confucian learning and inaugurating an era of Great Peace. This region west of the mountains is the first to receive his prestige and teachings; its customs—wherein the people are well-ordered and illustrious, and every household is worthy of enfeoffment—were not brought about by replacing the populace in order to transform them. How, then, in selecting scholars in the homeland of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], could one worry about a lack of talent? Yet I have heard it said: when a sage king is on the throne, even if there is one scholar in a hundred li, it is as though there were none; and if a sage appears once in several generations, or a worthy once in a thousand li, it is as though they stood shoulder to shoulder…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
至矣則材大小之辨也
明興二百餘年鉅公碩輔起家幵
冀而顯功名者何可僂數乃
璧宮俎豆右祀聲宗之列或
曠代難其人而河津薛先生
崛起與焉
國家得一薛先生而教化借以
===
大重材誠在傑不在多也予
諸士斌斌登貢籍甚盛第令
續食計偕不辭無能析圭儋
爵不讓無才惟產自唐虞之
鄉繼河津而出則有不難于
盛而難于傑者矣要之學以
立身非以飾名仕以濟時非
punctuated: 至矣，則材大小之辨也。明興二百餘年，鉅公碩輔起家幵、冀而顯功名者，何可僂數？乃璧宮俎豆、右祀聲宗之列，或曠代難其人，而河津薛先生崛起與焉。國家得一薛先生而教化借以大重，材誠在傑不在多也。予諸士斌斌登貢籍，甚盛。第令續食計偕，不辭無能；析圭儋爵，不讓無才。惟產自唐、虞之鄉，繼河津而出，則有不難于盛而難于傑者矣。要之，學以立身，非以飾名；仕以濟時，非
translation_en: … arriving, such is the distinction between great and small talent! In the more than two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, how could one count on one's fingers all the great statesmen and eminent ministers who rose from Qian and Ji [Shanxi] to achieve illustrious merit and fame? Yet when it comes to receiving sacrificial offerings in the Confucian Temple and being enshrined in the honored ranks of the revered masters of moral renown, perhaps for generations it is hard to find such a person—and yet Master Xue [Xue Xuan 薛瑄] of Hejin 河津 rose up suddenly to take his place among them. By gaining this one Master Xue, the dynasty's moral transformation borrowed greatly in weight; talent truly lies in outstanding quality, not in mere numbers. Now you gentlemen, refined and accomplished, have ascended the register of tribute scholars in great abundance. If it is merely a matter of receiving public provisions to travel to the Metropolitan Examination without declining on account of inability, or splitting jade tallies and bearing noble ranks without yielding on account of a lack of talent, that is one thing; but since you are born in the homeland of Yao and Shun [Tang 唐 and Yu 虞] and come forth in succession to Master Xue of Hejin, what is difficult is not flourishing in numbers, but being truly outstanding! In sum, learning is for establishing oneself, not for embellishing one's reputation; serving in office is for aiding the times, not…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
以干祿嘗考薛先生爲學從
政一本諸篤實居平辭受取
予操義甚嚴比當大節至遺
利害死生不顧嘗言讀書窮
理須實見得是然後驗于身
心體而行之斯先生之所以
深于道也爾諸士誠安于里
===
里則已設欲蜚英騰茂歸然
表樹于世而擅不朽之稱緣
見習聞取法不遠舍河津將
安師乎語曰至誠之極金石
可靡其惟以誠心自任學蘄
立身仕蘄濟世毋樹頤頦而
略躬行毋騖虛聲而虧實際
punctuated: 以干祿。嘗考薛先生爲學從政，一本諸篤實。居平辭受取予，操義甚嚴；比當大節，至遺利害、死生不顧。嘗言：「讀書窮理，須實見得是，然後驗于身心，體而行之。」斯先生之所以深于道也。爾諸士誠安于里里則已；設欲蜚英騰茂，歸然表樹于世，而擅不朽之稱，緣見習聞，取法不遠，舍河津將安師乎？語曰：「至誠之極，金石可靡。」其惟以誠心自任：學蘄立身，仕蘄濟世；毋樹頤頦而略躬行，毋騖虛聲而虧實際，
translation_en: … for the purpose of seeking emoluments. I have examined how Master Xue [Xue Xuan 薛瑄] pursued learning and engaged in governance: everything was rooted in earnestness and substance. In ordinary life, whether declining or accepting, taking or giving, he upheld righteousness with the utmost strictness; when confronted with great matters of principle, he went so far as to cast aside personal advantage and harm, disregarding life and death. He once said: "In reading books and fathoming principles, one must truly see what is right, and only then test it in one's own body and mind, embodying it and putting it into practice." This is why the Master was so profound in the Way. If you scholars are truly content with remaining mediocre [reading 卑卑 for 里里?], then so be it; but suppose you wish to let your renown soar and your splendor flourish, to stand toweringly [reading 巋然 for 歸然] as a model established in the world and lay claim to an imperishable reputation—since what you see and hear by familiarity provides a model not far to seek, if you set aside the Master of Hejin [Xue Xuan], whom else will you take as your teacher? The saying goes: "At the utmost height of supreme sincerity, even metal and stone can be worn away." May you take up this charge with a sincere heart alone: in learning, aspire to establish yourselves; in serving in office, aspire to aid the world. Do not merely wag your jaws in talk while neglecting personal practice; do not chase after empty reputation to the detriment of actual substance; …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
母苟寵榮而輕志意毋急功
課而病雅俗毋椎魯少文毋
譸張以譁衆毋介特寡合毋
夸毗以趨時庶幾哉秉道循
理之士無忝堯舜之風教而
于先哲爲有光矣況進此乎
昔趙文子始冠受規于公族
===
以語張老張老曰善矣從欒
伯之言可以滋范叔之教可
以大韓子之戒可以成而欒
伯主務實范叔主戒寵韓子
主始與善此三言者文子終
承之以克光紹成宣之業不
隕其名〔允芳〕不佞無以佐諸
punctuated: 母苟寵榮而輕志意，毋急功課而病雅俗，毋椎魯少文，毋譸張以譁衆，毋介特寡合，毋夸毗以趨時。庶幾哉！秉道循理之士，無忝堯、舜之風教，而于先哲爲有光矣，況進此乎！昔趙文子始冠，受規于公族，以語張老。張老曰：「善矣！從欒伯之言可以滋，范叔之教可以大，韓子之戒可以成。」而欒伯主務實，范叔主戒寵，韓子主始與善。此三言者，文子終承之，以克光紹成、宣之業，不隕其名。〔允芳〕不佞，無以佐諸
translation_en:
…do not casually seek favor and glory while taking your aspirations lightly; do not rush after achievements and quotas to the detriment of both the refined and the common; do not be blunt, rustic, and lacking in refinement; do not engage in wild exaggerations to clamor for the crowd's attention; do not be aloof, isolated, and hard to get along with; and do not be obsequious and fawning just to follow the trends of the times. How close you will then be! As scholars who uphold the Way and follow principle, you will bring no shame to the moral teachings of Yao and Shun, and you will bring glory to the former sages—how much more so if you advance even further than this!

In the past, when Zhao Wenzi 趙文子 first underwent his capping ceremony, he received admonitions from the ducal kinsmen and repeated them to Zhang Lao 張老. Zhang Lao said: "Excellent! Following the words of Luan Bo 欒伯, you can grow; by the teachings of Fan Shu 范叔, you can become great; by the warnings of Hanzi 韓子, you can achieve completion." Now Luan Bo emphasized striving for substance, Fan Shu emphasized guarding against favor, and Hanzi emphasized beginning with goodness. Wenzi ultimately upheld these three counsels, and thereby was able to gloriously continue the enterprises of Zhao Chengzi 趙成子 and Zhao Xuanzi 趙宣子 without letting their reputation fall. Unworthy as I, 〔Yunfang 允芳〕, am, I have nothing with which to assist all you…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
士始進者第中晉人之語勗
之諸士勉乎哉是役也總督
軍務兵部左侍郎兼右僉都
御史鄭〔洛〕巡撫右僉都御史
辛〔應乾〕巡撫大同右副都御
史賈〔應元〕飭武右文乂民與
士巡鹽御史邢〔侗〕肅虔觀風
===
崇雅貞敎閱視兵科給事中
田〔大益〕督糧戶部郎中張〔鼐〕
〔訓〕主事程〔沂〕恤刑刑部郎中
王〔道純〕會逢盛舉嘉樂賓興
左叅政胡〔來貢〕朱〔孟震〕右叅
政杜〔良蘭〕梅〔友松〕左叅議栗
〔在庭〕韓〔應元〕右叅議劉〔忠中〕
punctuated:
士始進者，第中晉人之語勗之，諸士勉乎哉！

是役也，總督軍務、兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史鄭〔洛〕，巡撫、右僉都御史辛〔應乾〕，巡撫大同、右副都御史賈〔應元〕，飭武右文，乂民與士；巡鹽御史邢〔侗〕，肅虔觀風，崇雅貞敎；閱視兵科給事中田〔大益〕，督糧戶部郎中張〔鼐〕〔訓〕、主事程〔沂〕，恤刑刑部郎中王〔道純〕，會逢盛舉，嘉樂賓興；左叅政胡〔來貢〕、朱〔孟震〕，右叅政杜〔良蘭〕、梅〔友松〕，左叅議栗〔在庭〕、韓〔應元〕，右叅議劉〔忠中〕、
translation_en:
… gentlemen who are just entering upon their careers, and so I merely repeat the words of those men of Jin to encourage them. May you gentlemen strive!

In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Left Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Zheng Luo 鄭洛, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Xin Yingqian 辛應乾, and Grand Coordinator of Datong and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Jia Yingyuan 賈應元 have regulated military affairs and esteemed civil culture, governing the common people and encouraging the scholars. Salt-control Censor Xing Tong 邢侗 has observed local customs with solemn reverence, exalting refinement and rectifying instruction. Inspecting Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War Tian Dayi 田大益, Grain-supervising Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Naixun 張鼐訓 [?] and Secretary Cheng Yi 程沂, and Judicial-review Bureau Director of the Ministry of Justice Wang Daochun 王道純 happened to be present for this grand occasion and rejoiced in the ceremonial send-off of the Worthies. Left Administration Vice Commissioners Hu Laigong 胡來貢 and Zhu Mengzhen 朱孟震, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Du Lianglan 杜良蘭 and Mei Yousong 梅友松, Left Assistant Administration Commissioners Li Zaiting 栗在庭 and Han Yingyuan 韓應元, Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Liu Zhongzhong 劉忠中 [?]…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
王〔學書〕副使鄧〔林喬〕錢〔進學〕
僉事張〔惟誠〕劉〔葵〕總兵官王
〔國勳〕參將雷〔以誠〕署都指揮
僉事王〔國翰〕分猷展寀巃外
宣勞在參政嚴〔用和〕副使宋
〔應昌〕前期以入
賀行光祿寺寺丞謝〔杰〕戶科左
===
給事中萬〔象春〕中書舍人劉
〔任〕行人司行人林〔廷陞〕龔〔仲〕
〔慶〕後先以使事至法得備書
云
山東濟南府德州儒學學正
蘇〔允芳〕謹序
punctuated:
、王〔學書〕，副使鄧〔林喬〕、錢〔進學〕，僉事張〔惟誠〕、劉〔葵〕，總兵官王〔國勳〕，參將雷〔以誠〕，署都指揮僉事王〔國翰〕，分猷展寀，巃外宣勞。在參政嚴〔用和〕、副使宋〔應昌〕前期以入賀行，光祿寺寺丞謝〔杰〕，戶科左給事中萬〔象春〕，中書舍人劉〔任〕，行人司行人林〔廷陞〕、龔〔仲〕〔慶〕，後先以使事至，法得備書云。
山東濟南府德州儒學學正蘇〔允芳〕謹序。
translation_en:
…and Wang Xueshu 王學書; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Deng Linqiao 鄧林喬 and Qian Jinxue 錢進學; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhang Weicheng 張惟誠 and Liu Kui 劉葵; Regional Commander Wang Guoxun 王國勳; Assistant Regional Commander Lei Yicheng 雷以誠; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wang Guohan 王國翰—all shared in the planning, carried out their official duties, and exerted themselves outside the examination compound [? 巃外, likely a transcription error for 場外]. As for Administration Vice Commissioner Yan Yonghe 嚴用和 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Song Yingchang 宋應昌, who had departed earlier to present congratulations at court, and Aide in the Court of Imperial Entertainments Xie Jie 謝杰, Left Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue Wan Xiangchun 萬象春, Drafter Liu Ren 劉任, and Messengers in the Messenger Office Lin Tingsheng 林廷陞 and Gong Zhongqing 龔仲慶, who arrived one after another on official missions—by custom, all are duly recorded here in full.

Respectfully prefaced by Su Yunfang 蘇允芳, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Dezhou Department in Jinan Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學道則愛人
子曰天下國家可均也爵祿可辭也白刃
可蹈也中庸不可能也
堯以不得舜爲已憂舜以不得禹皐陶爲
已憂
易
公用亨于天子
===
彖曰大壯大者壯也剛以動故壯大壯利
貞大者正也正大而天地之情可見矣
象曰雷在天上大壯君子以非禮弗履
言行君子之所以動天地也
震一索而得男故謂之長男
書
同寅協恭和衷哉
古有夏先后方懋厥德罔有天災山川鬼
神亦莫不寧暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若
punctuated:
第壹場

四書：
「君子學道則愛人。」
「子曰：『天下國家可均也，爵祿可辭也，白刃可蹈也，中庸不可能也。』」
「堯以不得舜爲已憂，舜以不得禹、皐陶爲已憂。」

易：
「公用亨于天子。」
「彖曰：大壯，大者壯也。剛以動，故壯。大壯利貞，大者正也。正大而天地之情可見矣。象曰：雷在天上，大壯。君子以非禮弗履。」
「言行，君子之所以動天地也。」
「震一索而得男，故謂之長男。」

書：
「同寅協恭，和衷哉！」
「古有夏先后，方懋厥德，罔有天災，山川鬼神，亦莫不寧，暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books (Sishu):
"When the superior man learns the Way, he loves others."
"The Master said, 'The empire, its states, and its families may be perfectly ruled; dignities and emoluments may be declined; naked, sharp weapons may be trampled under foot;—but the course of the Mean cannot be attained to.'"
"Yao 堯 made it his own anxiety that he could not find Shun 舜; Shun made it his own anxiety that he could not find Yu 禹 and Gao Yao 皐陶."

Book of Changes (Yi):
"A prince with this presents his offerings to the Son of Heaven."
"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: 'Da Zhuang (Great Invigoration) denotes that which is great becoming strong. Strength is here combined with movement, and therefore it is strong. "In Da Zhuang it is advantageous to be firm and correct"—that which is great should be correct. Given correctness and greatness, the tendencies of heaven and earth can be seen.' The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Thunder above heaven forms Da Zhuang. The superior man, in accordance with this, does not tread in paths that do not accord with propriety.'"
"Words and actions are the means by which the superior man moves heaven and earth."
"In Zhen, at the first seeking, a male was obtained, and therefore it is called the eldest son."

Book of Documents (Shu):
"Share a reverent harmony and work together in respectful accord—let your hearts be united in harmony!"
"In antiquity, when the former kings of Xia 夏 were earnestly cultivating their virtue, there were no calamities from heaven; the spirits of the hills and rivers likewise were all in tranquility; and the birds and beasts, the fishes and tortoises, all enjoyed their nature."

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
明作有功敦大成裕
出入自爾師虞庶言同則繹
詩
雞既鳴矣朝既盈矣
以我齊明與我犧羊以社以方我田既臧
農夫之慶琴瑟擊鼓以御田祖以祈甘
雨以介我稷黍以穀我士女
干祿百福子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
不競不絿不剛不柔敷政優優百祿是遒
===
春秋
秋八月公及齊侯盟于落姑〔閔公元年〕
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕楚子圍鄭〔宣
公十有二年〕
荊人來聘〔莊公二十有三年〕徐人取舒〔僖
公三年〕公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳
人鄫人于戚〔襄公五年〕冬楚子蔡侯陳
侯許男頓子沈子徐人越人伐吳〔昭公〕
punctuated:
明作有功，敦大成裕。
出入自爾師虞，庶言同則繹。

《詩》
雞既鳴矣，朝既盈矣。
以我齊明，與我犧羊，以社以方。我田既臧，農夫之慶。琴瑟擊鼓，以御田祖，以祈甘雨，以介我稷黍，以穀我士女。
干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
不競不絿，不剛不柔。敷政優優，百祿是遒。

《春秋》
秋八月，公及齊侯盟于落姑。〔閔公元年〕
春，王正月，城楚丘。〔僖公二年〕楚子圍鄭。〔宣公十有二年〕
荊人來聘。〔莊公二十有三年〕徐人取舒。〔僖公三年〕公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。〔襄公五年〕冬，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、沈子、徐人、越人伐吳。〔昭公
translation_en:
“When there is clear-sighted action, there will be achievement; when there is generous largesse, there will be abundance.”
“In measures looking outward or inward, consult with your multitude; when the words of the many agree, then think them through.”

Book of Odes (Shi)
“The cock has already crowed; the court is already full.”
“With our pure millet and our sacrificial sheep, we sacrifice to the altar of the soil and to the four quarters. That our fields are in such good condition is cause for the husbandmen’s rejoicing. With zithers and lutes and beating of drums, we welcome the Father of Husbandry, to pray for sweet rain, to increase our millet and panicled millet, and to nourish our men and women.”
“Seeking emolument and a hundred blessings, his sons and grandsons are a thousand, a hundred million. Reverent and august, fit to be lord, fit to be king.”
“Neither contentious nor急迫 [hasty/urgent], neither hard nor soft, he spreads his governance gently and generously, and a hundred blessings gather to him.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
“In autumn, in the eighth month, the Duke and the Marquis of Qi made a covenant at Luogu.” [1st year of Duke Min]
“In spring, in the king’s first month, Chuqiu was walled.” [2nd year of Duke Xi] “The Viscount of Chu besieged Zheng.” [12th year of Duke Xuan]
“Men of Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiries.” [23rd year of Duke Zhuang] “Men of Xu took Shu.” [3rd year of Duke Xi] “The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, men of Wu, and men of Zeng at Qi.” [5th year of Duke Xiang] “In winter, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Shen, men of Xu, and men of Yue attacked Wu.” [… year of Duke Zhao]…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
五年
冬十有一月庚午蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰
于柏舉〔定公四年〕
禮記
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
故禮也者義之實也協諸義而協則禮雖
先王未之有可以義起也
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮樂者敦和率神而從天禮者
===
別宜居鬼而從地
儒有席上之珍以待聘
第貳場
論
學先義利之辨
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢舉茂材異等詔〔元封五年〕
擬唐以張九齡爲中書令誥〔開元二十二
年〕
punctuated:
五年〕

冬十有一月庚午，蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰于柏舉。〔定公四年〕

《禮記》：

凡爲君使者，已受命，君言不宿於家。

故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。

春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。樂者敦和，率神而從天；禮者別宜，居鬼而從地。

儒有席上之珍以待聘。

第貳場：

論：

學先義利之辨。

詔、誥、表〔内科一道〕：

擬漢舉茂材異等詔。〔元封五年〕

擬唐以張九齡爲中書令誥。〔開元二十二年〕
translation_en:
… fifth year.]

"In winter, in the eleventh month, on the gengwu day, the Marquis of Cai, taking with him the Viscount of Wu, fought with the men of Chu at Boju." [Fourth year of Duke Ding]

Record of Rites (Liji):

"Whenever one is commissioned by the ruler as an envoy, once he has received the charge, the ruler's words do not stay overnight at his home."

"Therefore, ritual is the substance of righteousness. If one harmonizes a matter with righteousness and it accords, then even if it is a ritual that the former kings did not have, it may be originated on the basis of righteousness."

"To initiate in spring and cause to grow in summer is benevolence; to gather in autumn and store in winter is righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music, and righteousness is akin to ritual. Music promotes harmony, following the spirit and conforming to Heaven; ritual distinguishes what is fitting, grounding the earthly soul and conforming to Earth."

"The scholar possesses treasures upon his mat with which to await an invitation to serve."

Second Session

Discourse:

"Learning puts first the distinction between righteousness and profit."

Edict, Mandate, and Memorial [Candidates answer one inside]:

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
擬
駕幸西苑
御無逸殿
命輔臣坐講尚書無逸篇詩豳風七月之章講
畢
賜宴謝表〔嘉靖十年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
功臣田土
===
上書陳言
申報軍務
辯明冤枉
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問制治稽謀莫大乎議堯有衢室之問舜
有總章之訪皆議之謂也我
國家重熙累洽於今二百餘年百度粲然具
舉如議曆元議定郊議張秋決河議撫
punctuated:
擬駕幸西苑，御無逸殿，命輔臣坐講《尚書·無逸篇》、《詩·豳風·七月》之章，講畢賜宴謝表〔嘉靖十年〕。

策〔五道〕：
問：制治稽謀，莫大乎議。堯有衢室之問，舜有總章之訪，皆議之謂也。我國家重熙累洽，於今二百餘年，百度粲然具舉，如議曆元、議定郊、議張秋決河、議撫

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
處其中衆論紛卒統於一我
列聖鴻猷睿斷虎炳可述也乃至議交趾而猶
以昇夷則郡縣之者非與議營制而統
以一勳臣則團營之設非與議貢市而
款塞不絕則拒之者非與抑各有所宜
匪可執方論也夫議一也有當事而議
者有睹事而議者有攬衆議而議者此
三者孰爲難易與抑古人有言君晝之
相守之閫晝之百官守之則持議之權
固有所獨重與我
===
皇上
神聖睿哲自
臨御以來日明習
國家事法度振飭方禺敉寧矣安所事議顧
議論貴省非可盡廢也茲欲采羣議以
裨
國是而賚
宸斷當如何而可願悉意陳之毋顧望不盡也
punctuated: 處，其中衆論紛，卒統於一，我列聖鴻猷睿斷，虎炳可述也。乃至議交趾而猶以昇夷，則郡縣之者非與？議營制而統以一勳臣，則團營之設非與？議貢市而款塞不絕，則拒之者非與？抑各有所宜，匪可執方論也？夫議一也，有當事而議者，有睹事而議者，有攬衆議而議者，此三者孰爲難易與？抑古人有言：「君晝之，相守之；閫晝之，百官守之。」則持議之權，固有所獨重與？我皇上神聖睿哲，自臨御以來，日明習國家事，法度振飭，方禺敉寧矣，安所事議？顧議論貴省，非可盡廢也。茲欲采羣議以裨國是，而賚宸斷，當如何而可？願悉意陳之，毋顧望不盡也。
translation_en: … resettlement; in the midst of these matters, public opinions were profuse, yet ultimately they were unified into one. The grand plans and wise decisions of our successive Sacred Emperors shine brightly like tiger stripes and are worthy of recounting. Yet when it came to deliberating over Jiaozhi (Northern Vietnam) and still handing it over to the barbarians, was it then wrong to have organized it into commanderies and counties? In deliberating over the military camp system and placing it under the unified command of a single merit noble, was the establishment of the Integrated Division Camps (tuanying) then wrong? In deliberating over tribute and border markets, whereby those coming in submission to the frontier never cease, was it then wrong to have rejected them? Or is it that each had its own appropriateness and cannot be judged by clinging to a fixed formula? Now, deliberation is one and the same in name, yet there are those who deliberate while bearing responsibility for the affair, those who deliberate while observing the affair, and those who deliberate by gathering the deliberations of the multitude—among these three, which is easy and which is difficult? Or, as the ancients had a saying: "When the ruler lays down the rule [晝, for 畫], the chief minister abides by it; when the subsequent ruler [閫, for 嗣?] lays down the rule, the百官 (hundred officials) abide by it"—does the authority to guide deliberations indeed have a place where it carries sole weight? Our Emperor, divinely sacred and sagely wise, since ascending the throne has daily grown more clear and practiced in the affairs of the dynasty; laws and institutions are invigorated and ordered, and the four quarters of the realm [方禺, for 方隅] are pacified and tranquil—what need is there to engage in deliberations? Yet while deliberations ought to be kept economical, they cannot be entirely abolished. Now, if we wish to gather the deliberations of the multitude so as to benefit the national policy and assist the imperial decision, how should we proceed so that it will be right? We hope you will set forth your thoughts in full, without hesitating and looking about or leaving anything unsaid.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
問周禮一書經畫大備王制冢宰以三十
年之通制國用曰量入以爲出昔人理
財未有不先定經制之書矣漢事無論
唐元和間其臣撰國計簿上之卽其意
云迨於宋有不進錢穀之數君子以爲
正有輒上會財之書君子以爲佞豈財
用會計不當聞於人主與其後祥符熙
寧皇祐治平元祐皆有會計錄可一一
言之與卽其中又孰爲得與我
===
皇上御極以來脩舉實政主計之臣思所以求
利經制乃爲萬曆會計錄以
上其於積貯大計果有裨與說者謂總括計
錄財用之數歲入大不能當歲出居平
無事且憂不繼設一旦有急何以應之
此又主計者所握籌而思載筆不能盡
者也今天下利源猶有可開其流或有
當塞者藉令授策諸子使佐大司農奚
施而可願熟計焉
punctuated: 問：《周禮》一書，經畫大備；《王制》，冢宰以三十年之通制國用，曰：「量入以爲出。」昔人理財，未有不先定經制之書矣。漢事無論，唐元和間，其臣撰《國計簿》上之，卽其意云。迨於宋，有不進錢穀之數，君子以爲正；有輒上會財之書，君子以爲佞。豈財用會計，不當聞於人主與？其後祥符、熙寧、皇祐、治平、元祐，皆有《會計錄》，可一一言之與？卽其中又孰爲得與？我皇上御極以來，脩舉實政，主計之臣思所以求利經制，乃爲《萬曆會計錄》以上。其於積貯大計，果有裨與？說者謂總括《計錄》財用之數，歲入大不能當歲出，居平無事，且憂不繼，設一旦有急，何以應之？此又主計者所握籌而思，載筆不能盡者也。今天下利源猶有可開，其流或有當塞者，藉令授策諸子，使佐大司農，奚施而可？願熟計焉。
translation_en: Question: The book Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) is comprehensive in its institutional planning; in the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi), the Grand Steward (zhongzai) regulates state expenditures based on the average of thirty years, saying, "Measure revenues in order to determine expenditures." Among the ancients who managed finances, none failed to first establish a book of regular fiscal institutions. Setting aside the affairs of the Han, during the Yuanhe reign of the Tang, a minister compiled the Register of State Finances (Guojibu) and presented it to the throne, which embodied this very principle. Coming down to the Song, there was one who declined to present the figures for money and grain, whom gentlemen regarded as upright; and there was another who readily submitted books of fiscal accounts, whom gentlemen regarded as sycophantic. Could it be that the ruler ought not to be informed of the accounting of wealth and expenditures? Thereafter, in the Xiangfu, Xining, Huangyou, Zhiping, and Yuanyou reigns, there were in each case Records of Fiscal Accounts (Kuaijilu). Can you speak of them one by one? And among them, which succeeded best? Since Our Majesty ascended the throne and revived practical governance, the officials in charge of fiscal administration sought ways to benefit the regular fiscal system, and thus compiled the Wanli Record of Fiscal Accounts (Wanli kuaijilu) and presented it to the throne. Does it truly benefit the grand plan of accumulation and storage? Commentators say that when summing up the figures of wealth and expenditure in the Record of Accounts, annual revenues fall far short of matching annual expenditures. Even in times of peace and quiet there is worry that resources cannot be sustained; suppose an emergency suddenly arises, how is one to respond to it? This, too, is what those in charge of fiscal administration ponder tally in hand, and what cannot be fully exhausted in writing. Today, are there still sources of revenue in the empire that can be opened, or outflows of expenditure that ought to be stemmed? Suppose we were to entrust planning to you gentlemen and have you assist the Minister of Revenue (da sinong)—what measures should be implemented? We wish you to deliberate carefully upon this.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
問帝王馭世之具曰大經大法今學士窮
年佔畢於經勤矣至法律輒委之曰曰
不足道不識二者果若枘鑿不相入與
且禮經於刑法詳哉其言之矣試譚其
槩三典三訊三赦三宥奚由而設三宥奚由
而立均之法而有五禁五戒五聽之殊
均之正法而有八刑八辟八成之異虞
周五刑有無相沿後世六篇九章十二
章以至五百餘條幾千餘條有無可議
===
是皆法之當講者
明興酌古準今裁定律令罔拘拘漢唐故事不
知與虞周之意有同否也我
皇上好生德洽邇遐歲分遣理官出讞疑獄復納
臺臣之議欲令經生兼習法律其說度
可行否夫爨爨六經以吏爲師此秦事
之非者乃宋臣蘇軾又謂不讀律則致
君無術爾多士將何從焉其爲我言之
問
punctuated:
問：帝王馭世之具，曰大經大法。今學士窮年佔畢，於經勤矣；至法律，輒委之曰，曰：「不足道。」不識二者果若枘鑿不相入與？且禮經於刑法，詳哉其言之矣。試譚其槩：三典、三訊、三赦、三宥奚由而設？三宥奚由而立？均之法，而有五禁、五戒、五聽之殊；均之正法，而有八刑、八辟、八成之異。虞、周五刑有無相沿？後世六篇、九章、十二章，以至五百餘條、幾千餘條，有無可議？是皆法之當講者。明興，酌古準今，裁定律令，罔拘拘漢、唐故事，不知與虞、周之意有同否也？我皇上好生德洽邇遐，歲分遣理官出讞疑獄，復納臺臣之議，欲令經生兼習法律，其說度可行否？夫爨爨六經、以吏爲師，此秦事之非者；乃宋臣蘇軾又謂「不讀律則致君無術」。爾多士將何從焉？其爲我言之。

問：
translation_en:
Question: The instruments by which emperors and kings govern the world are called the Great Classics and the Great Laws. Today, scholars spend their entire years poring over texts, diligent indeed in the Classics; yet when it comes to the laws and statutes, they readily dismiss them [?], saying, "They are not worth discussing." I do not know whether the two are truly as incompatible as a square peg and a round hole. Moreover, the Rites Classics (Lijing) speak of penal law in great detail! Let us try to discuss their general outlines: On what basis were the Three Codes (sandian), the Three Interrogations (sanxun), the Three Pardons (sanshe), and the Three Mitigations (sanyou) instituted? And how were the Three Mitigations [?; duplicated phrase in transcription] established? All are alike in being laws, yet there are distinctions among the Five Prohibitions (wujin), the Five Injunctions (wujie), and the Five Modes of Hearing Cases (wuting); all are alike in being corrective laws, yet there are differences among the Eight Punishments (baxing), the Eight Statutory Enactments (bapi), and the Eight Judicial Precedents (bacheng). Did the Five Punishments (wuxing) of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou follow one from the other or not? As for the Six Chapters (Liupian), the Nine Chapters (Jiuzhang), and the Twelve Chapters (Shi'er zhang) of later ages, down to the codes of over five hundred articles or nearly a thousand and more articles—is there room for critical discussion of them or not? All of these are aspects of the law that ought to be examined. When the Ming arose, it weighed antiquity and took the present as its standard in tailoring and fixing the statutes and ordinances, without rigidly clinging to the precedents of the Han and Tang; I wonder whether this accords with the intentions of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou or not? Our Augustus the Emperor, whose virtue of loving life suffuses near and far, periodically dispatches judicial officials to go out and review doubtful criminal cases; and he has further accepted the proposal of Censorate officials, wishing to have students of the Classics concurrently study the laws and statutes. Do you reckon this proposal is feasible or not? Now, burning [?] the Six Classics and taking legal clerks as teachers was the error of Qin affairs; yet the Song official Su Shi 蘇軾 also said, "Without reading the statutes, one has no art with which to serve the ruler." Which course will you gentlemen follow? Pray set it forth for me.

Question: …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
國家財賦歲有額徵今寓內墾田籍於官者
四百六十餘萬耳㪅昔先分九州幅員
未廣迺墾田以九百餘萬計秦漢而下
頃畝不加至宋復浸縮矣我
國家統一輿圖遠邁前代乃墾田之數葷與
宋治平中相埒此其故何也議者謂賦
課縮額貧富不均則遂請度田然是度
田之制豈直自今日始哉蓋其法始於
周而行法之弊則莫如宋姑置勿論已
===
在漢時或詔州郡檢覈墾田或令牧守
區種增耕或以山陽守所立條式班諸
三府其法孰爲得與語有之民可與樂
成難與慮始方始舉事時衆見刺謬叓
間或阻格
詔書令執度明章以次報竣矣然慮始固難圖
終非易即欲熟慮詳畫爲善後計者其
道安在爾諸士生長畎畝習聞之矣幸
縱言之毋徒籠爾胷中事而已
punctuated: 國家財賦，歲有額徵，今寓內墾田籍於官者，四百六十餘萬耳。㪅昔先分九州，幅員未廣，迺墾田以九百餘萬計。秦漢而下，頃畝不加，至宋復浸縮矣。我國家統一輿圖，遠邁前代，乃墾田之數，葷與宋治平中相埒，此其故何也？議者謂賦課縮額，貧富不均，則遂請度田。然是度田之制，豈直自今日始哉？蓋其法始於周，而行法之弊，則莫如宋，姑置勿論已。在漢時，或詔州郡檢覈墾田，或令牧守區種增耕，或以山陽守所立條式班諸三府，其法孰爲得與？語有之：「民可與樂成，難與慮始。」方始舉事時，衆見刺謬，叓間或阻格，詔書令執度明章，以次報竣矣。然慮始固難，圖終非易，即欲熟慮詳畫，爲善後計者，其道安在？爾諸士生長畎畝，習聞之矣，幸縱言之，毋徒籠爾胷中事而已。
translation_en: … The state's fiscal revenues have fixed annual quotas for collection, yet today the cultivated land within the empire registered with the authorities amounts to only some 4.6 million [qing]. Looking back to antiquity when the Nine Provinces were first divided, the territory was not yet vast, yet cultivated land was reckoned at over nine million [qing]. From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, the acreage did not increase, and by the Song dynasty it had gradually shrunk again. Our dynasty has unified a territory that far surpasses former eras, yet the amount of cultivated land is merely [?] on a par with that of the Zhiping reign period (1064–1067) of the Song—what is the reason for this? Those who deliberate on policy say that because tax quotas have shrunk and wealth is unevenly distributed, they have consequently requested a land survey. Yet how could this system of surveying the land have begun only today? Indeed, the method originated in the Zhou, while the abuses in implementing the law were never worse than in the Song—let us set those aside and not discuss them for now. In Han times, at times edicts ordered the regions and commanderies to inspect and verify cultivated land, at times Regional Governors and Grand Administrators were ordered to use pit-planting to increase cultivation, and at times the regulations and formulas established by the Grand Administrator of Shanyang were promulgated to the Three Ducal Offices—which of these methods was the most effective? As the saying goes, "The people can be made to rejoice in the completion of an undertaking, but it is hard to take counsel with them at its beginning." When this undertaking was first launched, popular opinions were perverse and mistaken, and the affair was at times obstructed; now imperial edicts have ordered that the standards be upheld and the rules made clear, so that completion is being reported one after another. Yet while planning at the beginning is certainly difficult, securing the end is not easy either. If one wishes to deliberate maturely and plan in detail to devise measures for long-term maintenance, wherein does the way lie? You gentlemen have grown up among the fields and are familiar with hearing of these matters. Please speak freely of them, and do not merely keep cached within your breasts what you have to say [?].

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
問夷狄爲中國患非一日而中國所以制
馭之亦非一策任德尚矣其次無出戰
守和三者可得聞其槩與有謂縉紳之
儒守和親介胄之士言征伐當時謀國
之臣可考而知也守和親者果皆縉紳
言征伐者果皆介胄與且獨不及守何
與有謂周得中策漢得下策秦無策然
與所謂上策者又安在與
國家自俺酋款塞以來邊鄙不聳可謂至治
===
之世矣然和可恃爲長策與虜近失俺
酋是師旅動靜之首也使虜不渝盟而
常勝在我其道將安出夫徹土戒禦聖
有明訓而雲中上谷爾諸士之鄉也今
且寧爲過計毋寧爲後圖願借箸籌之
毋讓於肉食者
punctuated: 問：夷狄爲中國患非一日，而中國所以制馭之亦非一策。任德尚矣，其次無出戰、守、和三者，可得聞其槩與？有謂「縉紳之儒守和親，介胄之士言征伐」，當時謀國之臣可考而知也。守和親者果皆縉紳，言征伐者果皆介胄與？且獨不及守，何與？有謂「周得中策，漢得下策，秦無策」，然與？所謂上策者，又安在與？國家自俺酋款塞以來，邊鄙不聳，可謂至治之世矣。然和可恃爲長策與？虜近失俺酋，是師旅動靜之首也。使虜不渝盟，而常勝在我，其道將安出？夫「徹土戒禦」，聖有明訓，而雲中、上谷，爾諸士之鄉也。今且寧爲過計，毋寧爲後圖，願借箸籌之，毋讓於肉食者。
translation_en: Question: The Yi and Di peoples have been a scourge upon the Central States for more than a single day, and the measures by which the Central States have controlled and managed them have likewise not been restricted to a single policy. Relying on virtue is the highest course; next to that, nothing goes beyond the three options of war, defense, and peace. May we hear a general outline of these? Someone has said, "Gentry scholars hold fast to harmonious kinship (heqin), while armored warriors speak of punitive expeditions." The ministers who planned for the state in those times can be examined and known. Were those who held fast to harmonious kinship indeed all gentry, and were those who spoke of punitive expeditions indeed all armored warriors? Moreover, why did this statement alone fail to mention defense? Someone has said, "The Zhou attained the middle policy, the Han attained the lower policy, and the Qin had no policy." Is this so? And where, then, does the so-called "upper policy" lie? Since the chieftain Altan Khan (An qiu 俺酋) submitted at the frontier barriers, the borderlands of our State have been free of alarm, which may well be called an era of supreme governance. Yet can peace be relied upon as a permanent policy? Thec northern caitiffs have recently lost the chieftain Altan Khan; this is the critical juncture determining whether armies will mobilize or remain still. If we are to ensure that the caitiffs do not violate their covenant and that constant victory rests with us, from whence shall the way to achieve this proceed? Now, "peeling mulberry root-bark to prepare against contingencies" is a clear precept of the sages, and Yunzhong and Shanggu are the native regions of you gentlemen. At present, we would rather make overly cautious calculations beforehand than belated plans afterward; I wish to borrow your chopsticks to devise a strategy for this, and do not yield this responsibility to the meat-eating officials!

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學道則愛人
白所知
同考試官教諭劉　批〔仁愛原從人心上來是篇根極理要融會意旨傑作也錄之以式〕
考試官教諭官　批〔體格莊重理趣悠揚〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔精到典雅〕
道爲立愛之原學之不可已也夫愛人固君子
===
之心也然必於學道得之道其與政通哉子游
治武城蓋尊其所聞者若曰善言治者以心善
事心者以道偃也聞諸夫子矣蓋上之於民非
徒以其分足以臨之謂其仁能以愛之也仁根
於性雖非緣學而後有愛見乎情實則因道而
後生道有恭儉而莊敬者君子學之以約此心
於中也一中之渾涵愛於是乎立焉道有廣博
而易良者君子學之以導此心於和也太和之
融液愛於是乎流焉心固無外也學以制其私
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

「君子學道則愛人」

白所知
同考試官教諭劉　批〔仁愛原從人心上來，是篇根極理要，融會意旨，傑作也，錄之以式。〕
考試官教諭官　批〔體格莊重，理趣悠揚。〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔精到典雅。〕

道爲立愛之原，學之不可已也。夫愛人，固君子之心也，然必於學道得之。道其與政通哉！子游治武城，蓋尊其所聞者，若曰：善言治者以心，善事心者以道，偃也聞諸夫子矣。蓋上之於民，非徒以其分足以臨之，謂其仁能以愛之也。仁根於性，雖非緣學而後有；愛見乎情，實則因道而後生。道有恭儉而莊敬者，君子學之以約此心於中也，一中之渾涵，愛於是乎立焉。道有廣博而易良者，君子學之以導此心於和也，太和之融液，愛於是乎流焉。心固無外也，學以制其私，
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books

"When the gentleman studies the Way, he loves others." (Analects 17.4)

Bai Suozhi 白所知
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉, comments: [Benevolence and love originally arise from the human mind. This essay probes to the very root of the essential principles and thoroughly integrates the meaning and purport. It is a masterpiece; we record it as a model.]
Examiner, Instructor Guan 官, comments: [Its structure is dignified and grave; its philosophical interest is lingering and resonant.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Su 蘇, comments: [Precise, thorough, and classically elegant.]

The Way is the source for establishing love; learning it cannot be ceased. Now, loving others is assuredly the mind of the gentleman, yet it must be obtained through learning the Way. How the Way communicates with governance! When Ziyou 子游 governed Wucheng 武城, he honored what he had heard, as if to say: "Those who speak well of governance do so by means of the mind, and those who serve the mind well do so by means of the Way. I, Yan 偃, have heard this from the Master: When superiors relate to the common people, it is not merely that their status is sufficient to oversee them; it means that their benevolence is able to love them." Benevolence is rooted in human nature, and although it does not come into existence only because of learning, love is manifested in the feelings, and in fact it is born only on account of the Way. In the Way there is that which is reverent, frugal,莊 dignified, and respectful; the gentleman learns it in order to restrain this mind within equilibrium. In the all-embracing profundity of unitary equilibrium, love is thereby established. In the Way there is that which is broad, extensive, easy, and good; the gentleman learns it in order to guide this mind into harmony. In the pervasive confluence of Supreme Harmony, love thereby flows forth. The mind assuredly has nothing outside itself; when one learns in order to control its selfishness, …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
則廓然者與天地相似乾父坤母之量隨感之
而輒應矣心本無間也學以忘其累則藹然者
與萬物相通民胞物與之懷時措之而皆宜矣
是君子之愛由心而出者也其於道自學而入
者也養之有素則道不窮出之有本故施不匱
武城有爲君子者將責以愛人而不教之以學
道其可哉吁於此見儒者用世之略也吾觀三
代而上政與學出於一禮樂達於天下晩近世
出於二禮樂遂爲虛文無善教斯無善學而民
===
遂不蒙善治蓋自申韓學刑名而慘刻寡恩卒
以禍天下彼而學道詎至是耶世乃謂儒者拘
於道迂而無當非然也
子曰天下國家可均也爵祿可辭也白刃
可蹈也中庸不可能也
張甲傚
同考試官訓導馬　批〔中庸雖能卽在事中見言者率多支離此作體認親切辭意高古必邃於理學者〕
考試官教諭官　批〔見理精明脩辭勁爽〕
punctuated:
則廓然者與天地相似，乾父坤母之量，隨感之而輒應矣。心本無間也，學以忘其累，則藹然者與萬物相通，民胞物與之懷，時措之而皆宜矣。是君子之愛，由心而出者也；其於道，自學而入者也。養之有素，則道不窮；出之有本，故施不匱。武城有爲君子者，將責以愛人，而不教之以學道，其可哉！吁！於此見儒者用世之略也。吾觀三代而上，政與學出於一，禮樂達於天下；晩近世出於二，禮樂遂爲虛文。無善教斯無善學，而民遂不蒙善治。蓋自申、韓學刑名，而慘刻寡恩，卒以禍天下。彼而學道，詎至是耶？世乃謂儒者拘於道，迂而無當，非然也。

子曰：「天下國家可均也，爵祿可辭也，白刃可蹈也，中庸不可能也。」
張甲傚
同考試官訓導馬　批〔中庸雖能卽在事中見，言者率多支離。此作體認親切，辭意高古，必邃於理學者。〕
考試官教諭官　批〔見理精明，脩辭勁爽。〕
translation_en:
… then in its vast openness it resembles Heaven and Earth; with the capacity of regarding Heaven as father and Earth as mother, it immediately responds whenever moved. The mind originally has no barriers; when through learning one forgets its entanglements, then in its gentle harmony it communicates with all things, and the sentiment of regarding the people as one's siblings and all living things as one's companions becomes fitting whenever put into practice. Thus, the love of the gentleman issues forth from the mind, and his attainment of the Way is entered through learning. Because his nourishment of it is habitual, the Way is inexhaustible; because its issuing forth has a root, its bestowal never fails. When there are those in Wucheng who act as gentlemen, if one were to expect them to love the people without teaching them to learn the Way, how could that be acceptable? Ah! In this we see the Confucian's strategy for serving the world. When I observe the Three Dynasties and earlier, governance and learning issued from a single source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm. In more recent ages they have issued from two, and rites and music have consequently become empty formalities. Without good teaching there is no good learning, and the people consequently do not receive the benefit of good governance. Ever since Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非 studied forms and names (xingming), being cruel, harsh, and scant in grace, they ultimately brought disaster upon the realm. Had they learned the Way, how would it have come to this? Yet the world says that Confucians are bound by the Way, pedantic and impractical—this is not so.

The Master said: "The empire, its states, and its families may be peacefully ordered; ranks and emoluments may be declined; naked blades may be trodden upon; but the Mean (Zhongyong) cannot be attained."
[By] Zhang Jiaxiao 張甲傚.
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Ma 馬, comments: 〔Although the ability to practice the Mean is seen right within affairs, those who speak of it are mostly fragmented and disconnected. This composition shows an intimate personal realization, and its diction and meaning are lofty andantique; he must be someone profound in the study of Principle.〕
Examiner, Instructor Guan 官, comments: 〔His grasp of principle is discerning and clear; his rhetoric is vigorous and brisk.〕

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正蘇　批〔沖融警㥦〕
天下無難為之事而難於中焉夫中固非絶德
也而人之所能者獨中爲不易焉顧可忽之也
哉中庸曰天下之道中焉止矣人皆有之宜人
皆能之而民固鮮能者以其易而難耳何者今
夫天下國家之均也爵祿之辭也白刃之蹈也
據其事勢所在孰不視之以爲難然任智者能
均之苦節者能辭之輕生者能蹈之隨其資力
所近則皆勉之而可至三者而果難也進無能
===
之者人苟能之君子以爲易矣惟就其可能之
中求其所不可者其中庸乎中也者以之當治
平之任則弛張闔闢有權存焉以之臨利害之
間則辭受死生有義存焉智能可以自運而材
質所賦或得其一偏則寬焉而慢猛焉而殘者
有之矣名節能以自許而意氣所激或出於一
時則辭而傷廉蹈而傷勇者有之矣蓋折義之
不精斯見易惑非天資可以偶合也爲仁之不
熟斯守易搖非人力可以襲取也故曰中庸不

考試官學正蘇　批〔沖融警㥦〕

天下無難為之事，而難於中焉。夫中固非絶德也，而人之所能者，獨中爲不易焉，顧可忽之也哉？《中庸》曰：天下之道，中焉止矣。人皆有之，宜人皆能之，而民固鮮能者，以其易而難耳。何者？今夫天下國家之均也，爵祿之辭也，白刃之蹈也，據其事勢所在，孰不視之以爲難？然任智者能均之，苦節者能辭之，輕生者能蹈之。隨其資力所近，則皆勉之而可至。三者而果難也，進無能之者；人苟能之，君子以爲易矣。惟就其可能之中，求其所不可者，其中庸乎！中也者，以之當治平之任，則弛張闔闢有權存焉；以之臨利害之間，則辭受死生有義存焉。智能可以自運，而材質所賦，或得其一偏，則寬焉而慢、猛焉而殘者有之矣。名節能以自許，而意氣所激，或出於一時，則辭而傷廉、蹈而傷勇者有之矣。蓋折義之不精，斯見易惑，非天資可以偶合也；爲仁之不熟，斯守易搖，非人力可以襲取也。故曰「中庸不

Examiner Su, Subprefectural Director of Studies, comments: Harmonious and incisive.

There is no affair in the world that is difficult to accomplish, yet the difficulty lies in attaining the Mean. Now, the Mean is certainly not an unattainable virtue, yet among the things that people are capable of doing, attaining the Mean alone is not easy—how then could one treat it lightly? In the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), it is said: The Way of the world stops at the Mean. Everyone possesses it, so everyone ought to be capable of it; that the people are in fact rarely capable of it is simply because in its very easiness lies its difficulty. Why is this? Consider bringing order and balance to the empire, the state, and the family; declining ranks and emoluments; and treading upon naked blades. Judging by the circumstances involved, who would not regard these as difficult? Yet those who rely on intelligence are able to bring such order; those who practice bitter austerity are able to decline such rewards; and those who hold life lightly are able to tread upon blades. Following what is close to their natural endowments and strength, they can all reach these goals through exertion. If these three things were truly difficult, then moving forward no one would be capable of them; since people can indeed do them, the gentleman regards them as easy. Only when we seek what is impossible within what is possible—is that not the Mean in common action (zhongyong)? As for the Mean: when one applies it to bear the responsibility of governing and bringing peace, there is a standard of weighing (quan) in relaxing and tightening, closing and opening; when one applies it in facing advantage and harm, there is righteousness (yi) in declining and accepting, living and dying. Intelligence and ability can be exercised on one's own, yet the natural qualities with which one is endowed may incline toward a single side; thus there are cases where leniency turns into negligence and severity turns into cruelty. One may pride oneself on reputation and integrity, yet when stirred by temperament and impulse on the spur of the moment, there are cases where declining rewards injures true integrity and treading on blades injures true courage. For when the analysis of righteousness is not precise, one's judgment is easily confused—it is not something that natural endowment can hit upon by chance; and when the practice of benevolence is not mature, one's resolve is easily shaken—it is not something that human effort can seize by surprise. title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
可能也嗟夫中以庸名理固易簡耳惟中故難
必庸而後可中彼稱賢知者乃厭其卑近而高
遠是馳夫既不安於庸又安所得中耶藝如求
猾如憲勇如仲由夫非一時之選與律之以中
皆有間焉信乎中道之難能而賢智之易過也
堯以不得舜為巳憂舜以不得禹臯陶為
巳憂
同考試官教諭吳　批〔說透堯舜求賢圖治所以爲君〕
陳　熇
===
考試官教諭官　批〔道相業之大而理以周密體裁閑雅文之上乘也取之〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔温潤典雅當是作手〕
精確不凡
二聖之所急者惟爲天下得人而已蓋天下之
治天下之人成之也堯舜任人以治其斯爲憂
之大乎孟子所以言必稱之也蓋曰聖王治天
下豈必如許子而後治哉勞於求賢逸於圖治
如是而已矣吾觀陶唐之世以君有堯以相有
舜焉夫堯既爲君凡代天以憂者皆君之事也
punctuated:
可能也。嗟夫！中以庸名，理固易簡耳。惟中故難，必庸而後可中。彼稱賢知者，乃厭其卑近而高遠是馳。夫既不安於庸，又安所得中耶？藝如求，狷如憲，勇如仲由，夫非一時之選與？律之以中，皆有間焉。信乎中道之難能，而賢智之易過也。

堯以不得舜為巳憂，舜以不得禹、臯陶為巳憂。
陳熇

二聖之所急者，惟爲天下得人而已。蓋天下之治，天下之人成之也。堯、舜任人以治，其斯爲憂之大乎！孟子所以言必稱之也。蓋曰：聖王治天下，豈必如許子而後治哉？勞於求賢，逸於圖治，如是而已矣。吾觀陶唐之世，以君有堯，以相有舜焉。夫堯既爲君，凡代天以憂者，皆君之事也。
translation_en:
… cannot be achieved. Alas! Equilibrium is named together with the ordinary, for its principle is inherently easy and simple. Yet precisely because it is equilibrium, it is difficult; only by abiding in the ordinary can one attain equilibrium. Those who are called worthy and wise disdain what is humble and near at hand, and instead chase after what is lofty and distant. Since they are not content with the ordinary, how then can they attain equilibrium? Someone as accomplished in the arts as Ran Qiu (求), as fastidiously upright as Yuan Xian (憲) [transcribed as 猾], or as courageous as Zhong You (仲由)—were they not the finest choices of their age? Yet when measured against the standard of equilibrium, all of them fell somewhat short. Truly, the Way of the Mean is difficult to achieve, and the worthy and wise easily go beyond it!

"Yao made it his own anxiety not to find Shun; Shun made it his own anxiety not to find Yu and Gao Yao."
By Chen Hao (陳熇).
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wu (吳), comments: [He thoroughly explains how Yao and Shun sought worthies to bring about good governance, and why this constituted the anxiety of sovereign and chief minister [?]; precise and extraordinary.]
Examiner, Instructor Guan (官), comments: [It speaks of the greatness of the work of governance and administration with comprehensive and meticulous reasoning, and a composed, elegant style. It is a piece of the highest grade. Selected.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Su (蘇), comments: [Warm, lustrous, and classically elegant; this must be the work of a skilled master.]

What the two sages treated as most urgent was simply to find the right men for the empire. For the governance of the empire is brought to completion by the men of the empire. Yao and Shun entrusted men with the task of governing—was this not the greatest of their anxieties! That is why Mencius unfailingly cited them whenever he spoke. He meant to say: When a sage-king governs the empire, why must he act like Master Xu (許子) before it can be governed? To toil in seeking out the worthy and be at ease in accomplishing governance—it is simply like this and nothing more. When I observe the age of Taotang (陶唐), as sovereign there was Yao, and as chief minister there was Shun. Now, since Yao was the sovereign, everything involved in worrying on behalf of Heaven was the sovereign's affair. …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
乃堯曰天下可以一人君之何可一人理之側
陋未揚登庸未舉則吾之相位尚虛天工其誰
與亮是則可憂也夫是以皇皇焉爲四岳之詢
也迨夫得舜以諸難付之堯於是垂裳而理矣
至於舜既時敘天下頌如天者不曰舜而曰堯
之仁堯固善用其憂耶舜既爲相凡代堯以憂
者皆相之責也乃舜曰天下可以一人相之何
可一人成之司空不能其官士師不得其理則
君之庶官尚曠帝載其誰與熙是則可憂也夫
===
是以急急焉爲四門之闢也迨夫得禹皐陶以
庶績分之舜於是協帝而治矣至於禹皐陶奏
功天下言好生者不曰禹皐陶而曰舜之德舜
固善用其憂耶是則人君以論相爲職宰相以
得士爲功賢者之治如此並耕何事哉雖然任
人圖治自昔諱之然在唐虞以之基治後世或
不免階亂焉顧所任者何如耳藉令堯舜權度
不精使象恭庸違之夫與舜禹諧臣並列何以
稱唐虞皐陶陳謨曰在知人有味乎言之也
punctuated: 乃堯曰：「天下可以一人君之，何可一人理之？側陋未揚，登庸未舉，則吾之相位尚虛，天工其誰與亮？是則可憂也夫！」是以皇皇焉爲四岳之詢也。迨夫得舜，以諸難付之，堯於是垂裳而理矣。至於舜既時敘，天下頌如天者，不曰舜而曰堯之仁，堯固善用其憂耶！舜既爲相，凡代堯以憂者，皆相之責也。乃舜曰：「天下可以一人相之，何可一人成之？司空不能其官，士師不得其理，則君之庶官尚曠，帝載其誰與熙？是則可憂也夫！」是以急急焉爲四門之闢也。迨夫得禹、皐陶，以庶績分之，舜於是協帝而治矣。至於禹、皐陶奏功，天下言好生者，不曰禹、皐陶而曰舜之德，舜固善用其憂耶！是則人君以論相爲職，宰相以得士爲功，賢者之治如此，並耕何事哉！雖然，任人圖治，自昔諱之，然在唐虞以之基治，後世或不免階亂焉，顧所任者何如耳。藉令堯、舜權度不精，使象恭庸違之夫，與舜、禹諧臣並列，何以稱唐虞？皐陶陳謨曰：「在知人。」有味乎言之也！
translation_en:
Yet Yao said: "The realm may have one man rule over it as sovereign, how could one man put it in order alone? While the lowly and obscure have not yet been raised up, and those to be elevated and employed have not yet been promoted, my office of chief minister remains vacant—with whom, then, shall Heaven's work be assisted? This indeed is worthy of anxiety!" Therefore, he anxiously consulted the Four Peaks. Once he had found Shun and entrusted all difficulties to him, Yao thereupon let his robes hang down and governed in ease. And when Shun had brought everything into timely order, those throughout the realm who praised benevolence like unto Heaven's attributed it not to Shun, but to the benevolence of Yao—did not Yao indeed make good use of his anxiety?

Once Shun became chief minister, whatever involved bearing anxiety on Yao's behalf was entirely the responsibility of the chief minister. Yet Shun said: "The realm may have one man serve as its chief minister, how could one man bring it to completion alone? If the Minister of Works is unequal to his office and the Chief Justice fails to achieve proper order, then the sovereign's many offices remain neglected—with whom, then, shall the sovereign's undertakings be made to flourish? This indeed is worthy of anxiety!" Therefore, he urgently threw open the gates in all four directions. Once he had found Yu and Gao Yao and divided the manifold tasks between them, Shun thereupon harmonized with the sovereign and governed. And when Yu and Gao Yao achieved their successes, those throughout the realm who spoke of the love of life attributed it not to Yu and Gao Yao, but to the virtue of Shun—did not Shun indeed make good use of his anxiety?

Thus, the ruler takes selecting a chief minister as his duty, and the chief minister takes obtaining worthy men as his merit. Such is the governance of worthy rulers—what business have they with plowing side by side with the people! Even so, delegating to others in order to achieve good rule has been viewed with caution since antiquity; yet while in the eras of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] it laid the foundation of order, in later ages it sometimes could not avoid becoming a stepping-stone to disorder. It all depends on what sort of men are entrusted with office. Suppose Yao and Shun had not been precise in their weighing and measuring, allowing fellows who appeared respectful on the surface while acting perversely in practice to stand alongside harmonious ministers like Shun and Yu—how then could their eras have been praised as Tang and Yu? When Gao Yao set forth his counsels, he said: "It lies in knowing men." How deeply meaningful are those words!

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
易
彖曰大壯大者壯也剛以動故壯大壯利
貞大者正也正大而天地之情可見矣
象曰雷在天上大壯君子以非禮弗履
白所知

===
觀大壯之彖象而知君子之以理勝也夫君子
所恃者理也以理勝人亦以理自勝斯其善處
壯矣乎且天下惟禮爲至正亦惟正爲至大此
造化人事之所以爲壯也吾嘗即大壯之名詞
而觀之四陽盛長豪傑之會以開其時可以爲
矣乾剛震動明作之功以建其才可以爲矣然
時不可恃才不可逞由是有取於利貞焉良以
大而必正固君子之道所以異乎小人正以成
大亦君子之情所以通乎天地若是乎貞之不
punctuated:
《易》
「《彖》曰：大壯，大者壯也。剛以動，故壯。大壯利貞，大者正也。正大而天地之情可見矣。《象》曰：雷在天上，大壯。君子以非禮弗履。」

觀《大壯》之《彖》《象》，而知君子之以理勝也。夫君子所恃者，理也。以理勝人，亦以理自勝，斯其善處壯矣乎！且天下惟禮爲至正，亦惟正爲至大，此造化人事之所以爲壯也。吾嘗即《大壯》之名詞而觀之：四陽盛長，豪傑之會以開，其時可以爲矣；乾剛震動，明作之功以建，其才可以爲矣。然時不可恃，才不可逞，由是有取於「利貞」焉。良以大而必正，固君子之道所以異乎小人；正以成大，亦君子之情所以通乎天地。若是乎貞之不

"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: 'Great Strength (Dazhuang) means that what is great is strong. It is firm and moves, and therefore it is strong. Great Strength is advantageous in correctness (zhen), which means that what is great is upright. Through uprightness and greatness, the disposition of Heaven and Earth can be seen.' The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Thunder is above Heaven: Great Strength. The superior man, in accordance with this, does not tread where it is contrary to ritual propriety (li).'"

Bai Suozhi 白所知
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu comments: [Prevailing over others and prevailing over oneself both derive from a single principle; this ably elucidates Great Strength.]
Examiner, Instructor Guan comments: [Without indulging in ornate rhetoric, he uniquely blends the profundities of true meaning, while the formal structure is concise and the thread of thought is well connected—an excellent exposition of the meaning of the Changes.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Su comments: [The wording is concise and the meaning is fully expressed.]

Contemplating the Commentary on the Decision and the Commentary on the Images for the hexagram Great Strength, one knows that the superior man prevails through principle (li). What the superior man relies upon is principle. Prevailing over others through principle, and also prevailing over oneself through principle—is this not how he skillfully handles strength! Moreover, in all under Heaven, only ritual propriety is supremely upright, and only uprightness is supremely great; this is whereby both the creative transformations of nature and human affairs attain strength.

I have examined the name and the explanatory words of Great Strength: with four yang lines flourishing and advancing, the opportune gathering for heroic men is opened, so the time is such that one can act; with the firmness of the Qian trigram and the movement of the Zhen trigram, the achievements of enlightened action are established, so the talent is such that one can act. Yet the time cannot be presumed upon, and talent cannot be indulged; for this reason it takes its meaning from "advantageous in correctness." Truly, because what is great must be upright, this is fundamentally how the Way of the superior man differs from that of the petty man; and because uprightness brings about greatness, this is also how the disposition of the superior man communicates with Heaven and Earth. title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
可已也然天下之難勝者小人之私也其尤難
勝者一已之私也君子觀雷在天上之象有自
勝之道焉一念非禮以爲非正大之體也而克
之於幾微不使人得以勝乎天一息非禮以爲
非天地之情也而防之於念慮不使欲得以勝
乎理蓋如是而吾心之壯浩然其常伸世道之
壯亦賴之以維持矣乎噫欲勝人者當知所以
自勝矣大抵克已之道不可以有所待故貴於
剛去小人之道不可使之無所容故不可一於
===
剛以壯趾之戒施之於勝私則息矣以雷厲之
強施之於小人則激矣故曰告自邑又曰不利
即戎噫聖人之慮深夫
震一索而得男故謂之長男
余應泰
同考試官教諭劉　批〔題本枯淡而發揮詳盡趣味悠長結意歸重元子尤爲卓識〕
考試官教諭官　批〔構思精密措辭純雅〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔融暢可嘉〕
punctuated:
可已也。然天下之難勝者，小人之私也；其尤難勝者，一已之私也。君子觀雷在天上之象，有自勝之道焉。一念非禮，以爲非正大之體也，而克之於幾微，不使人得以勝乎天；一息非禮，以爲非天地之情也，而防之於念慮，不使欲得以勝乎理。蓋如是而吾心之壯，浩然其常伸，世道之壯，亦賴之以維持矣乎！噫！欲勝人者，當知所以自勝矣。大抵克已之道，不可以有所待，故貴於剛；去小人之道，不可使之無所容，故不可一於剛。以壯趾之戒施之於勝私則息矣，以雷厲之強施之於小人則激矣。故曰「告自邑」，又曰「不利即戎」，噫！聖人之慮深夫！

震一索而得男，故謂之長男。
余應泰

translation_en:
… cannot be dispensed with. Yet what is difficult to overcome in the world is the selfishness of petty men; what is even more difficult to overcome is the selfishness within oneself. The gentleman, observing the image of thunder above heaven, finds therein the way to overcome himself. If a single thought is contrary to ritual propriety, he regards it as not conforming to the substance of uprightness and greatness, and subdues it at its subtlest inception, not allowing the human to prevail over the Heavenly. If a single breath is contrary to ritual propriety, he regards it as not conforming to the disposition of heaven and earth, and guards against it in his thoughts and deliberations, not allowing selfish desires to prevail over principle. When it is thus, the vigor of one's own mind expands vastly and remains ever unyielding, and the vigor of the world's moral order likewise relies upon this to be sustained! Alas, one who wishes to overcome others must first know how to overcome himself. Generally speaking, the way of subduing oneself admits of no delay, and therefore prizes firmness; the way of removing petty men must not leave them with nowhere to be accommodated, and therefore must not rely solely on firmness. If the warning of "vigor in the toes" is applied to overcoming selfishness, one will grow lax; if the fierceness of thunderous might is applied to petty men, it will provoke them to extremes. Thus it is said, "Announce it from one's own town," and again, "It is not advantageous to take up arms." Alas, how deep were the concerns of the sage!

"Zhen, at the first seeking, obtains a male, and therefore is called the eldest son."
Yu Yingtai 余應泰
