Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Guan, comments: [The conception is precise and tight, the phrasing pure and elegant.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Su, comments: [Harmonious, fluent, and praiseworthy.]

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
知長男之所由名而易之分昭矣蓋乾道成男
也震得之於一索謂之長男也固宜且夫長長
之義尚矣家則重乎長子國則重乎長君達之
天下者也吾得文王命震之義矣彼乾稱父坤
稱母震謂之男固也而謂之長男曷故哉蓋震
之爲卦生於乾之初爻而乾之生震本於坤之
一索索之於乾而得之於乾則從其陽之質也
不得不謂之男索之於一而得之於一則從其
陽之序也不得不謂之長乾坤之氣均賦以成
===
形而震之得氣貧始焉始乎諸卦自長乎諸卦
而名之命也昭然其不可踰矣乾坤之理均受
以成性而震之得理最先焉先乎六子自長乎
六子而命之名也秩然其不可紊矣由是承祧
於宗廟可以奉神靈之統也繼體於朝廷可以
爲社稷之主也外此而坎之再索特中耳艮之
三索特少耳安可與長男竝哉吁震一出而乾
坤可謂有子矣文王其察於人倫者乎抑此爲
天王之元子發也蓋其生也謂之出震其出也
punctuated: 知長男之所由名，而《易》之分昭矣。蓋乾道成男也，震得之於一索，謂之長男也固宜。且夫長長之義尚矣。家則重乎長子，國則重乎長君，達之天下者也，吾得文王命震之義矣。彼乾稱父，坤稱母，震謂之男固也，而謂之長男曷故哉？蓋震之爲卦，生於乾之初爻，而乾之生震，本於坤之一索。索之於乾而得之於乾，則從其陽之質也，不得不謂之男；索之於一而得之於一，則從其陽之序也，不得不謂之長。乾坤之氣均賦以成形，而震之得氣貧始焉。始乎諸卦，自長乎諸卦，而名之命也，昭然其不可踰矣。乾坤之理均受以成性，而震之得理最先焉。先乎六子，自長乎六子，而命之名也，秩然其不可紊矣。由是承祧於宗廟，可以奉神靈之統也；繼體於朝廷，可以爲社稷之主也。外此，而坎之再索特中耳，艮之三索特少耳，安可與長男竝哉！吁！震一出而乾坤可謂有子矣，文王其察於人倫者乎！抑此爲天王之元子發也。蓋其生也謂之出震，其出也…
translation_en:
When one understands why the Eldest Son (zhangnan) is so named, the distinctions of rank in the Book of Changes (Yi) become clear. For the Way of Qian brings about the male; Zhen obtains this from the first seeking, so it is certainly fitting that he be called the Eldest Son.

Moreover, the principle of honoring the eldest is of great antiquity. A family attaches prime importance to the eldest son, and a state attaches prime importance to the eldest ruler; this is something that extends throughout the realm, and from it I grasp the meaning behind King Wen's naming of Zhen. Now, Qian is called the father and Kun is called the mother; that Zhen is called a son is natural enough, yet why is he called the Eldest Son? It is because the trigram Zhen is generated from the first line of Qian, and Qian's generation of Zhen is rooted in Kun's first seeking. Since it is sought from Qian and obtained from Qian, it follows the substance of its yang nature, and so he cannot but be called a son; since it is sought at the first and obtained at the first, it follows the sequence of its yang lines, and so he cannot but be called the eldest.

The vital force (qi) of Qian and Kun is equally endowed to form physical shapes, yet Zhen is the very first [貧始, ? probably a misprint for 實始 or 最始] to obtain that vital force. Being the beginning among the trigrams, he is naturally the eldest among the trigrams, and the bestowal of his name is so clear that it cannot be transgressed. The principle (li) of Qian and Kun is equally received to form the inner nature, yet Zhen is the earliest to obtain that principle. Preceding the six children-trigrams, he is naturally the eldest among the six children-trigrams, and the naming of his title is so orderly that it cannot be thrown into confusion.

From this, in succeeding to the ancestral line in the ancestral temple, he can uphold the lineage of the sacred spirits; in continuing the sovereign's body at court, he can serve as the lord of the altars of soil and grain. Beyond this, Kan, from the second seeking, is merely the middle son, and Gen, from the third seeking, is merely the youngest son—how could they be placed on a par with the Eldest Son! Ah! Once Zhen emerges, Qian and Kun may truly be said to have a son; how deeply did King Wen discern human relationships! Or perhaps this was expressed with reference to the Eldest Son (yuanzi) of the Heavenly King. For at his birth he is said to emerge in Zhen; in his emergence…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
謂之復乾而其壁也謂之元后然他日之元后
即今日之長子故曰主器者莫若長子然則爲
長子者當知忠震體元之義
書
古有夏先后方懋厥德罔有天災山川鬼
神亦莫不寧暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若
張甲徵
同考試官訓導馬　批〔夏后懋德格天是伊尹懇切訓王處此篇命意周悉措辭醇雅可誦〕
===
考試官教諭官　批〔不費詞說文理粲然〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔語意精到〕
夏王有聖德而休徵應焉蓋休徵之應天眷也
夏王以懋德得之豈偶然哉伊尹訓嗣王進意
謂天命不常惟德是輔殷鑒不遠在彼夏王吾
王亦知夏之所以興隆哉古有夏先后方其懋
德之時也惟精惟一上接執中之統克勤克儉
下開祗德之傳夫非有期於天之我眷也乃其
德格于皇天則罔有災焉以象懸者薦參循軌
punctuated:
謂之復乾，而其壁也謂之元后。然他日之元后，即今日之長子，故曰「主器者莫若長子」。然則爲長子者，當知忠震體元之義。
書
古有夏先后，方懋厥德，罔有天災，山川鬼神，亦莫不寧，暨鳥獸魚鼈咸若。
張甲徵
同考試官訓導馬　批〔夏后懋德格天，是伊尹懇切訓王處。此篇命意周悉，措辭醇雅，可誦。〕
考試官教諭官　批〔不費詞說，文理粲然。〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔語意精到。〕
夏王有聖德而休徵應焉。蓋休徵之應，天眷也；夏王以懋德得之，豈偶然哉？伊尹訓嗣王進意，謂天命不常，惟德是輔，殷鑒不遠，在彼夏王。吾王亦知夏之所以興隆哉？古有夏先后，方其懋德之時也，惟精惟一，上接執中之統；克勤克儉，下開祗德之傳。夫非有期於天之我眷也，乃其德格于皇天，則罔有災焉。以象懸者，薦參循軌，
translation_en:
…is called returning to Qian (the Creative), and when he ascends the throne [? 壁, likely for 辟, sovereign], he is called the Great Sovereign. Yet the Great Sovereign of a future day is none other than the eldest son of today; hence it is said, "For presiding over the sacrificial vessels, none is equal to the eldest son." If so, then he who is the eldest son ought to understand the meaning of reverently fearing [? 忠, likely for 恐, fearing] Zhen (the Arousing) and embodying the primal origin.

Book of Documents (Shu)

"In antiquity the former sovereign of Xia, at the time when he was earnestly cultivating his virtue, had no calamities from Heaven; the spirits of the hills and rivers likewise were none of them not tranquil; and the birds and beasts, the fishes and tortoises, all enjoyed their nature."

By Zhang Jiazheng.

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Ma comments: [That the sovereign of Xia earnestly cultivated his virtue and moved Heaven is the point where Yi Yin most earnestly admonished the king. This essay is comprehensive in its conception and pure and elegant in its phrasing; it is well worth reciting.]

Examiner and Instructor Guan comments: [Without wasting words or explanations, its literary structure and reasoning are brilliantly clear.]

Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Su comments: [The language and meaning are precise and penetrating.]

The King of Xia possessed sage virtue, and auspicious signs responded to him. Indeed, the response of auspicious signs is the favor of Heaven; the King of Xia obtained it through earnestly cultivating his virtue—how could that have been by chance? In admonishing the successor king, Yi Yin advanced this thought, saying in effect that the Mandate of Heaven is not constant and aids only virtue, and that the mirror for Yin is not far off, being found in that King of Xia. Does my King also know whereby Xia rose and flourished? In antiquity, the former sovereign of Xia, at the time when he was earnestly cultivating his virtue, was refined and single-minded, above continuing the tradition of holding fast the Mean; he was diligent and frugal, below opening the transmission of reverent virtue. Now, it was not that he had any expectation of Heaven's favoring him! Yet when his virtue reached August Heaven, there were no calamities. Among the phenomena suspended on high, the sun and moon [? 薦參, likely garbled for 躔度 or 日月] followed their orbits…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
無過忒也以氣行者四氣燮和無愆伏也而豈
惟是哉大而山川鬼神皆受職於天者也於是
不童而不涸焉來格而來享焉蓋天將奠其與
圖保其宗廟畀之以神靈之統故亦莫不寧如
此也山川鬼神何心耶微而鳥獸魚鼈皆受氣
於天者也於是飛走各適其性焉潛躍各順其
天焉蓋天將徵其太和昰其瑞應命之爲民物
之宗故爲之咸若如此也鳥獸魚鼈何心耶夫
天之眷夏后者如此皆懋德所致也使子孫能
===
世其德雖至今存可矣吾王其鑒之哉譬然和
氣致祥乖氣召戾自古記之若堯之水湯之旱
則何以故也蓋天人之際微矣顧君德何如耳
君而德則爲堯爲湯君而不德則敗亡之徵豈
必天災也哉故人君惟其可必者而聽其不可
必者不然見祥而喜其不化而爲災者幾希
明作有功敦大成裕
同考試官訓導馮　批
樊　鎔
明作敦大總爲治體作者泥於
punctuated:
無過忒也；以氣行者，四氣燮和，無愆伏也。而豈惟是哉？大而山川鬼神，皆受職於天者也，於是不童而不涸焉，來格而來享焉。蓋天將奠其與圖，保其宗廟，畀之以神靈之統，故亦莫不寧如此也。山川鬼神何心耶？微而鳥獸魚鼈，皆受氣於天者也，於是飛走各適其性焉，潛躍各順其天焉。蓋天將徵其太和，昰其瑞應，命之爲民物之宗，故爲之咸若如此也。鳥獸魚鼈何心耶？夫天之眷夏后者如此，皆懋德所致也。使子孫能世其德，雖至今存可矣。吾王其鑒之哉！譬然和氣致祥，乖氣召戾，自古記之。若堯之水、湯之旱，則何以故也？蓋天人之際微矣，顧君德何如耳。君而德，則爲堯、爲湯；君而不德，則敗亡之徵，豈必天災也哉？故人君惟其可必者，而聽其不可必者。不然，見祥而喜，其不化而爲災者幾希。

「明作有功，敦大成裕。」
同考試官訓導馮　批：
樊鎔
〔明作、敦大，總爲治體，作者泥於〕
translation_en:
…without error or deviation; as for that which operates through vital energy, the four seasonal breaths blend in harmony without excess or deficiency. And is it only this? Among great things, mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits all receive their charges from Heaven; thus the mountains do not go bare and the rivers do not run dry, and the spirits come to be present and accept offerings. Indeed, Heaven is about to stabilize his territory [?], preserve his ancestral temple, and endow him with dominion over the numinous spirits; therefore none fail to be tranquil like this. What intention of their own do mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits have? Among small things, birds, beasts, fishes, and turtles all receive their vital breath from Heaven; thus those that fly and run each find satisfaction in their nature, and those that dive and leap each follow their natural endowment. Indeed, Heaven is about to manifest his supreme harmony, display [?] his auspicious responses, and appoint him as the master of the people and all things; therefore they all conform like this for him. What intention of their own do birds, beasts, fishes, and turtles have? Now, that Heaven favored the Xia sovereigns in such a manner was entirely brought about by their diligent cultivation of virtue. Had their descendants been able to perpetuate their virtue from generation to generation, they could have survived even to this day. May our King take this as a mirror! Even so [?], that harmonious vital breath brings auspiciousness and perverse vital breath summons calamity has been recorded since antiquity. Yet as for the floods of Yao and the droughts of Tang, what was the reason for them? Indeed, the interaction between Heaven and man is subtle; it simply depends on what the ruler's virtue is like. If a ruler is virtuous, he becomes a Yao or a Tang; if a ruler lacks virtue, why must the signs of ruin and destruction be natural disasters? Therefore, a ruler attends [?] only to what he can be certain of, and leaves alone what he cannot be certain of. Otherwise, rejoicing upon seeing an auspicious omen, rarely will it not transform into a calamity!

"Discerning vigor achieves merit; generous magnanimity brings about abundance." [Book of Documents, Shangshu]
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Feng, comments:
Fan Rong
[Discerning vigor and generous magnanimity together constitute the fundamental substance of governance. Those who compose essays on this get bogged down in…]

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
分析殊失題旨此作　〔明辭雅宜錄式〕
考試官教諭官　批〔見理精明屬辭沖雅〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔融會經旨取之〕
論爲治之體功欲勵而俗欲厚也夫政固有體
也明作以立功惇大以裕俗斯世之治如此耶
且夫治天下者一於寬大則近於弛一於奮勵
則傷於急非政體也王旣示羣臣以意嚮其郎
有僚也當何如哉吾知事功興廢存乎人臣之
無功者惟其狃於因循而振揚之氣寡也今皆
===
知上意在立功而意氣若爲之會爲本之精白
之心鼓以邁往之力明明在下將夙夜以趨之
恐不及者也是臣無隱忠國有凝績且舉吾之
不及爲者而光大之矣不亦有功乎俗化寬急
視所尚民之不裕者惟其過於繩削而大雅之
治衰也今皆知上意在厚俗而德化若爲之培
焉主之惇厚之度持以博大之規渾渾其政將
從容以俟之無敢迫者由是上無苛政下有醇
風且舉東郊之不順者而涵濡之矣不其成裕
punctuated:
分析，殊失題旨。此作〔明辭雅，宜錄式。〕
考試官教諭官　批：〔見理精明，屬辭沖雅。〕
考試官學正蘇　批：〔融會經旨，取之。〕
論爲治之體，功欲勵而俗欲厚也。夫政固有體也，明作以立功，惇大以裕俗，斯世之治如此耶！且夫治天下者，一於寬大則近於弛，一於奮勵則傷於急，非政體也。王旣示羣臣以意嚮，其郎有僚也，當何如哉？吾知事功興廢存乎人，臣之無功者，惟其狃於因循而振揚之氣寡也。今皆知上意在立功，而意氣若爲之會焉，本之精白之心，鼓以邁往之力，明明在下，將夙夜以趨之，恐不及者，也是臣無隱忠，國有凝績，且舉吾之不及爲者而光大之矣，不亦有功乎？俗化寬急視所尚，民之不裕者，惟其過於繩削而大雅之治衰也。今皆知上意在厚俗，而德化若爲之培焉，主之惇厚之度，持以博大之規，渾渾其政，將從容以俟之，無敢迫者，由是上無苛政，下有醇風，且舉東郊之不順者而涵濡之矣，不其成裕
translation_en:
…dissecting them separately quite misses the point of the topic. In this piece [the elucidation is clear and the diction refined; it is worthy of being recorded as a model].
Examiner, Instructor Guan, comments: [Perceives the principles with incisive clarity and composes the words with poised elegance.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Su, comments: [Synthesizes the meaning of the Classic; selected.]

Discussing the fundamental structure of governance: achievements should be roused and customs should be enriched. Now, administration inherently has its fundamental structure. With clear-sightedness and energetic action to establish achievements, and with generous magnanimity to enrich customs—such is the governance of this age! Moreover, for one who governs all under Heaven, to be solely devoted to leniency and breadth borders on laxity, while to be solely devoted to vigorous exertion harms through haste; neither is the proper structure of administration. Once the King has shown the assembled ministers the direction of his intent, when they draw near to their colleagues in office, how should they conduct themselves?

I know that the rise and fall of accomplishments depend on men. Why ministers fail to achieve merit is simply because they are habituated to routine and lack a rousing, uplifting spirit. Now all know that the sovereign's intent lies in establishing achievements, and their spirit and resolve seem to converge for this purpose. Grounded in a pure and spotless heart, and spurred on by forward-striving vigor, shining brightly below, they will hasten to their duties morning and night as if fearing they might fall short. Thus ministers withhold no hidden loyalty, the state possesses consolidated achievements, and furthermore, they take even what I had not yet been able to accomplish and gloriously enlarge it—have they not then achieved merit?

Whether the transformation of customs is lenient or urgent depends on what is valued. Why the people lack abundance and ease is simply because they are subjected to excessive restriction and paring, so that governance of great elegance declines. Now all know that the sovereign's intent lies in enriching customs, and moral transformation seems to be nurtured for this purpose. Guided by a generous and thick-minded measure, and upheld by a broad and grand framework, their administration is vast and uncarved; they will wait upon the people with unhurried composure, none daring to press them harshly. Consequently, above there is no harsh administration, below there are pure and simple customs, and furthermore, they take even the disobedient of the eastern suburbs and steep them in moral influence—does this not bring about generous abundance…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
乎知是則若舜撫事之道盡而新邑之治斯謂
有體矣王其永有譽哉雖然此非人臣所自為
也上使之也上嚴明則下無敢以慢應上寬和
則下無敢以刻應周公之言徑犫也有旨哉後
世綜核者歸於苛察仁厚者失於優柔機始乎
上而習成乎下治之不古宜矣有天下者鑒之
詩
以我齊明與我犧羊以社以方我田既臧
農夫之慶琴瑟擊鼓以御田祖以祈甘
雨以介我稷黍以穀我士女
陳　熺
同考試官教諭吳　批〔報歲祈年公卿為民至意此篇〕
〔詞順氣和藹然一體之愛可錄〕
考試官教諭官　批〔詞壯而雅意婉而明〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔氣格舂容辭理俱□〕
===
公卿之所以事神者莫非為乎民也蓋國家以
有年為慶也報之祈之公卿之為民也殷哉歌
甫田者曰有田祿之入者不敢忘其民尤不敢
punctuated:
乎！知是，則若彝撫事之道盡，而新邑之治斯謂有體矣。王其永有譽哉！雖然，此非人臣所自為也，上使之也。上嚴明則下無敢以慢應，上寬和則下無敢以刻應，周公之言徑犫也，有旨哉！後世綜核者歸於苛察，仁厚者失於優柔，機始乎上而習成乎下，治之不古，宜矣。有天下者鑒之。

詩

以我齊明，與我犧羊，以社以方。我田既臧，農夫之慶。琴瑟擊鼓，以御田祖，以祈甘雨，以介我稷黍，以穀我士女。

陳熺

同考試官教諭吳批：〔報歲祈年，公卿為民至意。此篇〕〔詞順氣和，藹然一體之愛，可錄。〕
考試官教諭官批：〔詞壯而雅，意婉而明。〕
考試官學正蘇批：〔氣格舂容，辭理俱□。〕

公卿之所以事神者，莫非為乎民也。蓋國家以有年為慶也，報之祈之，公卿之為民也殷哉！歌《甫田》者曰：有田祿之入者，不敢忘其民，尤不敢
translation_en:
… [not become prosperous]? Understanding this, the way of observing the constant norms and managing affairs is fulfilled, and the governance of the new capital can thus be said to have attained its proper substance. May the King forever enjoy renown! Even so, this is not something that ministers bring about by themselves; it is the ruler above who causes them to do so. When the ruler above is strict and discerning, those below dare not respond with negligence; when the ruler above is lenient and harmonious, those below dare not respond with harshness. How meaningful are the Duke of Zhou's direct and earnest words [?]! In later ages, those who stressed comprehensive verification ended up in harsh scrutiny, while those who favored benevolent kindness erred in weak indecisiveness. The motivating force begins above and the custom forms below; it is no wonder that governance does not match antiquity. Let those who possess the Empire take this as a mirror.

Book of Odes (Shijing)

"With our pure millet, and our sacrificial sheep, we sacrifice to the spirits of the land and the four quarters. That our fields are in such good condition is a matter of joy for our husbandmen. With zithers and lutes, and beating of drums, we welcome the Father of Husbandry, to pray for sweet rain, to increase our millet, and to nourish our men and women."

Chen Xi 陳熺

Associate Examiner Instructor Wu 吳 comments: 〔Giving thanks for the harvest and praying for an abundant year reflect the utmost care of the dukes and ministers for the people. This essay is〕 〔smooth in diction and harmonious in vital breath, suffused with an amiable love that regards all as one body; it is worthy of being recorded.〕
Examiner Instructor Guan 官 comments: 〔The diction is vigorous yet refined; the meaning is gentle yet clear.〕
Examiner Director of Studies Su 蘇 comments: 〔The style and tone are calm and leisurely, and both the phrasing and reasoning are [?].〕

Everything the dukes and ministers do in serving the spirits is on behalf of the people. Indeed, the state takes an abundant year as its cause for celebration; in giving thanks for it and praying for it, how earnest are the dukes and ministers on behalf of the people! The singer of the ode "Broad Fields" (Futian 甫田) says: Those who receive the revenues of fields and emoluments dare not forget their people, and even less do they dare…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
庶其神我覩今日之祭知公卿之慮民者周矣
徵祭之有報所以答神貺也今也以我齊明粢
盛潔矣與我犧羊肥腯具矣備斯禮也於以即
方社之神而報賽行焉所以然者蓋我有黍稷
藝之者農夫而錫之者方社也今此薿薿之盛
我田亦既臧矣豈敢貪功於天哉良以農夫耘
耔之勤上感乎神神以善有之慶溥及於農我
實陰賴農夫之餘慶耳慶既在民則報不爲我
也烏容以不舉哉報而即祈所以望神倖也今
===
也爰補琴瑟聞其歌矣爰擊土鼓協其氣矣和
斯樂也於以御田祖之神而祈禱行焉所以然
者蓋我有士女穀之者黍稷而司之者田祖也
今此田祖之御甘雨由之祈矣豈徒徼福於己
哉正以天澤之盛既普及於大田黍稷之茂可
徧養乎士女我將永賴士女之餘休耳休既在
民則所不爲我也烏可以不舉哉可若公卿者
蓋無一念不在民矣抑此感世太和之象也上
之言曰農夫之慶曰穀我士女而下之思報則
punctuated: 庶其神。我覩今日之祭，知公卿之慮民者周矣。徵祭之有報，所以答神貺也。今也以我齊明，粢盛潔矣；與我犧羊，肥腯具矣。備斯禮也，於以即方、社之神而報賽行焉。所以然者，蓋我有黍稷，藝之者農夫，而錫之者方、社也。今此薿薿之盛，我田亦既臧矣，豈敢貪功於天哉？良以農夫耘耔之勤，上感乎神，神以善有之慶溥及於農，我實陰賴農夫之餘慶耳。慶既在民，則報不爲我也，烏容以不舉哉？報而即祈，所以望神倖也。今也爰補琴瑟，聞其歌矣；爰擊土鼓，協其氣矣。和斯樂也，於以御田祖之神而祈禱行焉。所以然者，蓋我有士女，穀之者黍稷，而司之者田祖也。今此田祖之御，甘雨由之祈矣，豈徒徼福於己哉？正以天澤之盛，既普及於大田，黍稷之茂，可徧養乎士女，我將永賴士女之餘休耳。休既在民，則所不爲我也，烏可以不舉哉？可若公卿者，蓋無一念不在民矣。抑此感世太和之象也。上之言曰「農夫之慶」，曰「穀我士女」，而下之思報，則
translation_en:
… neglect[?] their spirits. When I observe the sacrifices of today, I know that the consideration of the lords and high officials for the common people is thorough indeed.

Observing that among sacrifices there is thanksgiving, it is the means by which one answers the blessings of the spirits. Now, with our pure millet, the vessel-offerings are clean; along with our sacrificial sheep, the fat and plump victims are prepared. Completing these rites, we thereby approach the spirits of the Four Quarters and the Soil, and the thanksgiving sacrifice is performed. The reason for this is that although we possess glutinous and panicled millet, those who plant it are the farmers, while those who bestow it are the spirits of the Four Quarters and the Soil. Now, with this luxuriant abundance, our fields have already been blessed with good fortune—how would we dare to greedily claim the merit of Heaven as our own? Truly, it is because the farmers' diligence in weeding and hilling has moved the spirits above, and the spirits have broadly extended the blessing of a bountiful harvest to the farmers; we in truth secretly rely upon the surplus blessings of the farmers. Since the blessing resides with the people, the thanksgiving is not for our own sake—how could we fail to perform it?

Following thanksgiving immediately with supplication is the means by which one hopes for the favor of the spirits. Now, we strike up[?] the zithers and lutes, and their songs are heard; we beat the earthen drums, and their vital breath is harmonized. Harmonizing this music, we thereby welcome the spirit of the Father of Husbandry, and the prayers of supplication are performed. The reason for this is that although we possess young men and women, what nourishes them is the glutinous and panicled millet, while the one who presides over it is the Father of Husbandry. Now, with this welcoming of the Father of Husbandry, sweet rain is thereby prayed for—is this merely to seek good fortune for ourselves? It is precisely because when the abundance of Heaven's moisture reaches universally across the great fields, the luxuriance of the glutinous and panicled millet can nourish the young men and women everywhere, and we shall forever rely upon the surplus felicity of those young men and women. Since the felicity resides with the people, the supplication[?] is not for our own sake—how could we fail to perform it?

Such lords and high officials[?] truly have not a single thought that does not rest with the people! Moreover, this is an emblem of the Supreme Harmony of a flourishing[?] age. The words of those above say, "It is the blessing of the farmers," and "to nourish our young men and women," while when those below think of repaying them, they…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
曰雨我公田遂及我私此豈復有君民之隔哉
後世泰山梁父歲不虛祀而祝史陳詞無關民
瘼民之疾視其上固宜矣
干祿百福子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
馬崇化
同考試官教諭吳　批〔人君昌後之福從纘統上說深〕
得祝頌之體
考試官教諭官　批〔溫潤懇切善發忠愛〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔意味雋永〕
===
詩人願王者之福惟後嗣之各宜其位也夫王
者以昌後爲慶也子孫多而且賢何君王之不
宜哉公尸莕鳧鷖也若曰王者之興孰非天命
是故既爲其身計又爲子孫計皆福之不易致
者也吾王有顯德而天命申焉則是顯顯之德
若以干祿也而天祿自從人民之宜非以求福
也而百福咸集曷以王之子孫觀之蓋萬世君
王之位匪多子孫孰與共之天福吾王爲之世
衍其派焉子以繼子也孫以繼孫也綿綿奕奕
punctuated:
曰：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」此豈復有君民之隔哉！後世泰山、梁父歲不虛祀，而祝史陳詞無關民瘼，民之疾視其上，固宜矣。

干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
馬崇化
同考試官教諭吳　批〔人君昌後之福，從纘統上說，深得祝頌之體。〕
考試官教諭官　批〔溫潤懇切，善發忠愛。〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔意味雋永。〕
詩人願王者之福，惟後嗣之各宜其位也。夫王者以昌後爲慶也，子孫多而且賢，何君王之不宜哉！公尸莕鳧鷖也，若曰：王者之興，孰非天命？是故既爲其身計，又爲子孫計，皆福之不易致者也。吾王有顯德而天命申焉，則是顯顯之德，若以干祿也，而天祿自從；人民之宜，非以求福也，而百福咸集。曷以王之子孫觀之？蓋萬世君王之位，匪多子孫，孰與共之？天福吾王，爲之世衍其派焉。子以繼子也，孫以繼孫也，綿綿奕奕，
translation_en:
… say, "May it rain on our public fields, and then reach our private ones!" How could there still be any barrier between ruler and people? In later ages, Mount Tai and Liangfu did not go a year without sacrifices, yet the words presented by the invocators and scribes had no bearing on the sufferings of the people; that the people looked upon their superiors with resentment was certainly fitting.

"Seeking emolument, a hundred blessings; / Sons and grandsons, a thousand, a hundred million. / Reverent and august, / Fitting to be lords, fitting to be kings." [Ode 249, Jia le]
Ma Chonghua 馬崇化
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wu 吳, comments: 〔Speaking of a ruler's blessing of prosperous descendants from the perspective of continuing the royal line deeply captures the proper form of celebratory praise.〕
Examiner, Instructor Guan 官, comments: 〔Warm, refined, and earnest, skillfully expressing loyalty and affection.〕
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Su 蘇, comments: 〔Of rich and lasting flavor.〕

The poet wishes for the king's blessing solely that his descendants may each be suited to their positions. Now, a true king takes making his posterity prosperous as his good fortune; if his sons and grandsons are both numerous and worthy, how could they not be suited to be lords and kings? In response to "Wild Ducks" (Fu yi, Ode 248) for the impersonator of the dead [reading 答 for 莕] [?], it is as if to say: In the rise of a true king, what is not the Mandate of Heaven? Therefore, taking thought both for his own person and for his sons and grandsons are alike blessings not easily attained. Our king possesses illustrious virtue and the Mandate of Heaven is renewed in him; thus this resplendent virtue, as though seeking emolument, is naturally followed by Heaven's emolument; and his suitability to the people and officers, though not aimed at praying for blessings, brings a hundred blessings all together. Why not observe this through the king's sons and grandsons? Indeed, for the positions of lords and kings through ten thousand generations, without numerous sons and grandsons, with whom could they be shared? Heaven blesses our king by extending his lineage from generation to generation. Sons succeed sons, and grandsons succeed grandsons; in unbroken continuity and splendid succession, …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
而千億相繩矣萬世君王之統匪賢子孫孰與
守之天福吾王爲之世作其德焉聖敬日躋也
章美中涵也穆穆皇皇而後先相繼矣嗣而多
不患無君王之託也多而賢不患無君王之具
也由是而支庶世有其國必能祇德亮采以式
是百辟人將稱之曰顯諸侯也不宜君哉本宗
世有天下必能篤恭豈弟以統馭萬方人將稱
之曰明天子也不宜王哉夫宜君者一國福也
亦吾王福也宜王者天下福也亦吾王福也百
===
福之萃孰大於是誠願以是祝焉雖然人主之
福誠在其後嗣乃公尸祝君必並言其嫡庶者
蓋宗子維城而侯封藩屛亦有夾輔之道焉周
之盛時同姓諸侯居天下半及其衰也叔父之
晉王室賴之人謂周過其歷由封建之多也然
後知公尸之言不虛矣
春秋
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕楚子圍鄭〔宣
公十有二年〕
punctuated:
而千億相繩矣。萬世君王之統，匪賢子孫，孰與守之？天福吾王，爲之世作其德焉，聖敬日躋也，章美中涵也，穆穆皇皇，而後先相繼矣。嗣而多，不患無君王之託也；多而賢，不患無君王之具也。由是而支庶世有其國，必能祇德亮采，以式是百辟，人將稱之曰：「顯諸侯也！」不宜君哉？本宗世有天下，必能篤恭豈弟，以統馭萬方，人將稱之曰：「明天子也！」不宜王哉？夫宜君者，一國福也，亦吾王福也；宜王者，天下福也，亦吾王福也。百福之萃，孰大於是？誠願以是祝焉。雖然，人主之福，誠在其後嗣，乃公尸祝君，必並言其嫡庶者，蓋宗子維城，而侯封藩屛，亦有夾輔之道焉。周之盛時，同姓諸侯居天下半；及其衰也，叔父之晉，王室賴之。人謂周過其歷，由封建之多也，然後知公尸之言不虛矣。
《春秋》
「春王正月，城楚丘」〔僖公二年〕；「楚子圍鄭」〔宣公十有二年〕。
translation_en:
…and continuing in an unbroken line of a hundred thousand and a hundred million! As for the dynastic succession of lords and kings for ten thousand generations, if not for worthy sons and grandsons, who could preserve it? Heaven blesses our king by cultivating virtue in his lineage from generation to generation—their sage reverence ascending daily, their resplendent beauty cherished within, solemn and majestic, succeeding one another from first to last. When heirs are numerous, there is no worry of lacking those to whom the charge of lords and kings may be entrusted; when they are both numerous and worthy, there is no worry of lacking the qualities required of lords and kings.

Thus, when the collateral branches possess their states from generation to generation, they will surely be able to revere virtue and brilliantly manage affairs so as to serve as a model for the hundred lords; people will praise them, saying, "Illustrious feudal lords!" Are they not well suited to be lords? When the main lineage possesses the realm from generation to generation, they will surely be able to be steadfastly reverent, amiable, and easy, so as to govern the ten thousand regions; people will praise them, saying, "Enlightened Sons of Heaven!" Are they not well suited to be kings? Now, being suited to be a lord is the blessing of a single state, and also the blessing of our king; being suited to be a king is the blessing of the whole realm, and also the blessing of our king. Among the gathering of a hundred blessings, which is greater than this? Truly, we wish to offer this as our benediction.

Even so, while a ruler's blessing truly lies in his descendants, the reason the impersonator of the dead, in blessing the ruler, обязательно speaks of both the principal and collateral heirs together is that the eldest son of the main line is a fortress wall, while the enfeoffed lords serving as a protective screen also fulfill the way of supporting and assisting. At the height of the Zhou, feudal lords of the same surname occupied half the realm; and when it declined, the royal house relied upon Jin, the state of its royal uncle. People say that the Zhou exceeded its divined span of years because of the great number of its feudal enfeoffments; from this we know that the words of the impersonator of the dead were not empty.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In spring, in the king's first month, they walled Chuqiu" [Second year of Duke Xi]; "The Viscount of Chu besieged Zheng" [Twelfth year of Duke Xuan].

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
馮養志
同考試官教諭周　批〔此題重君臣大節上是作發明〕
〔通透而措詞謹嚴結構精密蓋深於春秋者〕
考試官教諭官　批〔融會傳意莊重典雅〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔有斷案有筆力〕
春秋以大節律人有不論其功者有不録其過
者此封衛之桓入鄭之莊春秋皆略之者其有
所重也夫且賞必以功罰必以罪者王法之常
也功而不賞罪而不罰者王道之權也吾茲有
===
感於齊楚焉桓之城楚丘也木瓜瓊瑤之咏其
功高其利亦甚溥矣經乃深沒其迹者若曰臣
而侵君罪也滎澤告敗衛社已墟而宗伯而几
筵而內史舉無有建茅土之典者桓以諸侯封
之非得罪於天子耶雖斬衛蓬蒿而新其朝市
由君子觀之是皆小惠也已以其小者輕與之
其可哉不書桓公存大節也莊之入皇門也肉
袒牽羊之逆其勢急其情誠可哀矣經乃末減
其罪者若曰臣而無上誅也徵舒不道陳刃已
punctuated:
馮養志
同考試官教諭周　批〔此題重君臣大節上，是作發明通透，而措詞謹嚴，結構精密，蓋深於《春秋》者。〕
考試官教諭官　批〔融會傳意，莊重典雅。〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔有斷案，有筆力。〕
《春秋》以大節律人，有不論其功者，有不録其過者。此封衛之桓、入鄭之莊，《春秋》皆略之者，其有所重也夫！且賞必以功、罰必以罪者，王法之常也；功而不賞、罪而不罰者，王道之權也。吾茲有感於齊、楚焉。桓之城楚丘也，木瓜瓊瑤之咏，其功高，其利亦甚溥矣。經乃深沒其迹者，若曰：臣而侵君，罪也。滎澤告敗，衛社已墟，而宗伯、而几筵、而內史，舉無有建茅土之典者，桓以諸侯封之，非得罪於天子耶？雖斬衛蓬蒿而新其朝市，由君子觀之，是皆小惠也已。以其小者輕與之，其可哉？不書桓公，存大節也。莊之入皇門也，肉袒牽羊之逆，其勢急，其情誠可哀矣。經乃末減其罪者，若曰：臣而無上，誅也。徵舒不道，陳刃已
translation_en:
Feng Yangzhi 馮養志
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhou 周, comments: [This topic places weight on the great moral principle between ruler and subject. This composition elucidates it thoroughly, while its wording is rigorous and its structure tightly knit; surely the author is someone deeply versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu).]
Examiner, County Director of Studies Guan 官, comments: [Synthesizes the meaning of the commentaries; dignified and refined.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Su 蘇, comments: [Possesses decisive judgment and forceful brushwork.]

The Spring and Autumn Annals holds men to the standard of great moral principles: there are cases where it does not reckon their merits, and cases where it does not record their faults. That the Spring and Autumn Annals passes over both Duke Huan’s 桓公 enfeoffment of Wei 衛 and King Zhuang’s 莊王 entry into Zheng 鄭 is because there is something it attaches greater weight to! Moreover, that rewards must follow merit and punishments must follow crime is the constant rule of kingly law; that there is merit without reward and crime without punishment is the expedient weighing (quan 權) of the Kingly Way. In this I am moved to reflection by the cases of Qi 齊 and Chu 楚.

When Duke Huan walled Chuqiu 楚丘, the ode of the “Quince” and “precious jade” (Mugua 木瓜) celebrated it—his merit was lofty and the benefit he conferred was vast indeed. Yet the Classic deeply effaces his trace, as if to say: for a subject to encroach upon the prerogative of the ruler is a crime. When defeat was reported at Rongze 滎澤, the altars of Wei had already been reduced to ruins, yet neither the Minister of Rites (Zongbo 宗伯), nor the ancestral mats and seats, nor the Scribes of the Interior (Neishi 內史) undertook the ceremony of establishing a fief with thatched soil; when Huan, as a feudal lord, enfeoffed it himself, was this not offending against the Son of Heaven? Even though he cleared away the brambles and weeds of Wei and renewed its court and marketplace, from the standpoint of the superior man these were all merely minor favors. To lightly grant him approval on account of something minor—how could that be permissible? Not writing “Duke Huan” preserves the great moral principle.

When King Zhuang entered the Huang Gate (Huangmen 皇門), he was met by the prince of Zheng baring his torso and leading a sheep—the situation was desperate, and the plight was truly pitiable. Yet the Classic mitigates his crime, as if to say: a subject who defies his sovereign must be executed. Xia Zhengshu 夏徵舒 acted against the Way; the blade in Chen 陳 had already…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
發而天王而方伯而四鄰舉無有正殘勅之刑
者莊以外夷討之非有功於中國那雖入鄭國
都而辱其君臣由君子觀之是皆小過也已以
其小者厚誅之其可哉特書圍鄭取大鼎也是
蓋所正者王法則衛不必存所重者人倫則鄭
不必恤聖人爲君臣慮者至矣雖然桓能城衛
不能却狄莊雖討陳幾於縣陳亡國而後存是
假仁也蹊田而奪人是假義也其益稱五又得
罪三王有以夫然皆能糾合主盟則以仲父申
===
叔爲之謀主二君能降心聽之故也國以賢興
詎不信夫
荊人來聘〔莊公二十有三年〕徐人取舒〔僖公三年〕公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳
人鄫人于戚〔襄公五年〕冬楚子蔡侯陳
侯許男頓子沈子徐人越人伐吳〔昭公五年〕
劉繼志
punctuated:
發，而天王、而方伯、而四鄰，舉無有正殘勅之刑者，莊以外夷討之，非有功於中國那？雖入鄭國都而辱其君臣，由君子觀之，是皆小過也已。以其小者厚誅之，其可哉？特書「圍鄭」，取大鼎也。是蓋所正者王法，則衛不必存；所重者人倫，則鄭不必恤。聖人爲君臣慮者至矣。雖然，桓能城衛，不能却狄；莊雖討陳，幾於縣陳。亡國而後存，是假仁也；蹊田而奪人，是假義也。其益稱五，又得罪三王，有以夫！然皆能糾合主盟，則以仲父、申叔爲之謀主，二君能降心聽之故也。國以賢興，詎不信夫！
荊人來聘〔莊公二十有三年〕、徐人取舒〔僖公三年〕、公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚〔襄公五年〕、冬，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、沈子、徐人、越人伐吳〔昭公五年〕。
劉繼志
translation_en:
…been unsheathed, yet neither the Heavenly King, nor the Regional Earl, nor the neighboring states on all four sides took action to enforce the punishment for regicide and rebellion [? 殘勅, for 殘賊]. When King Zhuang, as an outer barbarian, punished him, was this not a service to the Central States? Although he entered the capital of Zheng and humiliated its ruler and ministers, from the perspective of a gentleman, these were all merely minor faults. Would it be right to severely condemn him on account of what is minor? The text specially records "besieged Zheng" because it approves the great moral principle [? 取大鼎, for 取大體]. For where what is being rectified is the King's law, the survival of Wei need not be made the priority; and where what is given weight is human moral relations, Zheng need not be pitied. The Sage's concern for the relationship between ruler and minister was profound indeed. Even so, while Duke Huan was able to wall Wei, he could not repel the Di; and while King Zhuang punished Chen, he nearly annexed Chen as a county. To preserve a state only after letting it perish is counterfeit benevolence; to seize another's ox because it trampled one's field is counterfeit righteousness. That they were grouped among the Five Hegemons and yet offended against the Three Kings—there was good reason for it! Nevertheless, that both were able to bring the states together and preside over covenants was because they had Zhongfu (Guan Zhong 管仲) and Shenshu (Shenshu Shi 申叔時) as their chief advisers, and the two rulers were able to humble their hearts and listen to them. "A state flourishes through worthy men"—how could this not be true!

"People of Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiry" [Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang]; "People of Xu took Shu" [Third year of Duke Xi]; "The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xie, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, people of Wu, and people of Zeng at Qi" [Fifth year of Duke Xiang]; "In winter, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Shen, people of Xu, and people of Yue attacked Wu" [Fifth year of Duke Zhao].

By Liu Jizhi 劉繼志.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭周　批〔發揮春秋待聖賢之意委曲詳盡且格力雅健詞語警拔三復歛衽〕
考試官教諭官　批〔體裁平正詞意馴雅〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔得聖人善善之意〕
春秋待聖賢之後志於善斯善之焉蓋聖人樂
與人為善也況明德之冑耶宜四國之不終於
夷也聞之徐始稱王楚繼稱王吳越因遂稱王
業已淪於夷矣夷狄於中國無時焉可通者然
無亦念其先世也歟思祝融之烈欲識其子孫
===
嘉伯益之忠當存其宗祀賢如太伯使之無後
為善者不亦懼乎功如神禹不得十世宥之懋
動者何以勸乎維玆聘莊之荆即祝融之裔也
方慮其蠶食我諸姬今且執玉而來脩東蒙之
好焉不墜佐帝之聲已取舒之徐即伯益之嗣
也方懼其朋附彼荆楚今且荷戈而往開南征
之徑焉克纘相禹之緒已吳方强大非可責以
禮者而壽夢之來俛首宗盟之晉來會而非往
會其猶有荆蠻之讓耶越在僻遠非可望以義
punctuated:
同考試官教諭周批：〔發揮《春秋》待聖賢之意，委曲詳盡，且格力雅健，詞語警拔，三復歛衽。〕
考試官教諭官批：〔體裁平正，詞意馴雅。〕
考試官學正蘇批：〔得聖人善善之意。〕

《春秋》待聖賢之後，志於善斯善之焉。蓋聖人樂與人為善也，況明德之冑耶？宜四國之不終於夷也。聞之，徐始稱王，楚繼稱王，吳、越因遂稱王，業已淪於夷矣。夷狄於中國，無時焉可通者。然無亦念其先世也歟？思祝融之烈，欲識其子孫；嘉伯益之忠，當存其宗祀。賢如太伯，使之無後，為善者不亦懼乎？功如神禹，不得十世宥之，懋動者何以勸乎？維玆聘莊之荆，即祝融之裔也。方慮其蠶食我諸姬，今且執玉而來，脩東蒙之好焉，不墜佐帝之聲已。取舒之徐，即伯益之嗣也。方懼其朋附彼荆楚，今且荷戈而往，開南征之徑焉，克纘相禹之緒已。吳方强大，非可責以禮者，而壽夢之來，俛首宗盟之晉，來會而非往會，其猶有荆蠻之讓耶？越在僻遠，非可望以義
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhou: [He draws out the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in treating sages and worthies in thorough and intricate detail; moreover, the style and vigor are elegant and robust, and the phrasing is incisive and striking. Having read it three times over, I gather my lapels in respect.]
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Guan: [The form is balanced and proper, and the phrasing and meaning are refined and elegant.]
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Su: [He grasps the Sage's intent in approving of what is good.]

In treating the descendants of sages and worthies, the Spring and Autumn Annals approves of them as soon as they set their minds on goodness. For the Sage delights in joining others in doing good—how much more so when it comes to the descendants of those of illustrious virtue! It is fitting indeed that the four states were not permanently relegated to the status of barbarians. It is heard that Xu first styled itself king, Chu subsequently styled itself king, and Wu and Yue thereupon followed suit in styling themselves king; they had already sunk into barbarianism. Between barbarians and the Central States, there is never a time when diplomatic relations should be conducted. Yet should one not also remember their ancestors? Recalling the meritorious achievements of Zhurong, one wishes to recognize his descendants; praising the loyalty of Boyi, one ought to preserve his ancestral sacrifices. If someone as worthy as Taibo were left without posterity, would not those who do good be afraid? If someone with achievements like the divine Yu could not be pardoned for ten generations, how could those who exert themselves in great endeavors [reading 勳 for 動][?] be encouraged? Now this Jing [Chu] that sent an envoy on a mission of friendly inquiry to Duke Zhuang is none other than the descendant of Zhurong. Just when there was worry that it would nibble away at our various Ji-surname states like a silkworm, now instead it comes holding jade tablets to cultivate friendly relations with the lord of East Meng [Lu], thus not letting fall the renown of having assisted the Sovereign. The Xu that took Shu is none other than the heir of Boyi. Just when there was fear that it would ally itself with and attach itself to that Jing-Chu, now instead it goes forth shouldering halberds to open a path for the southern campaign, thus proving able to continue the enterprise of having assisted Yu. Wu was just then strong and great, and was not one from whom ritual propriety could be demanded; yet with the coming of Shoumeng, it bowed its head to Jin, the leader of the covenant—coming to meet rather than us going to meet it—did it not still possess the yielding spirit of when Taibo fled to the Jing barbarians? Yue lay in a remote and distant region, and was not one from whom righteousness could be expected…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
者而壽過之遣仗鉞朱方之圍從兵而實從義
其庶幾防風之戮耶遡上世而論功德在人心
者不容遂忘山今日以談禮義如中國者豈得
終弃四國耕人蓋嘉其事也亦論其世也嗟夫
聖人善善之心何其長哉四國淫名僭號惡莫
大焉猶且推念其先引之使來旌錄其善褒之
以禮人知為善足以庇其後孰不勉而之善哉
後世乃有以子孫之故遂忘其先以父祖之愆
並錮其後者是皆不講春秋之義也
===
禮記
故禮也者義之實也協諸義而協則禮雖
先王未之有可以義起也
周一梧
同考試官教諭李　批〔禮本於義是聖人制作盡善處〕
此作雅辭逸趣讀之題意宛然稱作家也
考試官教諭官　批〔理精而明詞約而盡〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔簡當可式〕
禮為義之定制以其本於義也蓋禮以達義則
punctuated:
者，而壽過之遣，仗鉞朱方之圍，從兵而實從義，其庶幾防風之戮耶？遡上世而論，功德在人心者，不容遂忘；山今日以談，禮義如中國者，豈得終弃？四國耕人，蓋嘉其事也，亦論其世也。嗟夫！聖人善善之心，何其長哉！四國淫名僭號，惡莫大焉；猶且推念其先，引之使來，旌錄其善，褒之以禮。人知為善足以庇其後，孰不勉而之善哉？後世乃有以子孫之故遂忘其先，以父祖之愆並錮其後者，是皆不講《春秋》之義也。

《禮記》
「故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。」
周一梧
同考試官教諭李　批：〔禮本於義，是聖人制作盡善處。〕此作雅辭逸趣，讀之題意宛然，稱作家也。
考試官教諭官　批：〔理精而明，詞約而盡。〕
考試官學正蘇　批：〔簡當可式。〕
禮為義之定制，以其本於義也。蓋禮以達義，則
translation_en:
… [cannot be expected to act with righteousness], yet when Shouguo 壽過 was dispatched, wielding a battle-axe at the siege of Zhufang 朱方, he joined a military expedition that was in truth a righteous cause—did this not come close to the execution of Fangfeng 防風 [by Yu the Great]? Tracing back to antiquity, merits and virtues that remain in people's hearts must not be hastily forgotten; speaking from the present day [reading 山 as 由], when [peripheral states] practice ritual and righteousness like the Central States, how could they be permanently cast aside? That the four states were recorded as "persons" (人) [rather than "耕" (?)] was both to commend their deeds and to take account of their lineages across generations. Alas! How far-reaching is the Sage's heart in praising goodness! There is no greater evil than the four states' usurping of titles and styles; yet he still remembered their ancestors, drew them in so that they might come forward, singled out and recorded their good deeds, and commended them through ritual protocol. Once people know that doing good suffices to shelter their descendants, who would not strive toward goodness? In later ages, however, there were those who forgot a family's ancestors because of the faults of the descendants, or barred the descendants from advancement along with the transgressions of their fathers and grandfathers—all because they failed to study the righteous principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu).

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore, ritual is the substance of righteousness. If one measures a practice against righteousness and it accords with it, then even if it is a ritual that the former kings did not have, it may be instituted on the basis of righteousness."
By Zhou Yiwu 周一梧.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li 李, comments: [That ritual is rooted in righteousness is wherein the institutions created by the sages achieve perfection.] This essay possesses refined diction and transcendent flair; upon reading it, the meaning of the topic comes vividly to life—it may truly be called the work of a master.
Examiner, Instructor Guan 官, comments: [The reasoning is subtle yet clear; the phrasing is concise yet exhaustive.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Su 蘇, comments: [Concise and apt; worthy of serving as a model.]
Ritual serves as the fixed institution of righteousness because it is rooted in righteousness. Indeed, since ritual is the means of giving expression to righteousness, then…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
義所以本之者也觀此則禮爲義之實不亦可
見哉今夫天下有當然之至理而後有已然之
成法是故禮非聖人意也義之實也吾心之制
不可見而品節之爲中正之規運量無端者燦
然可循也事理之宜無定在而裁定之爲不易
之則通變無方者秩然可執也禮非義之實乎
是何也蓋義者禮之權度而先王據之以定制
者也故君子用禮豈成迹之拘哉亦取裁於義
而已或因時以探其宜即之吾心而安焉則義
===
存此禮亦在此矣雖先王未之有吾可據義以
創作之章程自是可立也或因事以通其會質
之至理而當焉則義由此立禮由此出矣雖先
王未之有吾可據義以品秩之典禮自是可興
也夫禮起於義如此此所以爲義之實而先王
修之以治人情者謂不有由然哉嘗觀禮義均
性之德若非待義而後定者惟吾性有宜品節
斯斯之謂禮耳夫子不云乎義以爲質禮以行
之此合內外之道也後世以義爲外者既不知
punctuated: 義所以本之者也。觀此，則禮爲義之實，不亦可見哉？今夫天下有當然之至理，而後有已然之成法。是故禮非聖人意也，義之實也。吾心之制不可見，而品節之爲中正之規，運量無端者，燦然可循也；事理之宜無定在，而裁定之爲不易之則，通變無方者，秩然可執也。禮非義之實乎？是何也？蓋義者，禮之權度，而先王據之以定制者也。故君子用禮，豈成迹之拘哉？亦取裁於義而已。或因時以探其宜，即之吾心而安焉，則義存此，禮亦在此矣；雖先王未之有，吾可據義以創作之，章程自是可立也。或因事以通其會，質之至理而當焉，則義由此立，禮由此出矣；雖先王未之有，吾可據義以品秩之，典禮自是可興也。夫禮起於義如此，此所以爲義之實，而先王修之以治人情者，謂不有由然哉？嘗觀禮義均性之德，若非待義而後定者；惟吾性有宜，品節斯，斯之謂禮耳。夫子不云乎：「義以爲質，禮以行之。」此合內外之道也。後世以義爲外者，既不知
translation_en: … rightness is that upon which it is founded. Looking at it from this perspective, can one not see that ritual is the substance of rightness? Now, in the world there is first the supreme principle of what ought to be, and only afterward is there the established law of what has already been done. Therefore, ritual is not the arbitrary invention of the sages; it is the substance of rightness. The regulations of our minds are invisible, yet when graded and moderated into unbiased and upright rules, that which operates without bounds becomes brilliantly clear to follow; the appropriateness in the principles of affairs has no fixed location, yet when tailored and settled into immutable standards, that which adapts without limit becomes orderly to uphold. Is ritual not the substance of rightness? Why is this so? Because rightness is the scale and measure of ritual, upon which the former kings relied to establish their regulations. Therefore, when the gentleman employs ritual, how could he be bound by established traces? He simply takes his measure from rightness, and nothing more. Perhaps by responding to the times to seek out what is appropriate, bringing it to our minds and finding peace therein, rightness abides here, and ritual is also here; even if the former kings never had it, we can rely on rightness to originate it, and statutes and regulations can thus be established. Or perhaps by responding to affairs to comprehend their convergence, testing it against the supreme principle and finding it fitting, rightness is thereby established, and ritual thereby emerges; even if the former kings never had it, we can rely on rightness to grade and order it, and canonical rituals can thus be instituted. Since ritual arises from rightness in this way, this is why it is the substance of rightness—and as for the former kings cultivating it in order to govern human feelings, could one say that this was without reason? I have observed that ritual and rightness are both virtues of human nature, as if ritual did not have to wait upon rightness before being settled; it is only that when our nature possesses what is appropriate, grading and moderating this—this is what is called ritual. Did the Master not say, "The gentleman takes rightness as his basic stuff, and by ritual he puts it into practice"? This is the Way of uniting the internal and the external. In later ages, those who regard rightness as external neither understand …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
義而以禮爲僞者又豈知爲性術之形哉學者
尚合而觀之
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮樂者敦和率神而從天禮者
別宜居鬼而從地
俞狀□可
同考試官教諭李　批〔說禮樂同流造化旅體認真切〕
〔發揮明盡且通篇簡粹無一款語深養之士也敬服敬服〕
考試官教諭官　批〔精純沖邃迥異諸作〕
===
考試官學正蘇　批〔文整意盡〕
惟禮樂本於造化而所以合德者在是矣甚矣
聖人制作之精也效法於天地而天地賴以成
焉一體之應何如哉且禮樂之道原於天地制
於聖人是故推之於始可以究制作之原要之
於終可以觀合一之妙今夫天以陽生萬物而
春作夏長皆仁也皆乾元之所以資始也以陰
成萬物則秋斂冬藏皆義也皆坤元之所以代
終也仁則絪緼化醇至和行焉氣之統同者近
punctuated:
義，而以禮爲僞者，又豈知爲性術之形哉！學者尚合而觀之。

春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。樂者，敦和率神而從天；禮者，別宜居鬼而從地。
俞狀□可
同考試官教諭李　批〔說禮樂同流造化，旅體認真切，發揮明盡。且通篇簡粹，無一款語，深養之士也。敬服，敬服！〕
考試官教諭官　批〔精純沖邃，迥異諸作。〕
考試官學正蘇　批〔文整意盡。〕

惟禮樂本於造化，而所以合德者在是矣。甚矣，聖人制作之精也！效法於天地，而天地賴以成焉，一體之應何如哉！且禮樂之道，原於天地，制於聖人。是故推之於始，可以究制作之原；要之於終，可以觀合一之妙。今夫天以陽生萬物，而春作夏長，皆仁也，皆乾元之所以資始也；以陰成萬物，則秋斂冬藏，皆義也，皆坤元之所以代終也。仁則絪緼化醇，至和行焉，氣之統同者近
translation_en:
… righteousness; and as for those who regard ritual as artifice, how could they know that it is the outward manifestation of the operations of human nature! Scholars ought to examine them together.

"Spring brings forth and summer fosters growth: this is benevolence. Autumn gathers in and winter stores away: this is righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music, and righteousness is akin to ritual. Music strengthens harmony, leads the expansive spirit, and follows Heaven; ritual distinguishes what is fitting, settles the contracting spirit, and follows Earth."

Yu Zhuang[?]ke [?]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li, comments: "It explains how ritual and music flow together with the creative transformations of nature. The grasp of the substance [?] is earnest and exact, and the exposition is clear and exhaustive. Moreover, the entire essay is concise and pure, without a single clichés or stock phrase [?]. He is a scholar of deep cultivation. Admirable, admirable!"
Examiner, Instructor Guan, comments: "Refined, pure, serene, and profound—vastly different from the other compositions."
Examiner, Academic Director Su, comments: "The composition is well-ordered and the meaning is fully expressed."

Indeed, ritual and music are rooted in the creative transformations of nature, and that by which they harmonize with its virtue lies right here. Profound indeed is the subtlety of the sages' institutions! They modeled them upon Heaven and Earth, and Heaven and Earth in turn rely upon them for their completion—how great is the resonance of their forming a single body! Moreover, the Way of ritual and music originates in Heaven and Earth and was instituted by the sages. Therefore, by tracing it back to its beginning, one can investigate the origin of their creation; by summing it up at its end, one can observe the marvel of their unity. Now, Heaven gives birth to the myriad things through yang, so that bringing forth in spring and fostering growth in summer are all benevolence, and are all that by which the Primal Yang (Qianyuan) initiates the beginning of things. It brings the myriad things to completion through yin, so that gathering in during autumn and storing away in winter are all righteousness, and are all that by which the Primal Yin (Kunyuan) completes the end of things. With benevolence, generative forces fuse and transform into richness, and supreme harmony prevails therein; the unifying coalescence of vital energy is akin…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
於樂矣義則品類各正至序立焉質之異宜者
近於禮矣夫禮樂造端於天地如此究其用何
如哉吾知仁者和也陽之伸而行於天者也樂
作則太和自我鼓之天地之和感而益敦焉發
舒乎常伸之氣而隨天運以不息矣義者宜也
陰之屈而行於地者也禮制則物宜自我別之
天地之宜因之各定焉收斂乎退藏之化而隨
坤德以奠麗矣是則聖人之制作效法天地而
同流上下如此亦惟理之一耳嗚呼此聖人制
===
作之善也而所以基之者心也是故心天地之
心而後能體天地之撰不然經曲咸韶固在也
而合天之用不復見何哉然則君子欲究制作
之原當先禮樂之本
第貳場
論
學先義利之辨
同考試官教諭劉　批
白所知
發揮義利之辨若析秋毫而辭
punctuated:
於樂矣；義則品類各正，至序立焉，質之異宜者近於禮矣。夫禮樂造端於天地如此，究其用何如哉？吾知仁者和也，陽之伸而行於天者也。樂作則太和自我鼓之，天地之和感而益敦焉，發舒乎常伸之氣，而隨天運以不息矣。義者宜也，陰之屈而行於地者也。禮制則物宜自我別之，天地之宜因之各定焉，收斂乎退藏之化，而隨坤德以奠麗矣。是則聖人之制作，效法天地而同流上下如此，亦惟理之一耳。嗚呼！此聖人制作之善也，而所以基之者心也。是故心天地之心，而後能體天地之撰。不然，經曲、咸韶固在也，而合天之用不復見，何哉？然則君子欲究制作之原，當先禮樂之本。

第貳場
論
學先義利之辨
同考試官教諭劉　批
白所知
發揮義利之辨，若析秋毫，而辭
translation_en:
… to music; in righteousness, the various categories of things each attain their proper state and supreme order is established—thus, that which differentiates substances according to what is fitting is akin to ritual. Now, since ritual and music originate in Heaven and Earth in this way, what is the ultimate effect of their application? I know that benevolence is harmony—it is the expansion of yang operating in Heaven. When music is created, supreme harmony is roused by us, and the harmony of Heaven and Earth is moved and made ever deeper, unfolding the ever-expanding vital force and following the movement of Heaven without cease. Righteousness is appropriateness—it is the contraction of yin operating on Earth. When ritual is instituted, what is appropriate for things is distinguished by us, and the appropriateness of Heaven and Earth is thereby settled for each, gathering in the transformations that retreat into storage and following the virtue of Earth (kun) to establish their firm attachments. Thus, the creations of the sages model themselves on Heaven and Earth and flow together with them above and below in this manner, simply because their principle is one. Alas! Such is the perfection of the sages' creations, and that upon which they are founded is the mind. Therefore, one must take the mind of Heaven and Earth as one's own mind before one can embody the workings of Heaven and Earth. Otherwise, the major and minor rules of ritual and the Xianchao and Shao music would certainly still exist, yet their function of uniting with Heaven would no longer be seen—why is that? That being so, if the gentleman wishes to investigate the origin of creating institutions, he must first attend to the fundamental basis of ritual and music.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
意精微發爲名言場中作者殆不多得
考試官教諭官　批　闔闢操縱明瑩沖雅
考試官學正蘇　批　有學識有議論
人心之天不可以有所雜也天無爲也雜之以
有爲則人矣天人之介其端倪甚微其幾希甚
隱其微隱隱之地甚難析純之而天則天焉雜之
而人則人焉防之不豫將以人滅天而奔潰四
出至於不可禦識之不眞將指人爲天終身由
之而有不自覺者噫嘻可懼哉宋儒張子之論
===
學也而曰莫先於義利之辨夫喻義爲君子喻
利爲小人孔子已言之矣故儒者譚義利者別
蒼素是果何待於辨也嗚呼使義之與利信若
蒼之與素又焉用辨惟夫利固爲利義亦有時
爲利人而至於以義爲利則手目之擩視所不
及師友之箴規所不加其善與惡其欺與歉惟
已所獨知者故利之爲利易辨也義之爲利未
易辨也利之爲利卽途人能知之義之爲利在
儒者或不察焉則嘗怪師商在孔門稱高弟也
punctuated:
意精微，發爲名言，場中作者殆不多得。
考試官教諭官　批：闔闢操縱，明瑩沖雅。
考試官學正蘇　批：有學識，有議論。
人心之天，不可以有所雜也。天，無爲也；雜之以有爲，則人矣。天人之介，其端倪甚微，其幾希甚隱，其微隱隱之地甚難析。純之而天，則天焉；雜之而人，則人焉。防之不豫，將以人滅天，而奔潰四出，至於不可禦；識之不眞，將指人爲天，終身由之，而有不自覺者。噫嘻，可懼哉！宋儒張子之論學也，而曰：「莫先於義利之辨。」夫喻義爲君子，喻利爲小人，孔子已言之矣。故儒者譚義利者別蒼素，是果何待於辨也？嗚呼！使義之與利，信若蒼之與素，又焉用辨？惟夫利固爲利，義亦有時爲利。人而至於以義爲利，則手目之擩視所不及，師友之箴規所不加，其善與惡，其欺與歉，惟已所獨知者。故利之爲利，易辨也；義之爲利，未易辨也。利之爲利，卽途人能知之；義之爲利，在儒者或不察焉。則嘗怪師、商在孔門稱高弟也，
translation_en:
…and the meaning is subtle and refined, expressed in memorable words; there are probably few writers in the examination compound to match this.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Guan, comments: Opening and closing, controlling and releasing with mastery; clear, luminous, and serenely elegant.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Su, comments: Possesses both scholarly insight and persuasive argument.

The Heaven within the human mind must not be adulterated by anything. Heaven acts without ulterior motive (wuwei); if it is adulterated with ulterior motive, it becomes merely human. At the boundary between the heavenly and the human, the initial stirrings are exceedingly subtle, the slight distinction is deeply hidden, and that subtle, deeply hidden realm is extremely difficult to dissect. Keep it pure and heavenly, and it remains Heaven; adulterate it with the human, and it becomes human. If one does not guard against this beforehand, the human will extinguish the heavenly, bursting forth in all directions until it cannot be checked; if one does not recognize it truly, one will mistake the human for the heavenly, following it all one's life without ever realizing it. Alas, how terrifying!

When Master Zhang [Zhang Zai 張載 or Zhang Shi 張栻], the Song Confucian, discussed learning, he said: "Nothing comes before distinguishing between righteousness and profit." Now, that the gentleman understands righteousness while the petty man understands profit had already been stated by Confucius. Thus Confucians speak of righteousness and profit as being as distinct as dark blue and white—what need, then, is there to distinguish between them? Alas! If righteousness and profit were truly like dark blue and white, what need indeed would there be to distinguish them? It is only that while profit is of course profit, righteousness too can at times become profit. When a person reaches the point of using righteousness for the sake of profit, it is beyond what pointing hands and watching eyes [cf. Great Learning,十目所視，十手所指; 擩視 for 指視?] can reach, and beyond what the admonitions of teachers and friends can touch; its goodness or evil, its self-deception or dissatisfaction, are known to oneself alone. Therefore, when profit acts as profit, it is easy to distinguish; when righteousness acts as profit, it is not easy to distinguish. Profit as profit even a passerby on the road can recognize; righteousness as profit even Confucians sometimes fail to discern. Thus I have often wondered how Shi [Zizhang 子張,颛孫師] and Shang [Zixia 子夏,卜商], who were renowned as foremost disciples in the school of Confucius…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
乃記子張者曰學干祿孔子戒子夏曰小人儒
夫學與干祿異事也儒與小人異稱也師商不
能辨之庸非堂堂之習正才高意廣者之過紛
華之悅卽篤信聖人者且不免耶彼其誦詩書
談仁義日以聖人爲之依歸豈不曰吾爲義也
乃其心一有所爲而爲遂墮於利而不自覺甚
哉義利之難辨也能辨之斯可以入道也辨之
當何如我聞曰行而宜之之謂義義旣曰宜則
凡有所爲皆理之不得不爲非有所爲而後爲
===
之也是故饑之於食渴之於飲宜也非爲人而
食之飲之也寒之於裘暑之於葛宜也非爲人
而裘之葛之也夫學亦當如是也博聞而强記
非以待問也懷忠而守信非以待舉也積學而
力行非以待取也蹈義而履仁非以邇譽也飭
躬而勵行非以遠詆也以獨行爲義則毀譽是
非無私計焉以致身爲義則死生利害無苟避
焉以鞠躬爲義則成敗利鈍無逆覩焉董子曰
正其誼不謀其利明其道不計其功辨莫辨於
punctuated: 乃記子張者曰「學干祿」，孔子戒子夏曰「小人儒」。夫學與干祿，異事也；儒與小人，異稱也。師、商不能辨之，庸非堂堂之習，正才高意廣者之過；紛華之悅，卽篤信聖人者且不免耶？彼其誦《詩》、《書》，談仁義，日以聖人爲之依歸，豈不曰「吾爲義」也？乃其心一有所爲而爲，遂墮於利而不自覺。甚哉，義利之難辨也！能辨之，斯可以入道也。辨之當何如？我聞曰：「行而宜之之謂義。」義旣曰宜，則凡有所爲，皆理之不得不爲，非有所爲而後爲之也。是故饑之於食、渴之於飲，宜也，非爲人而食之、飲之也；寒之於裘、暑之於葛，宜也，非爲人而裘之、葛之也。夫學亦當如是也。博聞而强記，非以待問也；懷忠而守信，非以待舉也；積學而力行，非以待取也；蹈義而履仁，非以邇譽也；飭躬而勵行，非以遠詆也。以獨行爲義，則毀譽是非無私計焉；以致身爲義，則死生利害無苟避焉；以鞠躬爲義，則成敗利鈍無逆覩焉。董子曰：「正其誼不謀其利，明其道不計其功。」辨莫辨於
translation_en: …Yet what is recorded of Zizhang 子張 says that he "studied with a view to official emolument," and Confucius 孔子 admonished Zixia 子夏 against being a "petty scholar." Now, learning and seeking emolument are different endeavors; the Confucian scholar and the petty man are different designations. That Shi 師 [Zizhang] and Shang 商 [Zixia] could not distinguish between them—was it not because an imposing demeanor is precisely the fault of one with lofty talent and expansive ambition, and taking delight in worldly splendor is something that even one who devoutly believes in the Sage cannot avoid? When they recited the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu), discoursed on benevolence and righteousness, and daily took the Sage as their touchstone, did they not say, "I am acting for righteousness"? Yet the moment their minds acted with an ulterior motive, they fell into self-interest without realizing it themselves. How exceedingly difficult it is to distinguish between righteousness and profit! Only when one can distinguish between them can one enter the Way. How ought one to distinguish them? I have heard it said: "To act and do what is fitting is called righteousness." Since righteousness is defined as what is fitting, then in whatever one does, it is all what principle requires one to do, and not something done for an ulterior motive. Therefore, eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty are fitting; one does not eat and drink for the sake of others. Wearing furs in the cold and fine kudzu-cloth in the heat are fitting; one does not wear furs and kudzu-cloth for the sake of others. Now, learning should also be like this. Having broad learning and a strong memory is not for the purpose of awaiting questions; cherishing loyalty and keeping trustworthiness is not for the purpose of awaiting recommendation; accumulating learning and striving in practice is not for the purpose of awaiting selection; treading the path of righteousness and practicing benevolence is not for the purpose of drawing near to praise; disciplining oneself and encouraging good conduct is not for the purpose of keeping slander at a distance. If one takes independent conduct as righteousness, then there is no selfish calculation of praise and blame, right and wrong; if one takes devoting one's life as righteousness, then there is no ignoble evasion of life and death, advantage and harm; if one takes bending one's body in service unto death as righteousness, then there is no anticipation of success or failure, smooth or rough fortune. Master Dong 董子 [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] said: "Rectify what is righteous and do not scheme for its profit; clarify the Way and do not calculate its merit." No distinction could be clearer than…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
此矣不然者陽慕夫義之名陰濟其利之實内
懷夫利之心外假其義之迹証父者利在於直
辟兄者利在於廉辭千乘之國者利在於得名
以家量貸民者利在於得衆所爲在此而所欲
則在彼義固不如是也是故齊桓推亡固存似
惠也君子不謂之惠而謂之薄德宋襄不禽不
傷似正也君子不謂之正而謂之已甚忠如楚
令尹清如陳文子似仁也仲尼不許而曰未知
豈非以其所爲者則是其所以爲者則未必是
===
乎以是推之則急功攘善者利也有所爲而折
節退讓者亦利也貪生忍死者利也有所爲而
慷慨殺身者亦利也裂國以爭者利也有所爲
而潔身辭祿者亦利也論而至是則非惟人不
知其爲利雖已亦不自知其爲利者是則所當
辨也聖賢之爲義則不然義在於與賢則禪而
授非利人之德我也義在於愛弟則放而封非
利人之友我也義在於急君則諫而死非利人
之忠我也甚則傳子德衰也而禹爲之滅親非
punctuated: 此矣。不然者，陽慕夫義之名，陰濟其利之實，内懷夫利之心，外假其義之迹。証父者，利在於直；辟兄者，利在於廉；辭千乘之國者，利在於得名；以家量貸民者，利在於得衆。所爲在此，而所欲則在彼，義固不如是也。是故齊桓推亡固存，似惠也，君子不謂之惠，而謂之薄德；宋襄不禽不傷，似正也，君子不謂之正，而謂之已甚；忠如楚令尹，清如陳文子，似仁也，仲尼不許，而曰未知。豈非以其所爲者則是，其所以爲者則未必是乎？以是推之，則急功攘善者，利也；有所爲而折節退讓者，亦利也。貪生忍死者，利也；有所爲而慷慨殺身者，亦利也。裂國以爭者，利也；有所爲而潔身辭祿者，亦利也。論而至是，則非惟人不知其爲利，雖已亦不自知其爲利者，是則所當辨也。聖賢之爲義則不然。義在於與賢，則禪而授，非利人之德我也；義在於愛弟，則放而封，非利人之友我也；義在於急君，則諫而死，非利人之忠我也。甚則傳子，德衰也，而禹爲之；滅親，非…
translation_en: …than this. Otherwise, one outwardly admires the name of righteousness while secretly achieving the reality of profit, inwardly harbors a mind bent on profit while externally borrowing the semblance of righteousness. For the one who bore witness against his father, the profit lay in a reputation for uprightness; for the one who shunned his elder brother, the profit lay in a reputation for integrity; for those who declined a state of a thousand chariots, the profit lay in gaining fame; for those who lent grain to the people using their larger family measure, the profit lay in winning the multitude. What they did was here, yet what they desired was there—righteousness is certainly not like this. Therefore, Duke Huan of Qi overthrowing the perishing and strengthening the surviving seemed benevolent, yet the gentleman did not call it benevolence, calling it instead meager virtue; Duke Xiang of Song refusing to capture the elderly or wound a second time seemed upright, yet the gentleman did not call it uprightness, calling it instead excessive; loyalty like that of the Chief Minister of Chu (Ziwen) and purity like that of Chen Wenzi seemed humane, yet Confucius (Zhongni) did not grant them this, saying instead, "How can I know?" Is this not because while what they did was right, the motive for which they did it was not necessarily right? Reasoning from this, rushing after merit and seizing credit for goodness is for profit; bending one's will to yield and defer with an ulterior motive is also for profit. Clinging to life and enduring ignominy to avoid death is for profit; generously sacrificing one's life with an ulterior motive is also for profit. Tearing a state apart in contention is for profit; keeping oneself pure and declining emoluments with an ulterior motive is also for profit. When the discussion reaches this point, not only do others not realize that it is for profit, even the person himself does not realize that it is for profit—and this is precisely what must be distinguished. The practice of righteousness by the sages and worthies is not so. When righteousness lay in bestowing the throne upon the worthy, they abdicated and handed it over, not for the profit of having others consider them virtuous; when righteousness lay in loving a younger brother, he banished and yet enfeoffed him, not for the profit of having others consider him fraternal; when righteousness lay in urgent devotion to the ruler, they remonstrated and died, not for the profit of having others consider them loyal. Going even further: passing the throne to one's son was talked of as a decline in virtue, yet Yu did it; destroying one's own kin was considered un-…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
友也而周公爲之放伐非忠也而湯武爲之彼
其心惟知如此爲義則如此爲之遑計其於我
有不利焉不利且爲之又遑計其於我爲利焉
故知聖賢之於義皆無所爲而爲者也無爲而
爲此人之真心也一有所爲則僞矣真與僞之
分是即義與利之辨也辨之不早則名曰義而
實利矣適燕者北其轅適越者南其轅南北之
不辨則燕越終不可至也仲尼告子張以寡尤
悔勉子夏以爲君子正欲其辨之也義利之差
===
閒不容髮舜蹠之分良在於此噫可畏也哉雖
然儒者論學旣曰明辨之矣又曰篤行之何耶
蓋坐而談道里者不若疾走者之至也立而言
勝負者不若當奕者之審也世有知義之當爲
或不能擴充以滿其量知利之不當爲或不免
隱忍爲之此則非辨之艱乃行之艱也子張旣
聞言行之訓而問行問達不一而足乃子夏自
謂交戰而勝焉子夏勝子張不勝商之過於師
遠矣嗚呼此集義養氣孟子所以有功於後學
punctuated: 友也，而周公爲之；放伐非忠也，而湯、武爲之。彼其心惟知如此爲義，則如此爲之，遑計其於我有不利焉？不利且爲之，又遑計其於我爲利焉？故知聖賢之於義，皆無所爲而爲者也。無爲而爲，此人之真心也；一有所爲，則僞矣。真與僞之分，是即義與利之辨也。辨之不早，則名曰義而實利矣。適燕者北其轅，適越者南其轅，南北之不辨，則燕、越終不可至也。仲尼告子張以寡尤悔，勉子夏以爲君子，正欲其辨之也。義利之差，閒不容髮，舜、蹠之分，良在於此。噫！可畏也哉！雖然，儒者論學，旣曰「明辨之」矣，又曰「篤行之」，何耶？蓋坐而談道里者，不若疾走者之至也；立而言勝負者，不若當奕者之審也。世有知義之當爲，或不能擴充以滿其量；知利之不當爲，或不免隱忍爲之。此則非辨之艱，乃行之艱也。子張旣聞言行之訓，而問行、問達，不一而足；乃子夏自謂交戰而勝焉。子夏勝，子張不勝，商之過於師遠矣。嗚呼！此集義養氣，孟子所以有功於後學
translation_en: … brotherly affection, yet the Duke of Zhou (周公) did it; banishing and overthrowing a ruler is not loyalty, yet Tang (湯) and Wu (武) did it. In their minds, they knew only that acting thus was righteousness, and so they acted thus—what leisure had they to calculate whether it was disadvantageous to themselves? And if they did it even when it was disadvantageous, what leisure had they to calculate whether it would be profitable to themselves? Therefore, we know that in their relation to righteousness, the sages and worthies all act without any ulterior motive. To act without ulterior motive is a person's true heart; once there is an ulterior motive, it becomes false. The division between true and false is precisely the distinction between righteousness and profit. If one does not distinguish them early on, then what is called righteousness in name will in fact be profit. One who goes to Yan (燕) points his carriage shafts north; one who goes to Yue (越) points his carriage shafts south. If north and south are not distinguished, then Yan and Yue can never be reached. When Zhongni (仲尼, Confucius) instructed Zizhang (子張) on reducing faults and regrets, and urged Zixia (子夏) to be a gentleman (junzi 君子), it was precisely because he wanted them to distinguish this. The divergence between righteousness and profit does not admit a hair's breadth, and the division between Shun (舜) and Robber Zhi (蹠) truly lies in this. Alas! How fearful it is! Even so, when Confucian scholars discuss learning, having already said "distinguish it clearly," why do they also say "practice it earnestly"? It is because sitting and talking about the distance of a road is not as good as running swiftly and arriving there; standing by and speaking of victory and defeat is not as good as the careful judgment of the one actually playing the game of chess. In the world, there are those who know that righteousness ought to be done, yet perhaps cannot expand and fill out its full measure; and those who know that profit ought not to be pursued, yet perhaps cannot avoid secretly bringing themselves to pursue it. This, then, is not the difficulty of distinguishing, but the difficulty of practicing. After Zizhang heard the teaching on words and deeds, he asked about getting one's way (xing 行) and asked about attaining prominence (da 達), not just once; whereas Zixia said of himself that the two battled within him and he was victorious. Zixia was victorious, while Zizhang was not; Shang (商, Zixia) surpassed Shi (師, Zizhang) by far. Alas! In this accumulation of righteousness and nourishing of vital energy (qi 氣), how Mencius (孟子) rendered service to later learners…

同考試官訓導馬　批：〔坐講賜宴，聖朝盛典。子揚以駢麗之辭，發其忠誠之悃，宛然明良氣象，不獨四六之工也。佳士！佳士！〕
考試官教諭官　批：〔氣格嚴整，音韻鏗鏘，頌不忘規，尤見忠愛。〕
考試官學正蘇　批：〔摛詞藻麗，寓意淵微。〕

嘉靖十年某月某日，具官臣某等，恭遇聖駕幸西苑，
translation_en:
… [Mencius's teaching on accumulating righteousness and nourishing vital energy contributed so greatly to later scholars].

Memorial

A Simulated Memorial of Thanks for Bestowing a Banquet after the Completion of the Lectures, When the Imperial Carriage Visited the Western Park (Xiyuan), the Emperor Took His Seat in the Hall of No Ease (Wuyi dian), and Commanded the Hanlin Officials to Sit and Lecture on the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) Chapter of the Book of Documents (Shangshu) and the "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) Ode from the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng) in the Book of Odes (Shi) [Tenth Year of the Jiajing Era, 1531]

By Zhang Jiazheng 張甲徵

In ornate parallel prose, the candidate celebrates this occasion and expresses his sincere loyalty, vividly evoking the spirit of an enlightened ruler and virtuous ministers—not merely excelling in four-and-six syllable composition. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!]

Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Guan 官 comments: [Its tone and structure are dignified and orderly, its cadence is resonant and sonorous, and in offering praise it does not forget admonition—especially revealing loyal affection.]

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
御無逸殿
命臣等坐講尚書無逸篇詩豳風七月之章講
畢
賜宴臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首稱
謝者伏以
禁苑
天開忻邁泰交之
景運
講帷
===
日近祇承晉接之
殊榮敷陳靡效乎沃心拜
賜已深於飽德省循知愧忭舞奚勝竊以義象
乾坤道協於上行下濟舜歌喜起義重夫
元首股肱逮卷阿從遊興思吉士若嘉賓
式燕冀示周行蓼蕭揚豈弟之風湛露播
令儀之雅明良相說鼓宇宙之太和儆戒
無虞登國家於至理垂諸載籍允矣美談
自往哲既湮而前徽斯邈深居高拱羣臣
punctuated:
御無逸殿，命臣等坐講《尚書·無逸篇》、《詩·豳風·七月》之章。講畢，賜宴。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首稱謝者。

伏以：禁苑天開，忻邁泰交之景運；講帷日近，祇承晉接之殊榮。敷陳靡效乎沃心，拜賜已深於飽德。省循知愧，忭舞奚勝！

竊以羲象乾坤，道協於上行下濟；舜歌喜起，義重夫元首股肱。逮《卷阿》從遊，興思吉士；若《嘉賓》式燕，冀示周行。《蓼蕭》揚豈弟之風，《湛露》播令儀之雅。明良相說，鼓宇宙之太和；儆戒無虞，登國家於至理。垂諸載籍，允矣美談。自往哲既湮，而前徽斯邈。深居高拱，羣臣
translation_en:
… took His seat in the Hall of No Ease (Wuyi dian), and commanded Your servants and others to sit and lecture on the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) chapter of the Book of Documents (Shangshu) and the "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) ode from the Airs of Bin (Binfeng) in the Book of Odes (Shi). When the lecture concluded, He bestowed a banquet. Your servants and others, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground again and again to offer our thanks.

We humbly consider: As the Imperial Park opens like Heaven itself, we joyfully encounter a radiant era of harmonious communion between sovereign and ministers; as the lecturing curtain draws daily closer to the Sun, we reverently receive the extraordinary honor of frequent audiences. Though our exposition has failed to enrich Your Majesty's mind, in bowing to receive Your gifts we are already deeply sated with Your virtue. Examining ourselves, we know shame; yet how can we contain our celebratory dancing!

We humbly reflect that when Fuxi [written 羲 as 義] modeled the hexagrams on Heaven and Earth, the Way was harmonized through the descent of the above and the ascent of the below; when Shun sang of joy and vigor, the meaning laid weight upon the head and the limbs of the body politic. Coming down to the attendance on the royal excursion in "Curving Slope" (Juan'e), thoughts were inspired of fine gentlemen; and in the feasting of "Honored Guests" (Jiabin, i.e., the "Lubird" / Luming ode), the hope was to be shown the great highway. "Tall Artemisia" (Liaoxiao) extolled the air of easy-going amicability, and "Heavy Dew" (Zhanlu) broadcast the elegance of fine deportment. When an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers delight in one another, they stir the Great Harmony of the universe; when they maintain vigilance and caution even without cause for anxiety, they raise the state to the utmost order. Handed down in the written records, these are truly admirable tales. Yet since the bygone sages passed away, those former excellences have grown distant. Dwelling deep in seclusion with hands folded on high, the assembled ministers…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
莫得聞聲校獵奉觴一豫豈堪爲度東觀
設横經之席徒託空言南薰和觀稼之詩
終歸綺節欲睹非常之
曠典其惟不世之
昌期茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
毓粹貞元
應時熙洽
備中和以
===
建極默成位育之功
迪仁孝以綏猷永底豐亨之治協氣旁流於
寰寓
憂勤俯徹乎閭閻惟時惟幾方
焦思而
凝命省耕省斂欲觸目以警衷近卽
九閽規恢千畝聿崇
便殿肇創
鴻名屬
punctuated: 莫得聞聲；校獵奉觴，一豫豈堪爲度？東觀設横經之席，徒託空言；南薰和觀稼之詩，終歸綺節。欲睹非常之曠典，其惟不世之昌期。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下：毓粹貞元，應時熙洽。備中和以建極，默成位育之功；迪仁孝以綏猷，永底豐亨之治。協氣旁流於寰寓，憂勤俯徹乎閭閻。惟時惟幾，方焦思而凝命；省耕省斂，欲觸目以警衷。近卽九閽，規恢千畝；聿崇便殿，肇創鴻名。屬
translation_en:
…had no chance to hear the sovereign's voice; or else, offering wine cups during hunting excursions, how could a single pleasure outing serve as a proper standard? Setting out mats for expounding the Classics in the Eastern Lodge was merely consigned to empty words; harmonizing poems on viewing the crops at the Southern Breeze Hall ultimately amounted to nothing more than ornate ceremony. If one wishes to witness an extraordinary and rare grand rite, it can only happen in an unprecedentedly prosperous age.

Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, who nurtures the pure essence of the primal cycle and responds to an era of radiant harmony. Possessing equilibrium and harmony to establish the Supreme Ultimate, You silently accomplish the work of ordering heaven and earth and nourishing all things; practicing benevolence and filial piety to give repose to Your grand plans, You forever achieve a governance of abundance and prosperity. Harmonious vital energy flows out on all sides throughout the realm, while Your anxious diligence penetrates down to the humble alleys and villages. Mindful of the time and the subtle beginnings of things, You rack Your thoughts to consolidate the Heavenly Mandate; inspecting the spring plowing and the autumn harvesting, You wish the sights before Your eyes to admonish Your heart. Near the nine gates of the palace, You have laid out an expansive thousand-mu sacred field; having built up a side palace hall, You initiated for it a grand name. Just at the time when…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬幾多暇之辰正百穀告成之候
鑾輿夙發森羽蓋之星輝
鳳詔傳宣集冠紳而雲從嘉種植標於
華道豈云七聖皆迷奇禾呈瑞於
軒墀快覩三農滿望旁搜風雅欲監成憲以
無愆遐覽典謨將識前言而畜德謂周室
本田功開國而姬公以王道事君無逸一
篇述興衰之軌轍豳風七月詳稼穡之艱
難爰
===
秉菲葑俾登旃廈霽
威嚴乎咫尺優
寵數於尋常
虛以受人遠邁帝王之盛節坐而論道特隆保
傳之上儀考芳猷於簡策之中由今鑑古
探奧旨於傳註之外得意忘言彼宣室之
問鬼神何關民瘼即弘文之披典籍竟侈
詞華方之於
今膛乎其後者也伏念臣等佔畢末學樗櫟
punctuated: 萬幾多暇之辰，正百穀告成之候。鑾輿夙發，森羽蓋之星輝；鳳詔傳宣，集冠紳而雲從。嘉種植標於華道，豈云七聖皆迷；奇禾呈瑞於軒墀，快覩三農滿望。旁搜風雅，欲監成憲以無愆；遐覽典謨，將識前言而畜德。謂周室本田功開國，而姬公以王道事君；《無逸》一篇，述興衰之軌轍；《豳風·七月》，詳稼穡之艱難。爰秉菲葑，俾登旃廈；霽威嚴乎咫尺，優寵數於尋常。虛以受人，遠邁帝王之盛節；坐而論道，特隆保傳之上儀。考芳猷於簡策之中，由今鑑古；探奧旨於傳註之外，得意忘言。彼宣室之問鬼神，何關民瘼；即弘文之披典籍，竟侈詞華。方之於今，膛乎其後者也。伏念臣等佔畢末學，樗櫟
translation_en: …the time of ample leisure amid the myriad affairs of state, just at the season when the hundred grains announce their ripeness. The Imperial Carriage sets forth early in the morning, its feathered canopies arrayed in starry splendor; the Phoenix Edict is proclaimed, gathering the capped and girdled officials who follow like clouds. Fine grain-stalks stand as markers along the magnificent path—how could it be said that the seven sages all lost their way? Wondrous grain-ears present their auspicious signs before the palace steps, a joyful sight fulfilling the hopes of the farmers of the three terrains. Searching broadly through the Airs and Odes, You wish to mirror the established statutes so as not to err; surveying from afar the Canons and Counsels, You seek to remember the words of antiquity and thereby cultivate virtue. Considering that the House of Zhou founded its state upon agricultural merit, and that the Duke of Zhou served his lord through the Kingly Way—how the single chapter "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) recounts the tracks of rise and decline, and how the "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) in the Airs of Bin (Binfeng) details the hardships of sowing and reaping—You have therefore gathered even humble greens, permitting us to ascend the felt-carpeted halls; You have softened Your majesty within a foot's breadth of Your presence, and lavished favors beyond the ordinary. With an open mind You receive others, far surpassing the splendid conduct of former emperors and kings; sitting to discourse on the Way, You especially exalt the supreme ceremony due to Protectors and Tutors. Examining fragrant counsels within the bamboo slips and tablets, You mirror antiquity through the present; probing profound meanings beyond the commentaries and annotations, You grasp the intent and forget the words. That questioning about ghosts and spirits in the Xuan Chamber—what relevance had it to the sufferings of the people? And even the perusal of classical texts in the Hongwen Pavilion ultimately did no more than flaunt literary flourish. Compared with today, they lag hopelessly behind. We humbly reflect that Your servants are mere rote-learners of shallow scholarship, useless timber of ailanthus and oak…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
凡林頌詩讀書恥躬行之弗逮惠疇亮采
怓念慮之徒勤階咨與於
上林怓若登閬苑瀛洲之勝備
咨諭於
經幄遂獲抽玉函金匱之藏榮藉文茵謬陳
燕論胥訓告胥保惠胥教誨忠勤竊愧於
古人日于幷曰皋比曰臒場終始具詳乎
民事雖涓塵無裨
海嶽而
===
撫鞋兼擇芻蕘
玉醴
寵頒宣鹿鳴之雅韻
瓊筵弘啓泛魚藻之
恩波蓋坐講之規久荒於元祐而從官之宴莫
盛乎咸平詎意微臣乃兼
殊遇思仰酬夫
鴻造期殫竭乎微衷非堯舜不陳於前永效靖
共之誼有謀猷則告於
punctuated: 凡林。頌詩讀書，恥躬行之弗逮；惠疇亮采，怓念慮之徒勤。階咨與於上林，怓若登閬苑、瀛洲之勝；備咨諭於經幄，遂獲抽玉函、金匱之藏。榮藉文茵，謬陳燕論。「胥訓告、胥保惠、胥教誨」，忠勤竊愧於古人；「日于幷、曰皋比、曰臒場」，終始具詳乎民事。雖涓塵無裨海嶽，而撫鞋兼擇芻蕘。玉醴寵頒，宣《鹿鳴》之雅韻；瓊筵弘啓，泛《魚藻》之恩波。蓋坐講之規，久荒於元祐；而從官之宴，莫盛乎咸平。詎意微臣，乃兼殊遇！思仰酬夫鴻造，期殫竭乎微衷。非堯、舜不陳於前，永效靖共之誼；有謀猷則告於
translation_en: …ordinary timber. In reciting the Odes and reading the Documents, we are ashamed that our personal conduct falls short; in ordering the categories and assisting in official duties, we fear [?] that our anxious deliberations are merely toil in vain. Advancing to be consulted in the Shanglin Park, we feel as though [?] ascending the scenic realms of Langyuan and Yingzhou; attending to advise and expound at the Classics Mat, we have thus been privileged to draw forth the treasures of the jade caskets and golden coffers. Honored with patterned cushions to sit upon, we have unworthily set forth our commonplace discourses. "Mutually instructing, mutually cherishing, mutually teaching," in loyalty and diligence we privately feel ashamed before the ancients; speaking "of going to gather茅 [?], of climbing the ridges [?], of preparing the vegetable gardens and threshing floors [?]," from beginning to end all is detailed regarding the affairs of the people. Although drops of water and grains of dust add nothing to the seas and sacred peaks, yet in yellow [?] ear-flaps You also select the words of grass- and firewood-gatherers. When the jade-sweet wine is graciously bestowed, the elegant strains of "Lu ming" (The Deer Call) are proclaimed; when the琼 jade-like banquet is grandly opened, the waves of favor of "Yu zao" (The Fish in the Pondweed) overflow. Indeed, the regulation for lecturing while seated had long fallen into disuse since the Yuanyou era (1086–1094), and banquets for attending officials were never more flourishing than in the Xianping era (998–1003). How could Your humble servants have expected to enjoy both of these extraordinary favors! Thinking to look up and repay Your vast creative grace, we hope to exhaust our humble sincerity. Setting forth nothing before You save the ways of Yao and Shun, we shall forever devote ourselves to the duty of quiet and reverent service; having counsels and plans, we shall report them inside to…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
右勉輸弼直之忱伏願
主善爲師
帷敬作所
自朝至昃不遑食兢業克勤
逮天未雨而先憂綢繆必豫則四人迪哲允
符娠旦之箴而
萬壽無疆羣起豳人之祝臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
同考試官教諭劉 批〔我〕
余應秦
國家立法稽謀範今垂後
punctuated:
右，勉輸弼直之忱。伏願主善爲師，帷敬作所；自朝至昃不遑食，兢業克勤；逮天未雨而先憂，綢繆必豫。則四人迪哲，允符娠旦之箴；而萬壽無疆，羣起豳人之祝。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
同考試官教諭劉　批〔我〕
余應秦
國家立法稽謀，範今垂後，
translation_en:
… [inform our Sovereign at His] side, striving to offer our sincere devotion in assisting and rectifying. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will take goodness as Your teacher and make reverence Your dwelling place [? 帷 for 惟]; that from morning until past midday You will allow Yourself no leisure to eat, being cautious and diligent; and that before the sky rains You will take forethought and make preparations beforehand. Then the four predecessors who walked in wisdom will truly accord with the admonitions of the Duke of Zhou [? 娠旦 for 姬旦], and all will join in the prayers of the people of Bin for Your boundless longevity. Your servants are overcome with the utmost awe and earnest trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look upon Your Sacred Majesty, and we reverently present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays [Five Questions]
First Question
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Liu: "[Wait for next page context: 'Our']
Yu Yingqin
Dynasty's establishment of laws and deliberation of counsels, setting the standard for the present and bequeathing it to posterity, …"

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
列聖
皇上創始守成子能敷揚明悉而卜木復議定
國是仰賛
廟謨尤見忠藎可爲得人慶矣
考試官教諭官　批
今上纘承
列聖議法脩明此策酌古準今陳說揚烈其留心
國是者乎宜錄以
獻
===
考試官學正蘇　批〔議論精詳識見卓越錄之〕
愚聞屈羣策而揔廟謨者英君之上務也
酌時宜而定國是者哲士之忠謀也執事
以
國家大議策諸生㦲
列聖之鴻猷參
今日之長計此豈可與拘儒道㦲抑語有之
愚者設慮智者擇焉敢藉兹以畢其說昔
河汾王氏曰議其盡天下之心乎堯有衢
punctuated:
列聖、皇上創始守成，子能敷揚明悉。而卜木復議定國是，仰賛廟謨，尤見忠藎，可爲得人慶矣。
考試官教諭官　批：今上纘承列聖，議法脩明。此策酌古準今，陳說揚烈，其留心國是者乎！宜錄以獻。
考試官學正蘇　批〔議論精詳，識見卓越，錄之。〕
愚聞：屈羣策而揔廟謨者，英君之上務也；酌時宜而定國是者，哲士之忠謀也。執事以國家大議策諸生，㦲列聖之鴻猷，參今日之長計，此豈可與拘儒道㦲！抑語有之：「愚者設慮，智者擇焉。」敢藉兹以畢其說。昔河汾王氏曰：「議其盡天下之心乎！堯有衢
translation_en:
…the founding of the dynasty and the preservation of its achievements by the Successive Sacred Emperors and His Majesty the Emperor, you are able to expound upon and illuminate thoroughly. Moreover, at the conclusion [?] you again deliberate upon establishing the fixed policy of the state and look up to assist the counsels of the imperial court, which especially reveals your loyal devotion. We may rejoice at having obtained a capable man!

Examiner and Instructor Guan官 comments: The Reigning Sovereign succeeds the Successive Sacred Emperors, deliberating on the laws and cultivating brightness. This policy essay weighs antiquity and takes the present as its standard, setting forth explanations and extolling glorious achievements. Surely he is one who pays close attention to the fixed policy of the state! It is fitting to record it for presentation to the throne.

Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Su蘇 comments: 〔The argumentation is precise and detailed, and the insight is outstanding. Record it.〕

I, your humble student, have heard that exhausting the wisdom of all counsels to gather together the plans of the imperial court is the supreme task of a heroic ruler; weighing what is appropriate to the times to establish the fixed policy of the state is the loyal counsel of a wise scholar. Your Excellency has posed a policy question to us students concerning the great deliberations of the state, praising [?] the grand plans of the Successive Sacred Emperors and consulting on the long-term strategies of today—how could this be spoken of with narrow-minded Confucians! Yet there is a saying: "The foolish offer their thoughts, and the wise choose from among them." I venture to avail myself of this opportunity to present my argument in full. In former times, Master Wang of Hefen (Wang Tong王通) said: "Does not deliberation exhaust the minds of all under Heaven! Yao had the inquiries of the…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
室之問舜有總章之訪皆議之謂也唐虞
而下則莫盛於我
國家蓋自觀星築臺疇人羣集是以有曆元
之議或溯自至元辛巳或斷自洪武甲子
即聚訟不殊矣惟驗諸七政之交會而不
專定於二統故造曆授時迄於今用之視
崇天麟德不數歲而輒易者相去遠也自
祝融失令蕭儀建言是以有定都之議臺
諫隨聲而傳和公卿避罪而結舌幾於築
===
室無成矣惟持初議而不撓合
兩都以竝建定鼎肇基傳之無極視婁敬立
談而即日駕之關中者尤卓越甚也自東
隄横潰糧餉愆期是以有張秋決河之議
釣奇者擬復海運泥故者不厭陸輓吹竽
其莫辨矣惟任劉大夏而不疑濬賈魯河
之故道五旬竣役百世永賴彼沉璧負薪
而塞瓠子者奚可同日論也自戍卒倡亂
五堡再變是以有撫處大同之議恇懦者
punctuated: 室之問，舜有總章之訪，皆議之謂也。唐虞而下，則莫盛於我國家。蓋自觀星築臺，疇人羣集，是以有曆元之議。或溯自至元辛巳，或斷自洪武甲子，即聚訟不殊矣。惟驗諸七政之交會，而不專定於二統，故造曆授時，迄於今用之，視崇天、麟德不數歲而輒易者，相去遠也。自祝融失令，蕭儀建言，是以有定都之議。臺諫隨聲而傳和，公卿避罪而結舌，幾於築室無成矣。惟持初議而不撓，合兩都以竝建，定鼎肇基，傳之無極，視婁敬立談而即日駕之關中者，尤卓越甚也。自東隄横潰，糧餉愆期，是以有張秋決河之議。釣奇者擬復海運，泥故者不厭陸輓，吹竽其莫辨矣。惟任劉大夏而不疑，濬賈魯河之故道，五旬竣役，百世永賴，彼沉璧負薪而塞瓠子者，奚可同日論也。自戍卒倡亂，五堡再變，是以有撫處大同之議。恇懦者
translation_en: …Chamber of the Thoroughfare, and Shun had his consultations at the Hall of Total Regulation; both of these refer to deliberation. From the time of Tang and Yu downward, nothing has surpassed the flourishing state of our Dynasty. Indeed, ever since the astronomical observatory was built and calendar specialists gathered in crowds, there was the deliberation over the calendar epoch. Some traced it back to the xinsi year of the Zhiyuan era [1281], while others reckoned it from the jiazi year of the Hongwu era [1384]—it was no different from a contentious court case. Only by verifying it against the conjunctions of the Seven Regulators and not fixing exclusively upon either of the two systems did we construct the calendar to grant the seasons, which has been used down to the present day. Compared to the Chongtian and Linde calendars, which were repeatedly altered after only a few years, how far apart they are! Ever since the god of fire Zhurong lost control of his seasonal command [i.e., the palace fires occurred] and Xiao Yi 蕭儀 submitted his proposal, there was the deliberation over establishing the capital. The Censors and Remonstrators echoed one another in chorus, while the high ministers held their tongues to avoid blame, so that it nearly became like building a house by the roadside with no success. Only by upholding the initial resolution without wavering and uniting the Two Capitals in dual establishment did we settle the imperial tripods and lay the foundation to be transmitted without end. Compared to Lou Jing 婁敬 persuading the emperor in a standing conversation to drive his chariot into Guanzhong that very day, this was far more preeminent! Ever since the eastern dikes burst wildly and grain transport missed its deadlines, there was the deliberation over the Yellow River breach at Zhangqiu 張秋. Those fishing for novelty proposed restoring sea transport, while those clinging to old ways never tired of overland haulage—it was like indiscriminate pipe-playing where one could not tell who was skilled.
