Only by entrusting Liu Daxia 劉大夏 without doubt to dredge the old channel of the Jia Lu River 賈魯河 was the project completed in fifty days, providing a lasting reliance for a hundred generations. How could those of old who sank jade disks and carried firewood to plug the breach at Huzi 瓠子 be discussed in the same breath? Ever since the garrison soldiers instigated rebellion and the Five Forts mutinied a second time, there was the deliberation over pacifying and managing Datong 大同. The timid…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
養亂於豢虎發憤者快意於禽獮猶治亂
繩而棼之矣惟赦脅從以散逆黨殲渠魁
以明天誅反側既安邊鄙不聳彼詐誘王
弁而董乃勝之者相距奚啻萬里也之數
役者當羣言淆亂事機卒臨之際而
列聖裁以
宸斷動中機宜故創法貽謀若植表而望靡或
忒矣應變戡亂若省括而發罔弗中矣挈
前言而責後效若操券責負罔弗償矣茲
===
非明斷兼資之驗哉顧猶有異焉今之安
南都統非交趾藩司乎定之以張輔撫之
以黃福業已入版圖矣因黎利之叛而畀
之不武也然當天下一統之初則仗義以
弔伐當瘡痍甫息之後則罷兵以安民事
有同形而異時者此類是已今之戎政府
非三大營乎營制之設變而為團營者十
又增而為東西廳者十二夫既復其舊矣
乃以一戎臣統之非制也然昔也統以六
punctuated:
養亂於豢虎，發憤者快意於禽獮，猶治亂繩而棼之矣。惟赦脅從以散逆黨，殲渠魁以明天誅，反側既安，邊鄙不聳，彼詐誘王弁而董乃勝之者，相距奚啻萬里也。之數役者，當羣言淆亂、事機卒臨之際，而列聖裁以宸斷，動中機宜。故創法貽謀，若植表而望，靡或忒矣；應變戡亂，若省括而發，罔弗中矣；挈前言而責後效，若操券責負，罔弗償矣。茲非明斷兼資之驗哉？
顧猶有異焉。今之安南都統，非交趾藩司乎？定之以張輔，撫之以黃福，業已入版圖矣，因黎利之叛而畀之，不武也。然當天下一統之初，則仗義以弔伐；當瘡痍甫息之後，則罷兵以安民。事有同形而異時者，此類是已。今之戎政府，非三大營乎？營制之設，變而為團營者十，又增而為東西廳者十二。夫既復其舊矣，乃以一戎臣統之，非制也。然昔也統以六
translation_en:
…fostered rebellion as if rearing a tiger, while the indignant sought satisfaction in wholesale slaughter like an autumn hunt—it was like trying to untangle a knotted cord only to snarl it further. Only by pardoning those coerced into following so as to disperse the rebel faction, and annihilating the ringleaders to manifest Heaven's punishment, were the wavering reassured and the frontier borders kept free from alarm. Compared to enticing Wang Bian 王弁 by deceit and only barely overcoming him, does this not surpass it by ten thousand miles? In these several campaigns, at moments when diverse opinions were in confused contention and crises suddenly arose, the successive Sacred Emperors decided them through their imperial resolve, hitting the mark at every turn. Thus, in establishing laws and bequeathing plans, it was like erecting a gnomon and gazing at it—nothing ever erred; in responding to emergencies and quelling rebellions, it was like inspecting the arrow's nock before releasing—nothing failed to hit the mark; in holding up prior words and demanding subsequent results, it was like holding a tally to demand repayment of a debt—nothing failed to be made good. Is this not proof of combining clarity of vision with decisiveness?

Yet there are still cases that differ from this. Is not today's Pacification Commission of Annan 安南 the former Provincial Administration Commission of Jiaozhi 交趾? Pacified by Zhang Fu 張輔 and soothed by Huang Fu 黃福, it had already been incorporated into the imperial registers; to hand it over because of the rebellion of Lê Lợi 黎利 seems unmartial. Yet at the beginning of the unification of the realm, one relies on righteousness to console the people and punish the wicked; after the wounds of war have barely healed, one halts troops to give rest to the people. Affairs that share the same form but occur in different times are of this sort. Is not today's Supreme Headquarters of the Capital Training Divisions (Rongzheng fu 戎政府) the former Three Great Training Divisions (San da ying 三大營)? Once the division system was established, it was changed into the ten Integrated Divisions (Tuan ying 團營), and then further expanded into the twelve Divisions of the Eastern and Western Offices (Dong-Xi ting 東西廳). Now that the old system has been restored, to have a single military commander command all of them seems contrary to institutional precedent. Yet in the past, they were commanded by six…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
將軍而兵權分於衆今也統以一勳舊而
副遊叅佐備其員均之不專屬也事有異
名而同實者此類是已今之貢市諸酋非
陸梁黠虜乎一請於史道再請於翁萬達
皆閉關不受矣一旦而許之非計也然昔
之請貢也有要心許之則近於示弱今之
請貢也有順心拒之非所以示仁未可一
槩論也事有同體而異情者此類是已使
徒執而議之曰至是之是無非至非之非
無是也安見創守之同心而
===
先聖
後聖之一揆哉大都事無常形人無常見以一
目視不如以衆目視也以一慮謀不如以
衆慮謀也夫議惡可已矣顧居處異轡則
方隅易位東鄰之西即西鄰之東執方而
指之非矣才情異稟則趣舍異路北人之
不習於舟猶南人之不習於陸執一途而
取之非矣故曰議者義也義者宜也其變
punctuated: 將軍而兵權分於衆；今也統以一勳舊，而副、遊、叅、佐備其員，均之不專屬也。事有異名而同實者，此類是已。今之貢市諸酋，非陸梁黠虜乎？一請於史道，再請於翁萬達，皆閉關不受矣；一旦而許之，非計也。然昔之請貢也有要心，許之則近於示弱；今之請貢也有順心，拒之非所以示仁，未可一槩論也。事有同體而異情者，此類是已。使徒執而議之，曰「至是之是無非，至非之非無是也」，安見創守之同心，而先聖後聖之一揆哉？大都事無常形，人無常見，以一目視不如以衆目視也，以一慮謀不如以衆慮謀也，夫議惡可已矣？顧居處異轡，則方隅易位，東鄰之西即西鄰之東，執方而指之，非矣；才情異稟，則趣舍異路，北人之不習於舟猶南人之不習於陸，執一途而取之，非矣。故曰：議者，義也；義者，宜也。其變
translation_en:
… generals, so military authority was divided among many; today, they are commanded by a single veteran of merit, while Vice Commanders, Mobile Corps Commanders, Assistant Regional Commanders, and aides fill out the ranks—in either case, authority does not belong exclusively to one person. Matters that have different names but the same reality are of this sort. Are not the various chieftains who today present tribute and trade at the border markets the same unruly and cunning caitiffs of before? They requested it once through Shi Dao (史道) and requested it a second time through Weng Wanda (翁萬達), yet in both cases we closed the passes and refused them; to grant it to them all of a sudden would seem poor policy. Yet in the past, when they requested tribute, they harbored coercive intent, so granting it would have come close to showing weakness; today, when they request tribute, they harbor submissive intent, so rejecting them would not be the way to display benevolence. These cannot be judged by a single uniform standard. Matters that share the same form but differ in underlying circumstances are of this sort. If one merely clings stubbornly to a view and argues, saying, "What is supremely right has no wrong in it, and what is supremely wrong has no right in it," how could one perceive the shared mind of founding and preserving, or the identical principles of the former sages and later sages?

In general, affairs have no fixed form and men have no fixed views. Looking with a single eye is not as good as looking with many eyes; planning with a single mind is not as good as planning with many minds. How, then, could deliberation be dispensed with? Yet when people occupy different vantage points [?], directions shift their relative positions: what is west to the eastern neighbor is east to the western neighbor, so to cling to a fixed direction and point to it as absolute is wrong. When talents and dispositions are differently endowed, inclinations and aversions follow different paths: northerners being unaccustomed to boats is just like southerners being unaccustomed to overland travel, so to cling to a single path and judge by it alone is wrong. Therefore it is said: deliberation (yi) means rightness (yi), and rightness means appropriateness (yi). Its adaptation…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
通隨乎時推移隨乎勢而議者日紛紛焉
是故有目睹其事而議者有身當其事而
議者有攬衆議而議者危坐旃茵指顧而
譚咤畝誠晰然甚辨曾不知操耒耜披簑
薜者之獨苦心也是睹事而議者未易也
對局運譜捲手懸思自謂筭無遺筴曾不
知袖手旁觀者竊笑其當局而迷也是當
事而議者未易也淄澠合陳孰知正味朱
紫眩目孰辨正色是攬衆議而議者未易
===
也蓋嘗觀謀臣策士蒿目而憂當世抵掌
而籌廟堂豈不自謂石畫之見顧意向稍
偏而員機或滯睇審未熟而措置遂乖泥
牽繫之轍者守故常譬則圻旋而步傴僂
而趨可以行邇不可以及遠也狃錙銖之
筭者忘大計譬則程薪而爨數米而炊可
以治小不可以治大也尚操切之法者忽
訏謨譬則攻發之劑烏喙之毒可以療病
不可以養生也彼衆言盈庭方各是其議
punctuated: 通隨乎時，推移隨乎勢，而議者日紛紛焉。是故有目睹其事而議者，有身當其事而議者，有攬衆議而議者。危坐旃茵，指顧而譚咤畝，誠晰然甚辨，曾不知操耒耜、披簑薜者之獨苦心也，是睹事而議者未易也；對局運譜，捲手懸思，自謂筭無遺筴，曾不知袖手旁觀者竊笑其當局而迷也，是當事而議者未易也；淄澠合陳，孰知正味？朱紫眩目，孰辨正色？是攬衆議而議者未易也。蓋嘗觀謀臣策士，蒿目而憂當世，抵掌而籌廟堂，豈不自謂石畫之見？顧意向稍偏而員機或滯，睇審未熟而措置遂乖。泥牽繫之轍者守故常，譬則圻旋而步、傴僂而趨，可以行邇，不可以及遠也；狃錙銖之筭者忘大計，譬則程薪而爨、數米而炊，可以治小，不可以治大也；尚操切之法者忽訏謨，譬則攻發之劑、烏喙之毒，可以療病，不可以養生也。彼衆言盈庭，方各是其議
translation_en:
…adaptation follows the times, and its shifts follow the circumstances, while those who deliberate are daily in a hubbub of disagreement. Therefore, there are those who deliberate upon witnessing a matter with their eyes, those who deliberate while personally handling a matter, and those who deliberate by gathering the deliberations of the multitude. Sitting upright on felt rugs and cushions, pointing around and talking of the fields [? 咤畝, for 畎畝], they are truly clear and most eloquent, yet they know nothing of the solitary, bitter toil of those who grasp the plowshare and wear straw raincoats and wild-vine capes; thus it is not easy to deliberate upon merely witnessing a matter. Facing the game board and applying the manual, rolling up one's sleeves in anxious thought, one claims that one's calculations leave no stratagem overlooked, yet one knows nothing of the bystanders with hands in their sleeves who secretly laugh at how the player in the game is bewildered; thus it is not easy to deliberate while personally handling a matter. When the waters of the Zi and Sheng rivers are set out together, who knows the true flavor? When vermilion and purple dazzle the eyes, who distinguishes the true color? Thus it is not easy to deliberate by gathering the deliberations of the multitude.

Indeed, I have observed counselors and strategists looking out with furrowed brows in worry over the present age, clapping their hands as they plan for the imperial court—how could they not consider their views to be rock-solid plans? Yet if their inclinations are slightly biased, their adaptable mechanism may become obstructed; if their scrutiny is not yet thorough, their arrangements consequently go awry. Those who cling to fettered ruts hold to old routines: this is like walking by turning in a cramped space [? 圻旋, for 折旋] or hastening along with a hunched back—one can go near, but cannot reach afar. Those who are habituated to petty, penny-pinching calculations forget the grand plan: this is like measuring out firewood to light the stove or counting grains of rice to cook—one can manage the small, but cannot manage the great. Those who prize harsh and urgent methods neglect great counsels: this is like a purging draught or the poison of aconite—it can cure an illness, but cannot nourish life. Those multitudinous words fill the court, each party considering its own deliberation right…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
而不肯相下也惟在持議者酌而用之耳
故曰君畫之相守之相畫之而司守之此
之謂也
皇上御宇握乾於今十載日討
祖
宗故實而脩之法令更新萃策畢舉
今天下內寧外威赫然称盛治焉
皇上第垂拱受成而已又安所置議哉執事迺
欲采長議以裨
===
國計則愚何知焉敢掇摭所聞以對蓋昔楚
莊王問國是孫叔敖曰臣恐王之不能定
也是定國是者君之責也唐之興也玄齡
善謀如晦善斷以底貞觀之盛是協謀斷
者相之責也方
今海內恬熙
舊章具在省議論而責成功之時也顧夫法
度之脩廢綱紀之弛張亦豈得晏然無議
哉愚竊謂採議貴廣酌議貴虛定議貴審
punctuated:
而不肯相下也，惟在持議者酌而用之耳。故曰：「君畫之，相守之；相畫之，而司守之。」此之謂也。
皇上御宇握乾，於今十載，日討祖宗故實而脩之，法令更新，萃策畢舉。今天下內寧外威，赫然称盛治焉。皇上第垂拱受成而已，又安所置議哉？執事迺欲采長議以裨國計，則愚何知焉？敢掇摭所聞以對。蓋昔楚莊王問國是，孫叔敖曰：「臣恐王之不能定也。」是定國是者，君之責也。唐之興也，玄齡善謀，如晦善斷，以底貞觀之盛，是協謀斷者，相之責也。方今海內恬熙，舊章具在，省議論而責成功之時也。顧夫法度之脩廢，綱紀之弛張，亦豈得晏然無議哉？愚竊謂採議貴廣，酌議貴虛，定議貴審…
translation_en:
…and refuse to yield to one another. It rests solely with those who preside over the deliberations to weigh them and put them to use. Therefore it is said: "What the ruler plans, the chief minister upholds; what the chief minister plans, the various offices uphold." This is what is meant.

Since His Majesty ascended the throne and grasped the sovereign authority, ten years have now passed. Daily he examines the precedents of the Imperial Ancestors and cultivates them; laws and ordinances have been renewed, and the finest policies have all been enacted. Today the empire is peaceful within and awe-inspiring without, brilliantly acclaimed as an era of flourishing governance. His Majesty need only let his robes hang down and fold his hands to receive the accomplished results—what further room is there for deliberation? Yet Your Excellency wishes to gather sound deliberations to benefit the plans of the state. What does this ignorant student know? Still, I venture to gather up what I have heard in order to reply.

In antiquity, when King Zhuang of Chu 楚莊王 asked about the fundamental policy of the state, Sun Shu'ao 孫叔敖 said: "Your servant fears that Your Majesty will not be able to settle upon it." Thus, to settle the fundamental policy of the state is the responsibility of the ruler. At the rise of the Tang dynasty, Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 excelled at planning and Du Ruhui 杜如晦 excelled at making decisions, thereby achieving the flourishing governance of the Zhenguan 貞觀 reign. Thus, to harmonize planning and decision-making is the responsibility of the chief minister.

Right now, the realm within the seas is tranquil and prosperous, and the old statutes are all in place; it is a time for reducing empty discussions and demanding actual achievements. Yet when it comes to the cultivation or neglect of laws and institutions, and the slackening or tightening of fundamental order, how could one sit back at ease without any deliberation at all? In my humble view, in gathering deliberations one should value breadth; in weighing deliberations one should value an open mind; in settling deliberations one should value thoroughness…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
也語云以繡飾繡以素飾素何以知其美
也善爲國家者集思廣益是非得失咸獲
自效於前故言之而不用也不以爲愧今
聽納未弘人懷疑阻出語稍弗當即譴斥
隨之非所以開忠讜之路也採議廣則言
路開矣兩智相爭一愚者從旁而決之非
以智也以無心也人臣矣謀發慮期於共
濟豈以其言之售與否爲勝負哉今天下
積弊不在於撓法而在於訣法良由過揣
===
揣議者之心而主以先入之見也酌議宜
則厝注當矣歌者不期於繁聲期於中節
斷者不期於利巧期於中繩故治貴宜民
法斷可久惟其審之豫也令一令之施方
在聽睹而旋即窒矣至於捉襟見肘廓草
摧毫而後悔焉所損已多故定議審則事
功成矣雖然此百司職也宰相事也古人
有言權者神聖之所資也獨明者天下之
利器也獨斷者微密之營壘也聖王所以
punctuated: 也。語云：「以繡飾繡，以素飾素，何以知其美也？」善爲國家者，集思廣益，是非得失，咸獲自效於前，故言之而不用也，不以爲愧。今聽納未弘，人懷疑阻，出語稍弗當，即譴斥隨之，非所以開忠讜之路也。採議廣則言路開矣。兩智相爭，一愚者從旁而決之，非以智也，以無心也。人臣矣謀發慮，期於共濟，豈以其言之售與否爲勝負哉？今天下積弊，不在於撓法，而在於訣法，良由過揣揣議者之心，而主以先入之見也。酌議宜則厝注當矣。歌者不期於繁聲，期於中節；斷者不期於利巧，期於中繩。故治貴宜民，法斷可久，惟其審之豫也。令一令之施，方在聽睹，而旋即窒矣，至於捉襟見肘，廓草摧毫，而後悔焉，所損已多。故定議審則事功成矣。雖然，此百司職也，宰相事也。古人有言：「權者，神聖之所資也；獨明者，天下之利器也；獨斷者，微密之營壘也。」聖王所以
translation_en:
… As the saying goes: "If you adorn embroidery with embroidery, or adorn plain silk with plain silk, how can one know their beauty?" Those who are skilled at governing the state gather thoughts and broaden benefits, so that right and wrong, success and failure, all get a chance to present themselves before the throne; thus even if someone speaks and his words are not adopted, he does not consider it a disgrace. Nowadays, the reception of counsel is not yet broad, and people harbor doubts and hesitations. If someone utters a word that is slightly inappropriate, reprimand and dismissal immediately follow—this is not the way to open the path for loyal and forthright speech. When the gathering of deliberations is broad, the avenue of speech is opened.

When two wise men contend with each other, a single foolish man standing on the side can settle their dispute—not because of his wisdom, but because he has no preconceptions. When ministers put forth plans [?] and express their thoughts, they aim at working together for the common good; how could they treat whether their words are accepted or not as a matter of personal victory or defeat? Nowadays, the accumulated abuses in the empire lie not in bending the law, but in stubbornly clinging to [?] the law; this truly stems from overly suspecting the motives of those who deliberate, and being governed by preconceived notions. When the weighing of deliberations is appropriate [?], the implementation of measures will be proper.

A singer does not aim at elaborate notes, but at hitting the rhythm; a carpenter cutting wood does not aim at sharp cleverness, but at hitting the marking-line. Therefore, governance values what is suitable for the people, and laws are determined so as to be enduring—simply because they are examined beforehand. Now [?], when an order is issued, it is barely heard and seen before it is immediately obstructed; by the time one pulls the lapel only to expose the elbow, and drafts and brushes are worn out [?], and only then regrets it, the damage done is already great. Therefore, when the settling of deliberations is careful, achievements in state affairs are brought to completion.

Even so, these are the duties of the hundred officials and the business of the Chief Councilor. The ancients had a saying: "Weighing authority is what the divine sages rely upon; independent insight is the sharpest instrument in the world; independent decision is the most subtle and secure fortress." The means by which the sage kings…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
畢割萬幾者恃有此具耳天下之事紛然
衆矣事宜變通而或關於成憲則有變亂
之嫌事宜振飭而或錮於積習則有掣肘
之慮得失相仍孰任其失利害相半孰當
其害卽如乔交趾定營制許貢市非
宸謨獨斷其孰與成之夫惟
聖主躬聽斷之權弘延攬之量
明示德意洞悉下情毋搖惑於浮言毋長姦於
偏聽庶幾哉衆力競勸羣智效謀而熙雍
之治可長保矣此非草莽之士所敢盡言
也
===
第二問
樊鎔
同考試官訓導馮　批〔善理國者必先定經制主計者〕
者
仰體
皇上愴懷恭成萬曆會計錄事綜意婉子能鏡古籌今而塞流節用尤爲確論是留心於世用
者
考試官教諭官　批〔會計錄足爲萬世經制之書此〕
punctuated:
畢割萬幾者，恃有此具耳。天下之事紛然衆矣：事宜變通，而或關於成憲，則有變亂之嫌；事宜振飭，而或錮於積習，則有掣肘之慮。得失相仍，孰任其失？利害相半，孰當其害？卽如乔交趾、定營制、許貢市，非宸謨獨斷，其孰與成之？夫惟聖主躬聽斷之權，弘延攬之量，明示德意，洞悉下情，毋搖惑於浮言，毋長姦於偏聽，庶幾哉衆力競勸，羣智效謀，而熙雍之治可長保矣。此非草莽之士所敢盡言也。

第二問
樊鎔
同考試官訓導馮　批〔善理國者必先定經制，主計者〕者仰體皇上愴懷，恭成《萬曆會計錄》，事綜意婉。子能鏡古籌今，而塞流節用尤爲確論，是留心於世用者。
考試官教諭官　批〔《會計錄》足爲萬世經制之書，此〕
translation_en:
… thoroughly cut through and decide the myriad affairs of state is simply because he relies upon these instruments. The affairs of the realm are numerous and tangled: when a matter ought to be adapted to changing circumstances, yet happens to touch upon established statutes, there is the suspicion of disorderly alteration; when a matter ought to be invigorated and rectified, yet happens to be fettered by entrenched habits, there is the worry of having one's elbow impeded. When gains and losses follow upon one another, who will take responsibility for the loss? When benefits and harms are equally divided, who will bear the harm? Take, for example, relinquishing [?] Jiaozhi, establishing the military camp system, and permitting tribute and border markets—had it not been for the imperial counsels and independent resolve, who could have brought them to completion? Only when the Sage Ruler personally wields the authority to hear and decide, broadens his capacity to recruit and embrace talent, clearly manifests his virtuous intentions, thoroughly understands the conditions of those below, is not swayed or confused by floating talk, and does not foster treachery through one-sided listening—then, perhaps, the strengths of the multitude will vie in mutual encouragement, the wisdom of the crowd will offer up its plans, and a reign of bright harmony can be long preserved! This is not something a scholar from the rustic wilds dares to speak of exhaustively.

Second Question
Fan Rong 樊鎔
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Feng 馮, comments: 〔Those who excel at ordering a state must first fix its regular institutions. Those in charge of fiscal accounting〕 [?] have reverently embodied His Majesty's compassionate concern and respectfully compiled the Wanli Kuaiji Lu (Accounting Records of the Wanli Reign), comprehensive in its matters and tactful in its intent. You are able to use antiquity as a mirror to plan for the present, and your discussion of stopping up the outflow and economizing on expenditures is an especially sound argument; you are one who pays close attention to practical statecraft.
Examiner, Instructor Guan 官, comments: 〔The Kuaiji Lu is sufficient to serve as a book of regular institutions for ten thousand generations; this…〕

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
策條陳明備而區畫周詳足占經濟宜錄
考試官學正蘇　批　經生而達
國計眞俊傑哉
蓋宋臣蘇軾之言曰爲國有三計有萬世
之計有一時之計有不終月之計夫天地
生財只有此數乃有所謂計萬世無匱焉
者此豈有異謀奇筴鬼輸而神運之哉則
其經制素定也經制二出與入而已其入
也必有以取之取常在下常患不能當其
===
出孔而或爲竭澤之漁其出也必有以耗
之耗常在上常患不能顧其入孔而卒爲
漏卮之渙澤而竭是天下之大殘也卮而
漏是天下之大蠹也夫唯王政必自經制
始經制一定量入爲出時其贏詘而輕重
布之是故三年餘一年之蓄九年餘三年
之蓄三十年餘十年之蓄用者常足而有
餘蓄者常閒而無用卽有水旱之災非常
之變官可自辦而民不擾此之謂萬世之
punctuated:
策條陳明備，而區畫周詳，足占經濟，宜錄。
考試官學正蘇批：經生而達國計，眞俊傑哉！
蓋宋臣蘇軾之言曰：「爲國有三計：有萬世之計，有一時之計，有不終月之計。」夫天地生財，只有此數，乃有所謂計萬世無匱焉者，此豈有異謀奇筴，鬼輸而神運之哉？則其經制素定也。經制二：出與入而已。其入也，必有以取之；取常在下，常患不能當其出孔，而或爲竭澤之漁。其出也，必有以耗之；耗常在上，常患不能顧其入孔，而卒爲漏卮之渙。澤而竭，是天下之大殘也；卮而漏，是天下之大蠹也。夫唯王政必自經制始。經制一定，量入爲出，時其贏詘而輕重布之。是故三年餘一年之蓄，九年餘三年之蓄，三十年餘十年之蓄。用者常足而有餘，蓄者常閒而無用，卽有水旱之災、非常之變，官可自辦而民不擾。此之謂萬世之
translation_en:
…policy essay sets forth its points clearly and thoroughly, and its planning is comprehensive and detailed. It is enough to demonstrate administrative statesmanship, and it ought to be recorded.
Examiner Su, Subprefectural Director of Studies, commented: A student of the Classics who yet grasps the fiscal calculations of the state—truly an outstanding talent!
Now, the words of the Song-dynasty minister Su Shi 蘇軾 state: "In governing a state there are three kinds of plans: there are plans for ten thousand generations, plans for a single era, and plans that do not last out a month." Now, the wealth produced by Heaven and Earth exists only in a fixed amount; that there should nevertheless be what is called a plan whereby ten thousand generations suffer no scarcity—how could this come from some extraordinary scheme or marvelous stratagem, transported by ghosts and moved by spirits? Rather, it is because its regular fiscal system (jingzhi 經制) has long been established. The regular system consists of two things: expenditure and revenue, nothing more. As for its revenue, there must be a means of extracting it; extraction always falls upon those below, and the constant worry is that it cannot match the channels of expenditure, so that at times it becomes like draining the pond to catch the fish. As for its expenditure, there must be a means by which it is consumed; consumption always takes place among those above, and the constant worry is that it fails to take into account the channels of revenue, so that in the end it dissipates like a leaking goblet. For a pond to be drained is a great injury to the Empire; for a goblet to leak is a greatworm of ruin to the Empire. Truly, kingly governance must begin with a regular fiscal system. Once the regular system is fixed, one measures revenue to determine expenditure, timing its surpluses and deficits and distributing outlays heavily or lightly accordingly. Therefore, every three years there is a surplus of one year's reserves; every nine years there is a surplus of three years' reserves; and every thirty years there is a surplus of ten years' reserves. That which is used is always sufficient and has a surplus, while that which is stored always lies idle and does not need to be used. Even if there are disasters of flood or drought, or extraordinary crises, the officials can manage matters on their own without disturbing the people. This is what is meant by [a plan for] ten thousand generations…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
計也其法見於王制而詳於周禮周禮九
賦以斂其入九式以均其出司徒以制其
入太宰以制其出職內以會其入職歲以
會其出有日要有月要有歲會大都不越
出入贏詘之間而調劑之爾漢興人主猶
知此意孝文問每歲錢穀出入幾何其時
宰臣陳平不能舉謬對云有主者不當問
宰相夫王制冢宰周禮太宰則宰相職也
財賄出入然且制之彼陳平何人哉至孝
===
武不勝富侈神仙土木邊費百出大司農
往往告匱由是桑孔之徒起而扼腕言商
賈事矣入之益衆出之益浮不及數年海
內虛耗國家經制安可不先定哉唐元和
間李吉甫首撰元和國計錄上之天子說
者謂其綱羅一時出納之數人主得以居
今知昔劑量經費蓋猶得周禮王制遺意
云其在宋錢穀之數陳晉公蔓趣不進會
財之書丁謂一語輒上之君子謂恕爲正
punctuated: 計也。其法見於《王制》，而詳於《周禮》。《周禮》九賦以斂其入，九式以均其出；司徒以制其入，太宰以制其出；職內以會其入，職歲以會其出。有日要，有月要，有歲會，大都不越出入贏詘之間而調劑之爾。漢興，人主猶知此意。孝文問每歲錢穀出入幾何，其時宰臣陳平不能舉，謬對云：「有主者，不當問宰相。」夫《王制》冢宰、《周禮》太宰，則宰相職也；財賄出入，然且制之，彼陳平何人哉？至孝武不勝富侈，神仙、土木、邊費百出，大司農往往告匱。由是桑、孔之徒起，而扼腕言商賈事矣。入之益衆，出之益浮，不及數年，海內虛耗，國家經制安可不先定哉！唐元和間，李吉甫首撰《元和國計錄》上之天子，說者謂其綱羅一時出納之數，人主得以居今知昔，劑量經費，蓋猶得《周禮》、《王制》遺意云。其在宋，錢穀之數，陳晉公蔓趣不進；會財之書，丁謂一語輒上之。君子謂恕爲正，
translation_en: … plan. Its method appears in the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) and is detailed in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). In the Rites of Zhou, the Nine Imposts (jiufu) are used to collect its revenues, and the Nine Formulas (jiushi) are used to equalize its expenditures; the Minister of Education (Situ) regulates its revenues, and the Grand Councilor (Taizai) regulates its expenditures; the Director of Receipts (Zhinei) audits its revenues, and the Director of Annual Expenditures (Zhisui) audits its expenditures. There are daily summaries, monthly summaries, and annual audits, which on the whole do nothing more than balance the surpluses and deficits between revenues and expenditures. When the Han arose, rulers still understood this principle. Emperor Xiaowen asked how much coin and grain came in and went out each year. At the time, the chief minister Chen Ping 陳平 could not cite the figures, and gave the specious reply: "There are officials in charge of that; you should not ask the Councilor." Now, the Prime Minister (Zhongzai) of the Royal Regulations and the Grand Councilor (Taizai) of the Rites of Zhou correspond to the office of Councilor; yet even they regulated the inflow and outflow of wealth and goods—who was this Chen Ping to say otherwise? By the time of Emperor Xiaowu, unable to restrain his wealth and extravagance, expenses for immortals, construction projects, and frontier campaigns arose by the hundreds, and the Grand Minister of Agriculture (Dasinong) frequently reported depletion. From this, the likes of Sang Hongyang 桑弘羊 and Kong Jin 孔僅 arose, wringing their hands in eagerness to speak of mercantile affairs. The more varied the revenues became, the more profligate the expenditures grew; in less than a few years, the empire within the seas was depleted and exhausted. How could the regular fiscal system of the state not be established first? During the Yuanhe reign of the Tang, Li Jifu 李吉甫 first compiled the Record of State Finances of the Yuanhe Reign (Yuanhe guoji lu) and presented it to the Son of Heaven. Commentators said that by comprehensively gathering the figures for revenues and expenditures of the time, the ruler was able to know the past while dwelling in the present and to adjust and measure regular expenditures, thus still capturing the lingering intent of the Rites of Zhou and the Royal Regulations. In the Song, when repeatedly urged [?] for the figures on coin and grain, Chen Jingong 陳晉公 (Chen Shu 陳恕) refused to present them; whereas with the books of fiscal accounts, at a single word Ding Wei 丁謂 immediately presented them. Gentlemen considered Shu to be upright, …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
謂謂爲侒耍之此不可執一論也貫朽粟
腐侈心之娸公私殫竭儉德之階時方承
平府庫充羨人主一見可欲恐生侈心故
有所躊躇而不敢進乃若財匱而君弗知
民竭而君弗聞於斯時也曰吾爲恕不爲
謂可乎其後林特上祥符會計錄王安石
置熙寧旁通簿使眞宗東封西禪歲無寧
日神宗頭會箕斂民不完居則二子導之
也田況錄於皇祐蔡襄錄於治平蘇轍錄
===
於元祐夫仁宗節儉行之四十年治平元
祐皆稱盛際三子即上錢穀數亦恕比也
大抵君有侈心與之言豐亨是從欲也君
有儉德與之言虧竭是厚終也均一會計
未可同日語者我
朝稽古定賦輕重協中大司農領之以制其
出入二百年來未之有改然至於嘉靖之
季亦既不支矣
皇上留心節縮用始差饒主計者欲攷舊額裁
punctuated: 謂謂爲侒。耍之，此不可執一論也。貫朽粟腐，侈心之娸；公私殫竭，儉德之階。時方承平，府庫充羨，人主一見可欲，恐生侈心，故有所躊躇而不敢進。乃若財匱而君弗知，民竭而君弗聞，於斯時也，曰「吾爲恕，不爲謂」，可乎？其後林特上《祥符會計錄》，王安石置《熙寧旁通簿》，使眞宗東封西禪，歲無寧日，神宗頭會箕斂，民不完居，則二子導之也。田況錄於皇祐，蔡襄錄於治平，蘇轍錄於元祐。夫仁宗節儉，行之四十年，治平、元祐皆稱盛際，三子即上錢穀數，亦恕比也。大抵君有侈心，與之言豐亨，是從欲也；君有儉德，與之言虧竭，是厚終也。均一會計，未可同日語者。我朝稽古定賦，輕重協中，大司農領之以制其出入，二百年來未之有改。然至於嘉靖之季，亦既不支矣。皇上留心節縮，用始差饒。主計者欲攷舊額，裁
translation_en:
…and considered [Ding] Wei to be a sycophant [? 侒 for 佞]. In short [? 耍之 for 要之], this cannot be judged by a single rigid standard. When strings of cash rot and grain decays in the granaries, it serves as the matchmaker [? 娸 for 媒] of an extravagant heart; when public and private resources are exhausted, it becomes the stepping-stone to the virtue of frugality. When the times were peaceful and the treasuries were overflowing, if the ruler caught sight of things to covet, there was reason to fear an extravagant heart might arise; therefore [Chen Shu] hesitated and dared not present the figures. Yet suppose resources are depleted and the ruler does not know it, or the people are exhausted and the ruler does not hear of it—at such a time, would it be acceptable to say, "I shall act like [Chen] Shu and not like [Ding] Wei"?

Later, Lin Te 林特 presented the Accounting Record of the Xiangfu Era (Xiangfu kuaiji lu 祥符會計錄), and Wang Anshi 王安石 established the Comprehensive Ledger of the Xining Era (Xining pangtong bu 熙寧旁通簿). That Emperor Zhenzong 眞宗 performed the Feng sacrifices in the east and the Shan sacrifices in the west without a peaceful day all year, and that Emperor Shenzong 神宗 levied capitation taxes and gathered grain by the basketful until the people could no longer live in security—it was these two men who led them into it. Tian Kuang 田況 compiled his record in the Huangyou 皇祐 era, Cai Xiang 蔡襄 in the Zhiping 治平 era, and Su Zhe 蘇轍 in the Yuanyou 元祐 era. Now, Emperor Renzong 仁宗 practiced frugality for forty years, and both the Zhiping and Yuanyou eras were acclaimed as flourishing periods; even though those three men presented the figures of money and grain, they too are comparable to [Chen] Shu. In general, when a ruler has an extravagant heart, to speak to him of abundance and prosperity is to indulge his desires; when a ruler possesses the virtue of frugality, to speak to him of deficits and exhaustion is to help him bring things to a generous conclusion. Though the act of accounting is the same, the cases cannot be spoken of in the same breath.

Our Dynasty examined antiquity to fix the revenue quotas, achieving a balanced mean between light and heavy; the Minister of Revenue (da sinong 大司農) oversees them in order to regulate income and expenditure, and for two hundred years this has remained unchanged. Yet by the close of the Jiajing 嘉靖 reign, finances could no longer be sustained. Since Your Majesty has turned his attention to retrenchment, state resources have begun to become somewhat more ample. Those in charge of fiscal administration, wishing to examine the old quotas and curtail…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
積纍垂之永久毋以不得專書爲恨乃上
法周禮王制之遺下採唐宋諸臣之議纂
爲萬曆會計錄以
上今其書具在誠一按籍而財用源委有無
多寡之要可從舉矣雖然操奇贏而筭秋
毫者細人之謀也會簿書而考出入者計
臣之職也節出入之故審豐儉之宜以垂
久大之利者則
人主之事也今計錄所載歲入可一千四百六
===
十一萬有奇錢鈔不與焉歲出需之
內府者六百餘萬而以供祿俸糧芻商價邊
餉諸費踰九百三十一萬是一歲之入常
不能當一歲之出也歲稔時康且憂不繼
卒然有警何以應之公私詘乏乃爲一切
權宜補濟計非長筴也執事故以令天下
財源猶有可開其流或有當塞爲問蓋嘗
即是書攷之曰省郡田賦所繇出也大司
農歲按簿而責治粟使者治粟使者按簿
punctuated: 積纍，垂之永久，毋以不得專書爲恨。乃上法《周禮》、《王制》之遺，下採唐、宋諸臣之議，纂爲《萬曆會計錄》以上。今其書具在，誠一按籍，而財用源委、有無多寡之要可從舉矣。雖然，操奇贏而筭秋毫者，細人之謀也；會簿書而考出入者，計臣之職也；節出入之故，審豐儉之宜，以垂久大之利者，則人主之事也。今計錄所載，歲入可一千四百六十一萬有奇，錢鈔不與焉；歲出需之內府者六百餘萬，而以供祿俸、糧芻、商價、邊餉諸費，踰九百三十一萬。是一歲之入，常不能當一歲之出也。歲稔時康，且憂不繼，卒然有警，何以應之？公私詘乏，乃爲一切權宜補濟計，非長筴也。執事故以「令天下財源猶有可開，其流或有當塞」爲問。蓋嘗即是書攷之：曰省郡，田賦所繇出也，大司農歲按簿而責治粟使者，治粟使者按簿
translation_en: … accumulated abuses and pass down a standard in perpetuity, so that there would be no regret over lacking a dedicated treatise. Accordingly, modeling above on the legacy of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) and the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi), and below adopting the discussions of various ministers of the Tang and Song dynasties, they compiled the Accounting Record of the Wanli Era (Wanli kuaiji lu) and presented it to the throne. Now that the book exists in full, if one truly examines its registers, the essentials regarding the origins and courses of fiscal resources, their presence or absence, and their abundance or scarcity can all be grasped therefrom. Even so, grasping after surplus profits and calculating down to the finest autumn hair is the scheming of petty men; compiling account books and auditing revenues and expenditures is the duty of fiscal ministers; whereas regulating the causes of revenue and expenditure and judging the appropriateness of abundance and frugality so as to hand down enduring and great benefits—that is the business of the sovereign. According to what is recorded in the accounting record today, annual revenue is roughly 14,610,000 and more, not counting copper cash and paper notes. Of annual expenditure, what is required by the Inner Treasury exceeds 6,000,000, while what goes to supply official salaries and stipends, grain and fodder, merchant payments, frontier military rations, and other expenses exceeds 9,310,000. Thus the revenue of a single year regularly fails to match a single year's expenditure. Even in years of abundant harvests and times of peace, one worries that resources cannot be sustained; if there were suddenly an emergency, how could we respond to it? When public and private resources are exhausted, resorting to all manner of expedient measures to patch things up is no long-term policy. Therefore Your Excellency has posed the question of whether throughout the empire there are still sources of wealth that can be opened, or outflows that ought to bestemmed. I have tried examining the matter on the basis of this book: First, the provinces and prefectures, whence the land tax is derived. Each year the Minister of Revenue (da sinong) inspects the registers and holds the grain-tax commissioners accountable; the grain-tax commissioners inspect the registers …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
而責州邑吏徵輸追促逋負少矣曰漕運
漕河之臣經營督察歲轉輸四百萬石無
或損矣曰屯田比大戮民田稍稍併戮之
即舊額未卒復而伏田稍出可次第理矣
曰鹽法諸歲課輸太倉輸邊鎮凡百三十
萬有奇利故鉅矣曰錢法自京師達藩省
率官爲鼓鑄佐幣行矣曰鈔關歲遣司農
若司空之屬臨督之諸所徵商船貨賄闗
亦少密矣曰雜課舟車有箕鐵冶有征間
架有稅酒酤有榷民間所需尺寸以上靡
不登課額矣曰積穀中外贖鍰一以佐儲
備賑而又屬其令責有司取盈矣執事試
籌
===
今日於漢唐以來所謂財賦一有未備乎太
史公傳貨殖善者因之其次利之其次整
齊之下者與之爭今天下財源已盡開矣
因而利之則可整齊之則可而復求所以
開之是爭民之政也即桑孔且羞稱之矣
punctuated: 而責州邑吏，徵輸追促，逋負少矣。曰漕運：漕河之臣經營督察，歲轉輸四百萬石，無或損矣。曰屯田：比大戮民田，稍稍併戮之，即舊額未卒復，而伏田稍出，可次第理矣。曰鹽法：諸歲課輸太倉、輸邊鎮，凡百三十萬有奇，利故鉅矣。曰錢法：自京師達藩省，率官爲鼓鑄，佐幣行矣。曰鈔關：歲遣司農若司空之屬臨督之，諸所徵商船貨賄，闗亦少密矣。曰雜課：舟車有箕，鐵冶有征，間架有稅，酒酤有榷，民間所需尺寸以上，靡不登課額矣。曰積穀：中外贖鍰，一以佐儲備賑，而又屬其令，責有司取盈矣。執事試籌今日，於漢、唐以來所謂財賦，一有未備乎？太史公傳《貨殖》：「善者因之，其次利之，其次整齊之，下者與之爭。」今天下財源已盡開矣，因而利之則可，整齊之則可；而復求所以開之，是爭民之政也，即桑、孔且羞稱之矣。
translation_en: …and hold the subprefectural and county officials accountable, collecting, delivering, pressing, and urging, so that tax arrears have become few. Next is grain transport: the officials of the Grand Canal and Yellow River manage and supervise it, annually transporting four million piculs without any loss. Next is military state farms: recently, when there was a grand verification [? 戮, graphic error for 覈] of civilian lands, they gradually verified the military lands along with them; even if the old quotas have not been completely restored all at once, hidden lands have gradually come to light and can be put in order step by step. Next is the salt administration: the various annual salt revenues delivered to the Taicang Treasury and to the frontier commands total more than one million three hundred thousand, so the profit is already immense. Next is the coinage system: from the capital out to the provinces, officials generally carry out minting to assist the circulation of currency. Next is the customs barriers: each year subordinates of the Minister of Revenue or the Minister of Works are dispatched to oversee them in person, and as for the various levies on merchant vessels and goods, the barriers have become quite tight. Next is miscellaneous levies: boats and carts are assessed [? 箕, graphic error for 算], iron smelters are levied, house bays are taxed, and wine sales are monopolized; of everything required among the people, from a foot or an inch on up, there is nothing that is not entered into the tax quotas. Next is grain storage: redemption fines in the capital and the provinces are uniformly used to aid reserves and prepare for famine relief, and furthermore the ordinances have been made strict, holding the authorities responsible for filling the quotas to the full. If Your Excellency were to reckon up today's situation, among all that have been called sources of fiscal revenue since the Han and Tang dynasties, is there a single one not yet instituted? The Grand Historian, in his "Biographies of Usurers and Merchants" (Huozhi), wrote: "The best course is to follow along with them; the next is to guide them by means of profit; the next is to regulate them; and the worst is to compete with them." Today the sources of wealth in the empire have already been completely opened. To follow along with them and guide them by profit is permissible, and to regulate them is permissible; but to seek still further ways to open them up is a policy of competing with the people—something that even Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin would be ashamed to speak of.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
毋已則塞其流焉爾今所爲耗財者不出
是書所裁邊鎮也宗藩也營衛也光祿也
監庫也夫邊餉至今日極巳歲可三百五
十餘萬餽餉稍後輙執券索負謂宜加練
主兵少調客兵夫調兵一而當主兵之費
十練多則調省而食減此一議也
宗藩歲祿可九百萬盡天下不足以供而又
日益夫有益祿而無增田將安取給哉謂
宜稍限封爵而聽其從四民之利此又一
===
議也金吾世官冗不可詰而軍校廚匠又
數倍焉歲所糜漕糧二百餘萬太倉銀幣
不下六七十萬盍嚴而汰之乎光祿自近
年節省以來稍稍報羨邇來費出時溢額
外又庖役數幾三千豈盡司膳者餼亦太
糜矣盍稽而裁之乎至其大者則在監庫
司會不會度支不制闌出入莫可問今宜
使
宮府合爲一體盈虛豐儉大臣得與知如周
punctuated: 毋已，則塞其流焉爾。今所爲耗財者，不出是書所裁：邊鎮也、宗藩也、營衛也、光祿也、監庫也。夫邊餉至今日極巳，歲可三百五十餘萬，餽餉稍後，輙執券索負。謂宜加練主兵，少調客兵。夫調兵一而當主兵之費十，練多則調省而食減，此一議也。宗藩歲祿可九百萬，盡天下不足以供，而又日益。夫有益祿而無增田，將安取給哉？謂宜稍限封爵，而聽其從四民之利，此又一議也。金吾世官冗不可詰，而軍校、廚匠又數倍焉，歲所糜漕糧二百餘萬，太倉銀幣不下六七十萬，盍嚴而汰之乎？光祿自近年節省以來，稍稍報羨，邇來費出時溢額外，又庖役數幾三千，豈盡司膳者？餼亦太糜矣，盍稽而裁之乎？至其大者，則在監庫。司會不會，度支不制，闌出入莫可問。今宜使宮府合爲一體，盈虛豐儉，大臣得與知，如《周…
translation_en:
If it cannot be avoided, then we must simply staunch the outflow. Today, the things that drain our wealth do not go beyond what is set forth [?] in this book: the frontier commands, the imperial clansmen, the capital training divisions and guards, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the eunuch directorates and treasuries. Indeed, frontier military rations have reached an extreme today, amounting to over 3,500,000 a year; if the delivery of provisions is slightly delayed, the soldiers immediately clutch their tallies and demand what is owed. I would say that we ought to step up the training of local garrison troops and reduce the mobilization of guest troops. Mobilizing one guest soldier costs as much as ten local soldiers; if we train more local troops, mobilizations will be saved and food consumption reduced. This is one proposal.

The annual stipends of the imperial clansmen amount to roughly 9,000,000; the resources of the entire empire are insufficient to supply them, and yet their numbers grow day by day. When stipends increase without any increase in land, from where shall the supplies be drawn? I would say that we ought to somewhat restrict the enfeoffment of noble titles and permit clansmen to pursue the livelihoods of the four classes of commoners. This is another proposal.

The hereditary officers of the Imperial Bodyguard are so superfluous as to be beyond reckoning, and the soldiers, subalterns, cooks, and artisans are several times as numerous again. Every year they waste over 2,000,000 piculs of tribute grain and no less than 600,000 to 700,000 taels of silver and silks from the Ministry of Revenue’s Great Granary Treasury. Why not strictly weed them out? Since the Court of Imperial Entertainments instituted economies in recent years, it has gradually reported surpluses, yet lately its expenditures have at times exceeded the quota. Moreover, its kitchen attendants number nearly three thousand—how could all of them actually be tending to the imperial meals? Their rations are also an excessive waste; why not audit and curtail them?

As for the greatest drain of all, it lies in the eunuch directorates and palace treasuries. The accountants do not audit them, the revenue bureau does not regulate them, and no one dares question their unauthorized receipts and disbursements. We ought now to cause the Palace and the Court to be joined as a single body, so that the high ministers are permitted to be privy to their surpluses and deficits, their abundance and frugality, just as in the Rites of Zhou (Zhou…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
禮太宰掌王之玉府則玩好賜予之間
上敬憚而慎於濫下畏忌而杜於侵又何憂耗
蠹哉然此皆末議也竭九州之力以奉人
主君心豐約財用盈縮關焉
皇上天縱睿聖慎乃儉德
御書十二事以自儆而歸重於撙節用一言此
臣民所共頌也比乃頻下所司取溢常額
朴素之風漸不逮初誠願按籍而稽量入
爲出省不急之費惜不時之賞又於前所
===
謂耗財數者日講求而裁省之撙節抑損
自毫釐以上莫不有益行之既久積之自
裕蓄有九年計在萬世則是錄也雖謂周
禮盡在是可矣不然者入之已多猶不勝
其出出之既浮將復盈其入是錄雖存秪
陳牘耳即日程其錙銖奚裨焉
第三問
馬崇化
同考試官教諭吳　批　〔經律一道儒者均不可廢作者〕
punctuated:
禮》太宰掌王之玉府，則玩好賜予之間，上敬憚而慎於濫，下畏忌而杜於侵，又何憂耗蠹哉？然此皆末議也。竭九州之力以奉人主，君心豐約，財用盈縮關焉。皇上天縱睿聖，慎乃儉德，御書十二事以自儆，而歸重於「撙節用」一言，此臣民所共頌也。比乃頻下所司，取溢常額，朴素之風，漸不逮初。誠願按籍而稽，量入爲出，省不急之費，惜不時之賞，又於前所謂耗財數者，日講求而裁省之，撙節抑損，自毫釐以上莫不有益。行之既久，積之自裕，蓄有九年，計在萬世，則是錄也，雖謂《周禮》盡在是可矣。不然者，入之已多，猶不勝其出；出之既浮，將復盈其入。是錄雖存，秪陳牘耳，即日程其錙銖，奚裨焉？

第三問
馬崇化
同考試官教諭吳　批　〔經律一道，儒者均不可廢。作者〕
translation_en:
… the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), where the Grand宰 [Minister of State, Taizai] had charge of the king’s Jade Treasury, then in matters of curiosities and bestowals, the sovereign above will be reverently cautious and guard against extravagance, while subordinates below will stand in awe and refrain from embezzlement; what worry would there be over waste and rot? Yet all of these are merely secondary proposals. When the strength of the Nine Provinces is exhausted to serve the sovereign, the abundance or scarcity of financial resources hinges upon the extravagance or frugality of the ruler’s mind. His Majesty, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, is careful in his frugal virtue; he wrote out twelve maxims in his own imperial hand to admonish himself, placing ultimate emphasis on the single phrase "restrain and economize expenditures"—this is what officials and the common people all praise together. Lately, however, orders have frequently been sent down to the competent authorities to requisition amounts exceeding the regular quotas, and the custom of plainness and simplicity gradually falls short of how it was at the beginning. I truly wish that Your Majesty would examine the registers and verify them, regulate expenditures according to revenues, curtail non-urgent expenses, begrudge irregular rewards, and, regarding those several matters of financial depletion mentioned above, daily investigate and reduce them. Through restraint and curtailment, from the smallest fraction upward there will be nothing that is not beneficial. When practiced for a long time, accumulations will naturally become abundant; with reserves sufficient for nine years and plans laid for ten thousand generations, then of this compilation one might well say that the entirety of the Rites of Zhou is contained herein. Otherwise, even if revenues are already large, they still will not keep pace with expenditures; and once expenditures exceed bounds, one will seek to swell revenues yet again. Even though this compilation survives, it will be nothing more than a stale document—even if one were to weigh its ounces and grains every day, of what benefit would it be?

Question Three
Ma Chonghua
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Wu: [The Classics and the Penal Code are a single Way, neither of which Confucian scholars can afford to neglect. The author…]

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
多綴泛辭罔知實用獨此篇條對博洽議論明剴足裨
聖天子明刑之治矣允宜高薦
考試官教諭官　批
善達教人習律之旨而深醇淵
考試官學正蘇　批
明經學而通法家可為世用矣
世之譚者類曰儒以聖人為師不以吏為
師聞折衷於六經爾未聞折衷於法家而
號儒也嗟嗟為此說者是局井蛙之見而
未闚滄海爲夏蟲之識而冬冰之未睹耳
思此以發之予其通儒乎
===
道與法非二事也經與律無二道也學者
縈神乎術執之場秩秘於篇章之圖明先
聖之道而不習當世之故則誦說雖勤祇
供口耳藻績雖飾罔裨世務惡在其為有
用之學與是惟鎔鑄六經游習法律不詡
竊言而闇洽理不抱空文而執實用儒斯
其至哉愚生占執一經未習當世固局曲
佔畢流耳執事遽與之譚法律豈欲其爲
通儒耶敢不抒慺慺以對蓋自司馬氏敘
punctuated:
多綴泛辭，罔知實用；獨此篇條對博洽，議論明剴，足裨聖天子明刑之治矣，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭官　批：善達教人習律之旨，而深醇淵。
考試官學正蘇　批：明經學而通法家，可為世用矣。
世之譚者類曰：「儒以聖人為師，不以吏為師；聞折衷於六經爾，未聞折衷於法家而號儒也。」嗟嗟！為此說者，是局井蛙之見，而未闚滄海；爲夏蟲之識，而冬冰之未睹耳。思此以發之，予其通儒乎！道與法非二事也，經與律無二道也。學者縈神乎術執之場，秩秘於篇章之圖，明先聖之道，而不習當世之故，則誦說雖勤，祇供口耳；藻績雖飾，罔裨世務，惡在其為有用之學與？是惟鎔鑄六經，游習法律，不詡竊言而闇洽理，不抱空文而執實用，儒斯其至哉！愚生占執一經，未習當世，固局曲佔畢流耳。執事遽與之譚法律，豈欲其爲通儒耶？敢不抒慺慺以對。蓋自司馬氏敘
translation_en:
…mostly string together vague phrases without knowing practical utility; only this essay gives broad and well-informed itemized responses and clear, incisive arguments, sufficient to benefit the Sacred Son of Heaven's governance of clarifying punishments. It truly deserves a high recommendation.

Examiner, County Director of Studies Guan, comments: It skillfully conveys the intent of teaching men to study the statutes, and is profound, pure, and deep [?].

Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Su, comments: Understanding classical learning and well-versed in the Legalists, he can be of use to the world.

Those in the world who discuss such matters generally say: "Confucian scholars take the sages as their teachers, not clerks as their teachers; one hears of taking the Six Classics as the standard of judgment, not of taking the Legalists as the standard of judgment and calling oneself a Confucian." Alas! Those who make this argument are confined to the view of a frog in a well and have never glimpsed the vast sea; theirs is the knowledge of a summer insect that has never seen winter ice. Reflecting on this to expound upon the question, might I be a comprehensive Confucian scholar!

The Way and the law are not two separate matters; the Classics and the statutes do not have two separate Ways. If scholars entangle their spirits in the arena of scholarly arts and pursuits [?], and arrange secrets within the charts of chapters and sections, understanding the Way of the former sages while remaining unversed in the affairs of the present age, then although their recitation and exposition are diligent, they merely serve the mouth and ear; although their literary embellishments are ornate, they are of no benefit to worldly affairs. Wherein, then, lies the usefulness of their learning? Only by smelting and casting the Six Classics while familiarizing oneself with and practicing the laws and statutes, not boasting of pilfered words while remaining ignorant of the principles of governance [?], and not clinging to empty texts while holding fast to practical utility—in this does a Confucian reach the highest perfection!

Your foolish student specializes in a single Classic and is unversed in the affairs of the present age, truly no more than the sort of narrow, pedantic drone who merely pores over tablets. Yet Your Excellency suddenly discusses laws and statutes with us—could it be that you wish us to become comprehensive Confucian scholars? How dare I not pour forth my earnest thoughts in reply? Ever since Sima [Tan] categorized…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
六家班氏因之列九流而儒法之角立也
不能相一董子條策於建元則欲尊孔氏
而絀雜學勿使竝進路溫舒建言於地節
則欲貴文學而賤獄吏以興太平或謂儒
與法不可溷而爲伍也自徒法者言耳若
仲舒溫舒之論則均切救世豈謂法家爲
可廢耶柰之何拘學不與論廣淺見不以
指遠師授遺經見偶窺豹輒自命曰儒而
以吏相詬病是徒知法律不伉於詩書未
===
知經術之通於世務也蓋六經帝王垂訓
之書法律帝王馭世之具經以道勝法之
體立律以法勝經之用行禮禁未然之前
法施已然之後曾有一之相詩哉今觀周
禮一書非周公致太平之具耶乃於刑法
詳焉是故三典以刑邦國而新國輕典平
國中典亂國重典非斟酌其施與三訊以
定服刑而或於羣臣或於羣吏或於萬民
非考覈其眞與情苟可原則有三赦而夠
punctuated: 六家，班氏因之列九流，而儒、法之角立也，不能相一。董子條策於建元，則欲尊孔氏而絀雜學，勿使竝進；路溫舒建言於地節，則欲貴文學而賤獄吏，以興太平。或謂儒與法不可溷而爲伍也，自徒法者言耳。若仲舒、溫舒之論，則均切救世，豈謂法家爲可廢耶？柰之何拘學不與論廣，淺見不以指遠，師授遺經，見偶窺豹，輒自命曰儒，而以吏相詬病？是徒知法律不伉於《詩》、《書》，未知經術之通於世務也。蓋《六經》，帝王垂訓之書；法律，帝王馭世之具。經以道勝，法之體立；律以法勝，經之用行。禮禁未然之前，法施已然之後，曾有一之相詩哉？今觀《周禮》一書，非周公致太平之具耶？乃於刑法詳焉。是故「三典」以刑邦國，而新國輕典，平國中典，亂國重典，非斟酌其施與？「三訊」以定服刑，而或於羣臣，或於羣吏，或於萬民，非考覈其眞與？情苟可原，則有「三赦」，而夠
translation_en:
…the Six Schools, and Ban [Gu 班固] followed this in arraying the Nine Streams, so that Confucians and Legalists stood in opposition to one another and could not be unified. When Master Dong [Zhongshu 董仲舒] presented his itemized policy essays in the Jianyuan 建元 era (140–135 BCE), he wished to revere Confucius and dismiss miscellaneous learnings, not allowing them to advance together; when Lu Wenshu 路溫舒 submitted his counsel in the Dijie 地節 era (69–66 BCE), he wished to esteem classical scholarship and disparage prison officials in order to bring about Great Peace. Some say that Confucianism and Legalism cannot be mingled and placed in the same ranks, but that is spoken only with reference to those who rely solely on law. As for the arguments of Dong Zhongshu and Lu Wenshu, both were urgently concerned with saving the age; how could they have meant that the Legalists should be abolished? How is it that narrow scholars cannot be engaged in broad discussion, and those of shallow views cannot be pointed toward what is far-reaching? Receiving the bequeathed Classics from their teachers, with a view no wider than catching a glimpse of a leopard's spot, they readily style themselves "Confucians" while reviling administrative officials. This is merely knowing that laws and statutes are no match for the Odes and the Documents, without realizing that classical scholarship is thoroughly applicable to the affairs of the world.

For the Six Classics are the books through which emperors and kings handed down their teachings, while laws and statutes are the instruments by which emperors and kings govern the world. When the Classics prevail through the Way, the substance of the law is established; when the statutes prevail through the law, the function of the Classics is carried out. Ritual prohibits before something happens, while law is applied after it has happened—was there ever a single point on which they contradicted [? 詩, for 悖] one another? Now if we examine the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮), is it not the instrument by which the Duke of Zhou 周公 brought about Great Peace? Yet it is detailed with regard to penal law. Therefore, there are the "Three Codes" to apply punishment to the states and realms—a light code for a newly established state, a medium code for a peaceful state, and a heavy code for a disordered state; is this not deliberating upon how they are applied? There are the "Three Inquiries" to determine the imposition of punishments—inquiring first among the body of high officials, next among the lesser functionaries, and finally among the multitude of the people; is this not verifying the truth of the matter? If the circumstances are excusable, there are the "Three Pardons," whereby the young [? 夠, for 幼]…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
耆耄者愚者得以自全矣法或偶觸則有
三宥而不識者過失者遺忘者得以自免
矣爲之五禁則由宮而官而國而野而軍
無地非法也爲之五戒則自誓而誥而禁
而糾而憲無典非法也爲之五聽則曰辭
曰色曰氣曰耳曰目無舉非法也八刑之
設非不孝不睦不姻不弟不任不恤造言
亂民者乎八辟之設非議親議故議賢議
能議功議貴議勤議賓者乎八成之設非
===
邦汋邦賊邦諜與夫犯邦令橋邦令爲邦
盜邦朋邦誣者乎夫周禮何嘗不言刑又
何嘗言刑而不諄且懇也若虞之五刑則
爲墨爲劓爲剕爲宮爲大辟爾已周之五
刑則糾力糾守糾孝糾職糾暴爾已此吉
之所謂刑也總之上揆天理下揆人情劑
寬猛之中合欽恤之意經以議道畫之則
爲法律以議法裁之則爲道豈經獨名精
法獨名麤若枘鑿不相入哉三代而下法
punctuated: 耆耄者、愚者，得以自全矣；法或偶觸，則有三宥，而不識者、過失者、遺忘者，得以自免矣。爲之五禁，則由宮而官、而國、而野、而軍，無地非法也；爲之五戒，則自誓而誥、而禁、而糾、而憲，無典非法也；爲之五聽，則曰辭、曰色、曰氣、曰耳、曰目，無舉非法也。八刑之設，非不孝、不睦、不姻、不弟、不任、不恤、造言、亂民者乎？八辟之設，非議親、議故、議賢、議能、議功、議貴、議勤、議賓者乎？八成之設，非邦汋、邦賊、邦諜，與夫犯邦令、橋邦令、爲邦盜、邦朋、邦誣者乎？夫《周禮》何嘗不言刑？又何嘗言刑而不諄且懇也？若虞之五刑，則爲墨、爲劓、爲剕、爲宮、爲大辟爾已；周之五刑，則糾力、糾守、糾孝、糾職、糾暴爾已。此吉之所謂刑也。總之，上揆天理，下揆人情，劑寬猛之中，合欽恤之意。經以議道，畫之則爲法；律以議法，裁之則爲道。豈經獨名精、法獨名麤，若枘鑿不相入哉？三代而下，法
translation_en: … the aged and elderly, and the feeble-minded, are able to preserve themselves; and if the law is inadvertently violated, then there are the Three Mitigations, whereby the ignorant, those who err by mistake, and the forgetful are able to be spared. In establishing the Five Prohibitions, extending from the palace to the government offices, the capital, the countryside, and the army, there is no place without law; in establishing the Five Warnings, proceeding from military oaths to proclamations, prohibitions, denunciations, and posted statutes, there is no canon without law; in establishing the Five Modes of Judicial Hearing, namely examining words, facial expression, breathing, hearing, and vision, there is no action without law. As for the institution of the Eight Punishments, are they not for unfilial conduct, discord among kin, disharmony with affines, lack of fraternal respect, untrustworthiness, lack of compassion, fabricating rumors, and inciting the populace? As for the institution of the Eight Deliberations, are they not deliberations on relatives of the ruler, old acquaintances of the ruler, the worthy, the capable, the meritorious, the noble, the diligent, and royal guests? As for the institution of the Eight Adjudications, are they not for spying on state secrets, rebellion against the state, espionage for an enemy state, as well as violating state ordinances, forging [?] state ordinances, committing state banditry, forming state factions, and slandering the state? How did the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) ever fail to speak of punishments, and how did it ever speak of punishments without being earnest and sincere? As for the Five Punishments of Yu, they were merely tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputating the feet, castration, and capital punishment; as for the Five Punishments of Zhou, they merely policed exertion in agriculture, policed adherence to military duty, policed filial piety, policed official duties, and policed violence. This is what in antiquity [?] was called punishment. In sum, above they measured heavenly principle and below they measured human sentiment, balancing the mean between leniency and severity and conforming to the spirit of reverent compassion. The Classics discuss the Way, and when delineated they become law; the statutes discuss the law, and when regulated they become the Way. How could the Classics alone be called subtle and the laws alone be called crude, like tenon and mortise failing to fit one another? From the Three Dynasties downward, laws …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
令滋章爲六篇之律者李悝也爲九章之
律者蕭何也爲十二章之律者玄齡也若
乃因漢律九章而張湯趙禹廣至數千則
楊雄所謂不必學者也因唐律十二章而
長孫無忌輩廣至五百則叔向所謂不必
鑄者也科條不同要皆一代之法也已
明興律令損益千古大都制辟以威則令之爲
條一百四十五其法簡以嚴懸法以敎則
律之爲凡三百其法明以悉
===
欽恤之德媲美虞舜糺虔之度追蹤周官誠羽
翼六經而畢視漢唐之制矣邇者
皇上分遣理官出讞重辟頃復
嘉納臺疏凡士占一經者令兼習法律眞足
霈雨露勑雷霆而闢經生蔀斗之迷矣執
事令諸生度可行否豈非虞枸攣之見難
於驟破而局曲之習非責實以課之終罔
覩成效耶則嘗覽鏡往昔唐有律學宋有
善聽獄訟盡公得實科而胡安定之敎國
punctuated: 令滋章。爲六篇之律者，李悝也；爲九章之律者，蕭何也；爲十二章之律者，玄齡也。若乃因漢律九章而張湯、趙禹廣至數千，則楊雄所謂不必學者也；因唐律十二章而長孫無忌輩廣至五百，則叔向所謂不必鑄者也。科條不同，要皆一代之法也已。明興，律令損益千古，大都制辟以威，則令之爲條一百四十五，其法簡以嚴；懸法以敎，則律之爲凡三百，其法明以悉。欽恤之德，媲美虞舜；糺虔之度，追蹤《周官》。誠羽翼六經，而畢視漢、唐之制矣。邇者，皇上分遣理官，出讞重辟，頃復嘉納臺疏，凡士占一經者，令兼習法律，眞足霈雨露、勑雷霆，而闢經生蔀斗之迷矣。執事令諸生度可行否，豈非虞枸攣之見難於驟破，而局曲之習非責實以課之，終罔覩成效耶？則嘗覽鏡往昔，唐有律學，宋有善聽獄訟盡公得實科，而胡安定之敎國
translation_en:
…and ordinances proliferated. He who compiled the Code in Six Sections was Li Kui 李悝; he who compiled the Code in Nine Chapters was Xiao He 蕭何; he who compiled the Code in Twelve Chapters was [Fang] Xuanling 房玄齡. As for taking the nine chapters of the Han code and having Zhang Tang 張湯 and Zhao Yu 趙禹 expand them to several thousand, that is what Yang Xiong 楊雄 called something that need not be studied; and taking the twelve chapters of the Tang code and having Zhangsun Wuji 長孫無忌 and his colleagues expand them to five hundred articles, that is what Shuxiang 叔向 called something that need not be cast in bronze. Though the articles and statutes differed, in essence each was the law of a single era.

With the rise of the Ming, the Penal Code and Commandment Statutes added to and subtracted from the institutions of a thousand ages. In general, in establishing punishments to inspire awe, the Commandment Statutes comprise one hundred and forty-five articles, their provisions concise yet strict; in displaying the law to instruct, the Penal Code comprises some three hundred articles in all, its provisions clear and comprehensive. The virtue of reverent compassion rivals in beauty that of Yu Shun 虞舜; the measures for correcting and regulating trace the footsteps of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). Truly they serve as wings to the Six Classics and look down upon the institutions of Han and Tang!

Recently, His Majesty dispatched judicial officials to the provinces to review capital cases, and just lately He graciously accepted a memorial from the Censorate ordering that all scholars who specialize in one Classic be made to study the laws and statutes concurrently. This is truly sufficient to shower down rain and dew, command thunder and lightning, and dispel the benighted delusion of classical scholars! When Your Excellency asks the students to consider whether this is feasible or not, is it not because you worry that cramped and narrow views are difficult to break all at once, and that unless parochial habits are tested by demanding practical results, in the end no real success will be seen? Yet if we examine the mirror of the past, the Tang had the School of Law, the Song had the examination category for "skillfully hearing litigation with utter impartiality and obtaining the facts," and when Hu Anding 胡安定 (Hu Yuan 胡瑗) taught the National…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
子亦以經義治事揭齋名彼豈無所見而
然邪玆欲使佔畢之士兼習法律非可嘗
試而漫爲之也其機在上不在士焉今律
令之書不載學官窮鄉下邑罕所覩見謂
宜行所在黌序廣其梓本童儒出就外傅
能受經者即令受律而又擇精曉者爲之
講解布令已定耳目已熟人將視律猶視
經且家傳而戶誦之也士於六經窮年矻
矻白首不已者以起家在經也今鄉飲讀
===
法矣賓興試判矣然皆習爲故事勸陳言
以應誠使必通律理者與明經並進不諳
律文者與失經旨同科彼知非律無以起
家即禁之使不律不能也士操觚爲文剡
心秦漢一行作吏不啻土苴兩造具備百
態微曖高下輕重匪眇故焉謂宜取法呂
刑重懲五過治倍律師心之罪嚴失出失
入之罰士知莅官行法非律不可即欲空
談六籍得乎今世皆軒冕六經糠粃法律
punctuated: 子，亦以「經義」、「治事」揭齋名，彼豈無所見而然邪？玆欲使佔畢之士兼習法律，非可嘗試而漫爲之也，其機在上不在士焉。今律令之書不載學官，窮鄉下邑罕所覩見。謂宜行所在黌序，廣其梓本；童儒出就外傅，能受經者，即令受律，而又擇精曉者爲之講解。布令已定，耳目已熟，人將視律猶視經，且家傳而戶誦之也。士於《六經》窮年矻矻、白首不已者，以起家在經也。今鄉飲讀法矣，賓興試判矣，然皆習爲故事，勸陳言以應。誠使必通律理者與明經並進，不諳律文者與失經旨同科，彼知非律無以起家，即禁之使不律，不能也。士操觚爲文，剡心秦漢；一行作吏，不啻土苴。兩造具備，百態微曖，高下輕重，匪眇故焉。謂宜取法《呂刑》，重懲五過，治倍律師心之罪，嚴失出失入之罰。士知莅官行法非律不可，即欲空談六籍，得乎？今世皆軒冕《六經》、糠粃法律，
translation_en: … [Director of the] Directorate of Imperial Youth, also posted the names "Meaning of the Classics" (Jingyi) and "Administrative Affairs" (Zhishi) on his study halls; how could those men have done so without any insight? Now, if we wish to make scholars who pore over texts simultaneously study the laws and statutes, this cannot be done tentatively or casually; the pivot lies with those above, not with the scholars. At present, the books of statutes and ordinances are not established in the official schools, and in remote villages and lowly districts they are rarely seen. I would suggest that orders be sent to the local schools everywhere to widely distribute printed editions of them. When young students go out to study with an outside tutor, as soon as they are able to receive instruction in the Classics, they should be ordered to receive instruction in the statutes as well, and those who thoroughly understand them should be selected to explain and expound them. Once the promulgated ordinances are settled and people's ears and eyes have grown familiar with them, men will regard the statutes just as they regard the Classics, and moreover every family will transmit them and every household will recite them. The reason scholars toil year after year over the Six Classics, never ceasing even until their hair turns white, is that launching one's official career depends upon the Classics. Today, the laws are read at the District Symposium, and legal judgments (pan) are tested at the Provincial Examination; yet all treat this routinely as an old formality, plagiarizing [?] stale words to get by. If we truly cause those who thoroughly understand the principles of the statutes to advance alongside those who master the Classics, and those who are ignorant of the text of the statutes to be graded the same as those who miss the meaning of the Classics, then once they know that without the statutes they have no means to launch their careers, even if you forbade them to study the statutes, you could not stop them. When scholars take up writing tablets to compose essays, they sharpen their minds on the Qin and Han; once they go out to serve as officials, they discard that like mere mud and straw. When both parties to a lawsuit are present, the myriad circumstances are subtle and obscure, and the discrepancy between a heavier or lighter sentence is no trifling matter. I would suggest taking the Punishments of Lü (Lü xing) as a model, severely punishing the five failings of judicial administration, prosecuting the crime of turning one's back on the statutes to follow one's own personal whims, and strictly enforcing the penalties for erroneously exonerating the guilty or erroneously convicting the innocent. Once scholars know that in assuming office and enforcing the law they cannot do without the statutes, even if they wished to engage in empty talk about the Six Classics, could they do so? Nowadays, the world exalts the Six Classics like carriages and ceremonial caps, while treating the laws and statutes like chaff and husks; …

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
有通曉者閭里隷目之無甚炫異士一登
仕籍授之大邑於律茫然即引用不中輒
怒之曰固經生態無足過督者夫張鵠以
行賞無不射伐鼓以戒士無不奮人情鼓
之則動激之則發懲創之則改漸摩之則
成敎訓之不預賞罰之不嚴如此而欲使
天下改弦易轍反視易聽以從事於律吾
知其不能也或者曰律非聖人意也勢也
上古之時法懸而民不犯刑措而上不用
===
秦不師古以律爲制此惡足法也嗚呼若
是則虞不必象刑周不必呂刑先王讀法
之敎周官象魏之懸皆可不用已今士無
論爲大吏即綰符佩印受寄百里能無法
而可治乎士既屈首簿書日親刑獄訟興
如蝟情隱如蜮能曰吾爲經不爲律乎苟
師心自用比擬弗明大吏能不奉三尺以
繩之乎如其不然而曰吾不爲律是渡江
河亡舟楫載南畝而舍耒耜也不預敎於
punctuated: 有通曉者，閭里隷目之，無甚炫異。士一登仕籍，授之大邑，於律茫然；即引用不中，輒怒之曰：「固經生態，無足過督者。」夫張鵠以行賞，無不射；伐鼓以戒士，無不奮。人情鼓之則動，激之則發，懲創之則改，漸摩之則成。敎訓之不預，賞罰之不嚴如此，而欲使天下改弦易轍，反視易聽，以從事於律，吾知其不能也。或者曰：「律非聖人意也，勢也。上古之時，法懸而民不犯，刑措而上不用。秦不師古，以律爲制，此惡足法也？」嗚呼！若是，則虞不必象刑，周不必《呂刑》，先王讀法之敎、《周官》象魏之懸，皆可不用已！今士無論爲大吏，即綰符佩印、受寄百里，能無法而可治乎？士既屈首簿書，日親刑獄，訟興如蝟，情隱如蜮，能曰「吾爲經，不爲律」乎？苟師心自用，比擬弗明，大吏能不奉三尺以繩之乎？如其不然，而曰「吾不爲律」，是渡江河亡舟楫，載南畝而舍耒耜也。不預敎於
translation_en:
…and if there is anyone thoroughly versed in it, the local communities look upon him as a mere clerk, seeing nothing to admire as extraordinary. Once a scholar enters the official register and is entrusted with a large district, he is completely ignorant of the statutory code; even when his citations of the law miss the mark, people readily excuse [?] him, saying, "That is naturally the manner of a student of the Classics; it is not worth reproving him too strictly." Now, when a target is set up to bestow rewards, there is no one who does not shoot; when drums are beaten to alert the troops, there is no one who does not rouse himself. It is human nature to be moved when drummed on, to burst forth when stimulated, to reform when chastised, and to be perfected when gradually polished. When instruction is not provided in advance and rewards and punishments are not made strict like this, yet one wishes to make the empire restring its instruments and change its tracks, reverse its gaze and alter its hearing in order to apply itself to the statutes—I know this to be impossible.

Someone may say: "Statutes are not the intent of the sages; they are a matter of circumstance. In high antiquity, laws were posted yet the people did not violate them; punishments were set aside and the ruler did not use them. Qin did not model itself on antiquity and made statutes its system—how is this worthy of emulation?" Alas! If that were so, then Yu [Shun] would not have needed symbolic punishments, Zhou would not have needed the Punishments of Lü (Lü xing), and the former kings' instruction in reading out the laws as well as the posting of laws on the palace gate-towers in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) could all have been dispensed with! Today, to say nothing of serving as a high official, even when a scholar holds a tally and wears a seal, entrusted with a jurisdiction of a hundred li, can he govern without laws? Once a scholar bows his head over official registers and deals daily with criminal cases—where lawsuits rise up like hedgehog spines and hidden truths lurk like water-demons—can he say, "I practice the Classics, not the statutes"? If he relies on his own subjective judgment and his analogies in sentencing are unclear, can the high officials refrain from upholding the three-foot bamboo slips of the law to hold him to account? If it cannot be otherwise, and yet he says, "I do not practice the statutes," this is like crossing rivers without boat or oar, or setting to work in the southern fields while throwing away the plow! Not instructing them in advance…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
先徒責成於後是未稼穡而求穫未蠶績
而求其帛也必不得矣大抵聖人議法以
道儒者言律以經碎之醫然律則其方而
審標表之宜者經也碎之奕然律則其譜
而運動靜之機者經也秦取先王六籍付
於煨燼愚黔首以師吏世豈有師吏而可
治哉秦事之失斯悞之也今海內人師孔
孟家誦詩書士生斯時復明習法令折衷
六經斯稱通儒矣何秦事之云或又曰律
===
可使人畏不可使人習人皆習律將倚法
爲姦此其亂如蝟毛起也是又不然弓矢
戈矛以禦暴而姦民竊之爲暴因其竊也
遂廢之並禁民使不得蓄可乎典墳經籍
吾儒竊以行私者何筭然則經亦可不讀
與常人蹈夫故習曲士守其舊聞破拘攣
之習務變通之宜是在通達
國體者斷與不斷耳經生何敢贅焉
第四問
punctuated:
先，徒責成於後，是未稼穡而求穫，未蠶績而求其帛也，必不得矣。大抵聖人議法以道，儒者言律以經。碎之醫然，律則其方，而審標表之宜者經也；碎之奕然，律則其譜，而運動靜之機者經也。秦取先王六籍付於煨燼，愚黔首以師吏。世豈有師吏而可治哉？秦事之失，斯悞之也。今海內人師孔、孟，家誦《詩》、《書》，士生斯時，復明習法令，折衷六經，斯稱通儒矣，何秦事之云！或又曰：「律可使人畏，不可使人習。人皆習律，將倚法爲姦，此其亂如蝟毛起也。」是又不然。弓矢戈矛以禦暴，而姦民竊之爲暴，因其竊也遂廢之，並禁民使不得蓄，可乎？典墳經籍，吾儒竊以行私者何筭，然則經亦可不讀與？常人蹈夫故習，曲士守其舊聞。破拘攣之習，務變通之宜，是在通達國體者斷與不斷耳。經生何敢贅焉！

第四問
translation_en:
… beforehand, and merely demand results afterward; this is like seeking a harvest without having sown and reaped, or seeking silk without having raised silkworms and spun thread—it can never be achieved. In general, the sages deliberate on laws by means of the Way, and Confucian scholars discuss the statutes by means of the Classics. To take medicine as an analogy [碎 for 譬?]: the statutes are its prescriptions, while that which examines the appropriateness of symptoms and root causes is the Classics. To take the game of go (yi) as an analogy [?]: the statutes are its manuals, while that which directs the pivotal mechanisms of movement and stillness is the Classics. Qin took the Six Classics of the former kings and consigned them to ashes, keeping the black-headed commoners ignorant and making them take legal clerks as their teachers. How could the world ever be governed by taking clerks as teachers? The failure of Qin's affairs was misled by this very error. Today, everyone within the seas takes Confucius and Mencius as their teachers, and every household recites the Odes (Shi) and the Documents (Shu). When scholars born in this era also clearly master the laws and ordinances, weighing them against the Six Classics, they may truly be called comprehensive Confucian scholars—what talk could there be of the affairs of Qin!

Someone else may say: "The statutes may be used to make people fearful, but must not be allowed to be studied by people. If everyone studies the statutes, they will rely on the law to commit villainy, and disorder will rise up like the bristles of a hedgehog." This too is not so. Bows, arrows, halberds, and spears are used to ward off violence, yet villainous people steal them to commit violence. Because they steal them, would it be permissible to abolish them altogether and forbid the people to possess them? As for the ancient canons and classical texts, how could one count the number of our own Confucian scholars who have purloined them to pursue their private interests? Should the Classics, then, also not be read? Ordinary men tread in old habits, and parochial scholars cling to what they have long heard. Breaking away from cramped and fettered habits and striving for the appropriateness of flexible adaptation—this rests solely on whether those who thoroughly understand the fundamental principles of the state (guoti) have the resolve to decide or not. How would a student of the Classics dare to speak superfluously on the matter!

Question Four

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
周一梧
同考試官教諭李　批〔度田成賦此足〕
國裕民之遠圖也子揚確古今洞悉利弊而酌議允當尤鑿鑿可行是通達世務者可以式
矣
考試官教諭官　批〔度田今時急務此策晰利害而〕
酌興革若照燭指掌舉而措之誠百世利也錄之
考試官學正蘇　批〔精確詳盡具見遠猷〕
甚矣更化之難也晰利害之原者乃可與
慮始酌興革之要者乃可與圖終夫天下
===
之事利與害常相倚伏而一興一革匪可
嘗試漫爲之者也方未事之先羣議紛撓
非晰其原而斷之則徒滋築室之疑逮既
事之後法令叢共非酌其要而行之則徒
起烹鮮之擾是當事者所宜熟計而詳圖
也今郡國吏奉宣
詔書爲黔黎計長遠者莫急於度田蓋其法始
行於一方而民稱便焉已乃下諸郡縣著
爲令矣特人情方泥故常駭創見則從旁
punctuated:
周一梧

同考試官教諭李　批：〔度田成賦，此足國裕民之遠圖也。子揚確古今，洞悉利弊，而酌議允當，尤鑿鑿可行，是通達世務者，可以式矣。〕
考試官教諭官　批：〔度田，今時急務。此策晰利害而酌興革，若照燭指掌，舉而措之，誠百世利也。錄之。〕
考試官學正蘇　批：〔精確詳盡，具見遠猷。〕

甚矣，更化之難也！晰利害之原者，乃可與慮始；酌興革之要者，乃可與圖終。夫天下之事，利與害常相倚伏，而一興一革，匪可嘗試漫爲之者也。方未事之先，羣議紛撓，非晰其原而斷之，則徒滋築室之疑；逮既事之後，法令叢共，非酌其要而行之，則徒起烹鮮之擾。是當事者所宜熟計而詳圖也。今郡國吏奉宣詔書，爲黔黎計長遠者，莫急於度田。蓋其法始行於一方，而民稱便焉，已乃下諸郡縣，著爲令矣。特人情方泥故常，駭創見，則從旁
translation_en:
Zhou Yiwu 周一梧

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Li, comments: [Surveying land to establish the tax quota is a far-sighted plan for enriching the state and providing for the people. You thoroughly examine antiquity and the present, penetrate its advantages and abuses, and deliberate appropriately; above all, your proposals are concrete and practicable. This is the work of one well-versed in affairs of the world, and it may serve as a model.]
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Guan, comments: [Surveying land is an urgent task of the present day. This policy essay analyzes advantages and disadvantages and weighs what to initiate and what to abolish as clearly as shining a candle or pointing to one's palm. To take it up and put it into practice would truly bring benefit for a hundred generations. Recorded.]
Examiner, Director of Studies (xuezheng) Su, comments: [Precise, accurate, and exhaustive; it fully reveals far-reaching counsel.]

Great indeed is the difficulty of reforming administration! Only with one who clearly understands the origins of benefit and harm can one deliberate at the beginning of an undertaking; only with one who weighs the essentials of what to initiate and what to abolish can one plan for its completion. In the affairs of the world, benefit and harm constantly depend upon and conceal one another, and any single initiation or abolition is not something to be undertaken casually or experimentally. Before an undertaking is begun, competing opinions are confused and obstructive; unless one clearly discerns the root of the matter and makes a decisive judgment, one will merely increase the doubts of "building a house by the roadside." Once the undertaking is underway, laws and ordinances accumulate in profusion [?]; unless one weighs what is essential in carrying them out, one will merely stir up the disturbance of "over-handling a small fish while cooking it." This is what those in charge of affairs ought to calculate maturely and plan in detail. Now the officials of the prefectures and counties, respectfully proclaiming the imperial edict and planning for the long-term welfare of the common people, have nothing more urgent before them than surveying the land. For this method was first carried out in one region and the people praised its convenience; thereafter it was handed down to the various prefectures and counties and established as an ordinance. Yet human sentiment is ever bogged down in old habits and startled by unprecedented measures, so onlookers from the side…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
阻之曰版籍之定久矣第令均其兩稅將
兆催科公私不至甚病何至日浆諸四民
而馳驟之爲且事成必吏爲籍籍必有所
需卽計田輸直乎民將嗸嗸不者而取具
有司則牘鍰又已盡移之
內帑費妄從出宋熙寧中行其法十年而告
成者薹薹六路尋以勞擾報罷玆往事可
鏡也嗟乎事無全利亦無全害權其輕重
以爲弛張此可與拘攣者道哉田畝賦役
===
上繫公家緩急而下關黔赤利病自度田
法行則新斥之壤可以抵荒坍故額而國
無虧課利一姦豪鉅室不得賄連胥吏飛
詭爲姦利二產去稅存絕籍貽累者自玆
得稍蘇息利三且一勞永逸暫費永寧是
百世利也
廟堂之上力持其議四方羣吏循軌而趨蓋
報竣事如期者衆矣執事乃發策詢諸生
圖所爲善後之畫非筆研之士所敢知也
punctuated: 阻之曰：「版籍之定久矣，第令均其兩稅，將兆催科，公私不至甚病，何至日浆諸四民而馳驟之爲？且事成必吏爲籍，籍必有所需。卽計田輸直乎，民將嗸嗸；不者，而取具有司，則牘鍰又已盡移之內帑，費妄從出？宋熙寧中行其法，十年而告成者，薹薹六路，尋以勞擾報罷，玆往事可鏡也。」嗟乎！事無全利，亦無全害，權其輕重以爲弛張，此可與拘攣者道哉？田畝賦役，上繫公家緩急，而下關黔赤利病。自度田法行，則新斥之壤可以抵荒坍故額，而國無虧課，利一；姦豪鉅室不得賄連胥吏、飛詭爲姦，利二；產去稅存、絕籍貽累者，自玆得稍蘇息，利三。且一勞永逸，暫費永寧，是百世利也。廟堂之上力持其議，四方羣吏循軌而趨，蓋報竣事如期者衆矣。執事乃發策詢諸生，圖所爲善後之畫，非筆研之士所敢知也。
translation_en:
…obstruct it from the sidelines, saying: "The land and household registers have long been fixed. If we simply equalize the two annual taxes and manage [?] the tax collection, neither public nor private interests will suffer greatly. Why go so far as to daily gather [?] the four classes of people and drive them about at a gallop? Moreover, once the task is completed, clerks must compile the registers, and compiling registers necessarily requires funding. If the cost is assessed according to the acreage of land, the people will clamor in distress; if not, and it is instead drawn from the local authorities, the judicial redemption fees have already been entirely transferred to the Inner Treasury—so where [reading 安 for 妄] will the expenses come from? During the Xining reign of the Song (1068–1077), when this measure was carried out, after ten years only [reading 僅僅 for 薹薹] six circuits had reported completion, and soon thereafter it was halted due to the exhaustion and disturbance it caused. This past event can serve as a mirror."

Alas! No undertaking is wholly beneficial, nor is any wholly harmful; weighing their relative gravity in order to relax or tighten policy—how can this be discussed with those bound by narrow conventions? Land acreage, land taxes, and labor services are tied above to the urgent needs of the state, and relate below to the welfare and suffering of the common people. Since the implementation of the land measurement law, first, newly opened lands can offset the old quotas of wasteland and collapsed riverbanks, so the state suffers no deficit in revenue—this is the first benefit. Second, cunning magnates and great households can no longer bribe and collude with petty clerks to practice the fraud of false transfers and fictitious registrations—this is the second benefit. Third, those whose property is gone while the tax remains, or who suffer the lingering burden of extinct households, can from now on gain some relief and respite—this is the third benefit. Furthermore, one effort brings lasting ease, and temporary expense brings perpetual peace; this is a benefit for a hundred generations.

Above in the imperial court, this policy has been vigorously upheld, and local officials in all quarters have followed the tracks and hastened forward, so that great numbers have reported the completion of the work on schedule. Now you, sir, have issued this policy question to inquire of us students, planning measures for post-completion administration—this is not something that scholars of brush and inkstone would dare presume to know.

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
雖然問及之矣敢不攄所聞乎蓋自堯�THE
洪水禹作司空辨九等之田定墾田九百
二十萬頃維時水土方平荒服草昧所統
者九州耳秦漢而下幅員日增而頃畝不
能加闢也惟隋之開皇唐之天寶乃倍於
前宋人北無幽薊西無寧夏而諸路墾田
以頃計者不下四百六十餘萬我
國家興圖之盛遠視漢唐近陋宋代天下之
田籍於官者菫與宋治平中額數相埒抑
===
何尠也隆古之世淳風未泯耒作未興其
民辛勤稼穡重轉徙即漢唐時猶有引水
開渠歲增二萬頃者有築堰溉田獲利十
餘倍者今燕薊諸邊夷爲沙漠徐邳淮鳳
沮洳瀰漫卽堯禹所營九州其爲可耕之
地者凡幾而六軍萬姓咸仰給於東南持
籌者憂之則數數建議欲闢汙萊廣儲蓄
而有司未有以應也然則土田之縮額也
豈特隱匿之爲弊歟哉地有遺利民有遺
punctuated: 雖然，問及之矣，敢不攄所聞乎？蓋自堯THE洪水，禹作司空，辨九等之田，定墾田九百二十萬頃。維時水土方平，荒服草昧，所統者九州耳。秦漢而下，幅員日增，而頃畝不能加闢也；惟隋之開皇、唐之天寶，乃倍於前。宋人北無幽薊，西無寧夏，而諸路墾田以頃計者，不下四百六十餘萬。我國家興圖之盛，遠視漢唐，近陋宋代，天下之田籍於官者，菫與宋治平中額數相埒，抑何尠也！隆古之世，淳風未泯，耒作未興，其民辛勤稼穡，重轉徙。即漢唐時，猶有引水開渠、歲增二萬頃者，有築堰溉田、獲利十餘倍者。今燕薊諸邊夷爲沙漠，徐、邳、淮、鳳沮洳瀰漫，卽堯禹所營九州，其爲可耕之地者凡幾？而六軍萬姓咸仰給於東南。持籌者憂之，則數數建議，欲闢汙萊，廣儲蓄，而有司未有以應也。然則土田之縮額也，豈特隱匿之爲弊歟哉？地有遺利，民有遺
translation_en: Even so, since you have asked about it, how dare I not set forth what I have heard? Ever since Yao experienced [?] the great flood, Yu served as Minister of Works (Sikong), distinguished the nine grades of fields, and established the cultivated land at 9,200,000 qing. At that time, the waters and lands had just been pacified and the wilderness zone remained in primeval obscurity, so what was governed comprised only the Nine Provinces. From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, the territory expanded day by day, yet the acreage could not be further opened up; only during the Kaihuang era of the Sui and the Tianbao era of the Tang did it double what had gone before. Under the Song, they lacked Youzhou and Jizhou in the north and Ningxia in the west, yet the cultivated land across the various circuits, counted in qing, was no less than 4,600,000 and more. Our State, in the magnificence of its territory, matches the Han and Tang of distant times and looks down upon the recent Song dynasty; yet the lands of the empire registered with the authorities barely equal the quota of the Zhiping era of the Song—how meager this is! In high antiquity, simple customs had not yet vanished and corrupt practices [?] had not yet arisen; the people toiled diligently at sowing and reaping and were reluctant to migrate. Even in Han and Tang times, there were still those who diverted water and dug canals to add 20,000 qing of land a year, and those who built weirs to irrigate fields and reaped more than tenfold profit. Today, the frontier regions of Yan and Ji have been leveled into sandy deserts, while Xuzhou, Pizhou, Huaian, and Fengyang are vast expanses of marsh and swamp. Even within the Nine Provinces laid out by Yao and Yu, how much arable land actually remains? Meanwhile, the Six Armies and the myriad people all depend on supplies from the southeast. Those who hold the tallies of state finance worry over this and have repeatedly submitted proposals wishing to open up overgrown wastelands and expand reserves, yet the authorities have had no way to respond. This being so, is the shrinking quota of land due merely to the abuse of concealment? The fact that the land has untapped benefits and the people have untapped…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
力實使之然也顧亦有類於東而復於西
荒於昔而墾於後額課不均積弊相沿者
其勢不得不爲度田之議而度田之制所
由來久矣周司馬法六尺爲步步百爲畝
畝百爲夫時助法方行公私區別民各晝
地而耕法令不煩逮井田旣壞兼併莫稽
漢建武中詔州郡檢覆墾田有司多爲巧
詐至度民廬屋里落優饒豪右侵剋羸弱
自陳留吏牘徽於殿陛始有以度田不實
===
蒙譴者矣顯宗令牧守區種增耕而吏務
增額至於不種之地亦勤爲稅居巢侯劉
般入言於上乃申勑刺史二千石務令實
覈其有增加使與奪田同罪建初間秦彭
爲山陽守每於農月親度頃畝分別肥瘠
定爲三品各立文簿藏之鄉縣詔以其所
立條式班諸三府並下郡國而其法益加
詳焉夫度田不實區種增耕秖擾里廬而
無裨實用惟建初之法其近之乎今之有
punctuated: 力，實使之然也。顧亦有類於東而復於西，荒於昔而墾於後，額課不均，積弊相沿者，其勢不得不爲度田之議，而度田之制所由來久矣。周《司馬法》：六尺爲步，步百爲畝，畝百爲夫。時助法方行，公私區別，民各晝地而耕，法令不煩。逮井田旣壞，兼併莫稽。漢建武中，詔州郡檢覆墾田，有司多爲巧詐，至度民廬屋里落，優饒豪右，侵剋羸弱。自陳留吏牘徽於殿陛，始有以度田不實蒙譴者矣。顯宗令牧守區種增耕，而吏務增額，至於不種之地，亦勤爲稅。居巢侯劉般入言於上，乃申勑刺史、二千石務令實覈，其有增加，使與奪田同罪。建初間，秦彭爲山陽守，每於農月，親度頃畝，分別肥瘠，定爲三品，各立文簿，藏之鄉縣。詔以其所立條式，班諸三府，並下郡國，而其法益加詳焉。夫度田不實，區種增耕，秖擾里廬而無裨實用，惟建初之法其近之乎！今之有
translation_en: …labor that truly make it so. However, there are also cases where land is flawed [?] in the east and recovered in the west, or was wasteland in the past and reclaimed later, so that the assessed quotas are uneven and accumulated abuses have been perpetuated. Under such circumstances, one cannot help but propose the surveying of land, and the institution of surveying land has a long history indeed. According to the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) of the Zhou, six chi make a pace (bu), a hundred paces make a mu, and a hundred mu make a household allotment (fu). At that time, the mutual-aid tax system (zhu) was in effect, public and private fields were distinct, the people each marked out [晝 for 畫] their land to plow, and laws and ordinances were not burdensome. When the well-field system collapsed, land engrossment could no longer be checked. During the Jianwu era (25–56) of the Han, an imperial decree ordered the regions and commanderies to inspect and verify reclaimed land. The authorities mostly engaged in clever fraud, going so far as to include the people's houses, cottages, and village lanes in the measurements, showing favor to the powerful elites while encroaching upon and exploiting the weak and poor. Only after the wooden tablet of the subofficial functionary from Chenliu came to light [徽 for 徵?] at the steps of the throne were there finally those who suffered reprimand and punishment for untruthful land measurement. Emperor Xianzong (Emperor Ming, r. 57–75) ordered the Regional Pastors and Grand Administrators to promote pit-cultivation and increase plowing, yet the officials strove merely to inflate the quotas, to the point that even uncultivated land was arbitrarily [勤 for 勒?] assessed for tax. When the Marquis of Juchao, Liu Ban 劉般, entered court and spoke to the Emperor, an imperial instruction was issued to the Regional Inspectors and Two-Thousand-Bushel Officials (Grand Administrators) ordering them to verify the facts strictly, and stipulating that anyone who falsely added to the figures would be charged with the same crime as seizing land. During the Jianchu era (76–84), Qin Peng 秦彭 served as Grand Administrator of Shanyang. Every farming season, he personally measured the qing and mu, distinguished fertile from barren land, and classified them into three grades, establishing registers for each to be stored in the districts and counties. By imperial decree, the regulations and formulas he established were promulgated to the Three Ducal Offices and handed down to the commanderies and kingdoms, and thus the method became increasingly detailed. Now, untruthful land measurement and forced increases in pit-cultivation and plowing merely disturb the villages and cottages without benefiting practical use; only the method of the Jianchu era comes close to what is right! The present authorities…

title: 萬曆十年山西鄉試錄
text:
司兢兢奉
詔覈畝郊居辨界植埒要以如額而止宜
朝廷德意甚盛也慮生猶有狂瞽之見願爲
執事陳焉曰量程限也差等則也酌民情
也寬開田也議遷擢也夫法之始行也孰
敢不竭蹶從事顧地形相錯自巧歷者不
能窮駁脊末從徒煩聽睹比得其指歸矣
而或以它事去則請諸藩臬諸司又請諸
撫巡大吏而稱其事者始踐更也迺藩臬
===
撫巡之遷代又靡一也文移積而期會稽
勢所必至將欒致之期乎必且匆遽因循
以圖塞責語云雖有良馬疾行則蹶故曰
量程限民家之以田相貿易也計畝合劵
惟得一老農而質曰歲輸幾何則忻然任
之矣此無它惟其習故也今使里吏胥徒
握其尋丈而高下腴瘠懵然莫問殊不知
赤淤黑壚異色陂原平澤異宜或隘而反
腴或美而反瘠辨之不審所害滋多昔周
punctuated: 司兢兢奉詔，覈畝郊居，辨界植埒，要以如額而止，宜朝廷德意甚盛也。慮生猶有狂瞽之見，願爲執事陳焉：曰量程限也，差等則也，酌民情也，寬開田也，議遷擢也。夫法之始行也，孰敢不竭蹶從事？顧地形相錯，自巧歷者不能窮；駁脊末從，徒煩聽睹。比得其指歸矣，而或以它事去，則請諸藩臬諸司，又請諸撫巡大吏，而稱其事者始踐更也。迺藩臬、撫巡之遷代又靡一也。文移積而期會稽，勢所必至。將欒致之期乎？必且匆遽因循，以圖塞責。語云：「雖有良馬，疾行則蹶。」故曰量程限。民家之以田相貿易也，計畝合劵，惟得一老農而質曰：「歲輸幾何？」則忻然任之矣。此無它，惟其習故也。今使里吏胥徒握其尋丈，而高下腴瘠懵然莫問，殊不知赤淤黑壚異色，陂原平澤異宜，或隘而反腴，或美而反瘠，辨之不審，所害滋多。昔《周
translation_en:
…authorities conscientiously obey the imperial edict, verifying acreage in the rural settlements, distinguishing boundaries and erecting embankments, aiming only to meet the quota and stop there—thereby fittingly manifesting the court's most generous benevolence. Yet your thoughtful student still holds some rash and blind views that he wishes to present to Your Excellency: namely, calibrating the time limits, grading the tax rates, taking popular sentiment into account, showing leniency toward newly reclaimed land, and deliberating on promotions and transfers.

When a law is first put into effect, who would dare not exert themselves to the utmost in carrying it out? However, the terrain interlocks in complex ways that even a master calculator cannot exhaust; when disputes over land ridges [?] and minor details cannot be settled, they merely burden one's hearing and sight. By the time an official grasps the essentials of the task, he may have to leave on account of other business. One must then petition the various offices of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, and further petition the senior Grand Coordinators and Regional Inspectors, before someone suited to the task can take over in rotation. Moreover, the transfers and replacements of the Provincial Commissioners, Surveillance Commissioners, Grand Coordinators, and Regional Inspectors are themselves far from uniform. That official communications pile up and deadlines are delayed is the inevitable outcome. If one were to bind them strictly to a fixed deadline [?], they would surely act with hasty perfunctoriness just to shirk their responsibility. As the saying goes, "Even a fine horse will stumble if driven at a gallop." Therefore I say: calibrate the time limits.

When commoner households trade land with one another, in counting the mu and matching the deeds, they need only find an experienced farmer and ask squarely, "How much does it yield in annual tax?"—and then they gladly take it on. This is for no other reason than that he is thoroughly familiar with it.
